          A pictorial view of the solution architecture is above. While limited in scope, the
          diagram shows that users and EMS machines are defined in Active Directory,
          and these users and machines authenticate to AD within the domain context. A
          user named Ray Santini logs in to WebFG Client and authenticates to AD and
          the WebFG Server. WebFG server passes the authenticated identity to PERMIT
          and PERMIT subsequently looks up access permissions for Ray. Ray may have
          a slightly different name in PERMIT. e.g. Ray’s middle name is added in the
          PERMIT database. PERMIT does the name mapping to find the correct name,
          account, and permissions.

Scope of this Course
This course covers the basic data structures and associated data attributes that condition the manner in which the
e-terrascada subsystem gathers and processes real-time measurements from various data sources. This data is
provided to ALSTOM GRID software via a data model that is maintained via the e-terrasource product. Therefore, this
course looks at SCADA data from the e-terrasource perspective, making extensive use of the e-terrasource user
interface. The Alarm server model is also examined through the e-terrabrowser user interface. Tips for customizing
e-terrascada are also presented.


Content and Organization
Building a SCADA Model explains how to create and modify parameters affecting real-time processing of data objects
in the SCADAMOM database. Following the overview, the following topics are covered:

        •   SCADA as an Alarm Client

        •   Status Points (Discretes)

        •   Analogs

        •   Accumulators

        •   Controls

        •   Special Controls

        •   Calculated Measurements

        •   Topology Processing

        •   Historical Data Recording

        •   Communication and RTU Modeling

        •   InterSite Operations Modeling

        •   SCADA Online Editing

        •   Deploying the Model

        •   Efficiently Developing the Model
The lab sessions are based upon an existing, fictional, power system’s SCADA model, which is mapped to a
corresponding Generation and Network model. This course concentrates on only the SCADA model attributes. The
Generation and Network data attributes are left for later courses


                                        e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model                                        iv


<!-- salto de página -->

Course Objectives
After completing this course, students will be able to:

        •    Define the three components of the SCADA application

        •    Describe the data structures present in the SCADAMOM database

        •    Explain from the figure how e-terrascada interacts with ALARM service

        •    Navigate to and edit (insert, delete, modify) SCADA DISCRETES

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA ANALOGS

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA ACCUMULATORS

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA CONTROLS

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA SPECIAL CONTROLS

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA CALCULATION TEMPLATES

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA DEVICE TOPOLOGY

        •    Describe how e-terrascada processes device energization and connectivity

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA Historical Data recording parameters (HDR)

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA COMMUNICATION TOPOLOGY

        •    Navigate to and edit SCADA RTU TOPOLOGY

        •    Explain how data is sent and received with other sites (ISD)

        •    Navigate and use the displays used for Online SCADA Editing

        •    Describe how a new SCADA model is deployed

        •    Describe the early design factors for efficient SCADA modeling


Intended Audience
This course is intended for a large audience, mainly for developers and engineers who will perform database
and system modeling, display building, and programming. The student is expected to know how to operate an
e-terrahabitat modeling workstation, have access to a device or devices that can serve as e-terrahabitat
console/station and e-terrasource clients, and have access to online e-terrascada documentation.


Prerequisites
Students are expected to have completed the following courses prior to taking this course:

        •    Introduction to e-terrahabitat

        •    e-terrahabitat Databases

                     EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


•   e-terrasource is the central environment and repository where the EMS
    model is maintained.
•   e-terrasource is CIM (Common Information Model) compliant.
•   CIM is an Open IEC standard representing power system components
    that facilitate the data exchange among companies, allowing
    applications to exchange data about the configuration and status of an
    electrical network within a company.
•   e-terrasource includes extensions to cover features that are not
    currently covered by the CIM standard such as the e-terrascada model.
•   The e-terrasource model can be exported to be used by different target
    applications.
•   The e-terrasource transformation subsystem is the place where
    e-terrasource maintains and executes the rules to convert the
    e-terrasource data to e-terraplatform models, including the SCADA
    model.

1.    e-terrasource is the tool to model the EMS business model including SCADA.
2.    The e-terrasource business model is based on the CIM (IEC61970) standard,
      but has been extended to cover all the e-terraplatform features.
3.    The e-terrasource transformation subsystem transforms the e-terrasource
      modeled data into e-terraplatform data including SCADA data.

                    Lab 0: Logging In to the Clients
In this lab, you will start the e-terrasource and e-terrabrowser clients.

Task 1: Start the e-terrasource Client
The client operates as a plug-in to the Alstom (or Advanced) Presentation Framework (APF).

 1. If this lab is using Training laptops, your instructor will inform you how to log in to the
    training system.

 2. Log in to the Training Boot Camp VM as dbc01 / pw
    Alstomtra1n.

 3. Start the Advanced Presentation Framework by
    selecting the APF Icon on the desktop.


                                                               4. The Credential Input window
                                                                  opens. With this
                                                                  configuration, you will initially
                                                                  be presented with the option
                                                                  to “Enter Name and
                                                                  Password,” but instead, select
                                                                  the Other button to get a list
                                                                  of available Login Credential
                                                                  Types.

                                                               5. Select Current Windows
                                                                  User.

8. In the labs for this course, you will be making a series of changes to the e-terrasource
   database. Each of these changes will be captured in projects. For reference, the
   steps to create a project are:
   •   From the toolbar, select        New > Project

       change to the database is Lab 2, so you would call this project Scada_Lab#2.)

   •   Click OK to save the project.

   •   Note that the new project is now your current project, as reflected by the Project
       Selector on the toolbar.

NOTE: FEP DB is not an HDB database
e-terrascada includes SCADA, Tagging, Historian recording, SCADA Topology and
Front End management. ISD (SCADA InterSite Protocol) consists of the
mechanism created for the transfer of data, control, or TAG between application
programs at a site and between sites, as well as to and from external clients. It is
based on the following components:

• InterSite Data dedicated to the transfer of SCADA
• InterSite Control dedicated to the transfer of SCADA supervisory controls (single
or group control or setpoint)
• InterSite Tagging/Notes dedicated to the transfer of tagging and notes
information

ISD (SCADA InterSite Protocol), Load Shedding, and Mapboard management are
optional applications that require additional licenses.

Evolution to e-terrasource:

e-terrasource takes the approach that a model is a business system for
model construction and maintenance. It interacts with other business
systems requiring business system models. Transmission network models,
for example, can be managed by e-terrasource and supplied to EMS,
market and planning systems from e-terrasource.

e-terrasource is a system description. The transmission system model
defines the need for a certain kind of equipment in a particular substation
in a particular relationship to other elements of the transmission system. A
position in the system can be planned, with no actual asset corresponding -
or a position can be in a neighbor’s territory.
• e-terrasource stores all of the system descriptive data in a relational
  database (RDBMS).
• From there, it is deployed to the HDB clones using the Transformation
  Subsystem.

Note: SCADA is one of many clients of ALARM.
1.   Registered Client decides what is worthy to report.
         •   Client creates an EVENT block (category, exception, location, area, text, options).
         •   Client makes an API call to alarm – PostEvent.
2.   Alarm- wakes up and processes the Event from some client.
         •   Updates the ALARMLST database in the ALARM clone.
         •   Uses PERMIT to validate the client “AREA” in the event.
         •   Uses the ALARM modeling database to validate the CAT, LOC, EXC, options.
3.   ALARM - Makes an API call to LOGMAN (if used).
4.   ALARM - Issues an audible tone (via Webfg) to any workstations modeled as HORNS
5.   ALARM - Records the event in its ALARMARC recording file (for history).
6.   System Operators - from an ALARM or CLIENT screen, acknowledge (indicate that they have
     seen) the Alarm.
7.   ALARM - Updates its own database, records the ACK from the SC action - Webfg or rule.
8.   ALARM - if so configured, wakes up the client - “your event has been ACKed”.
9.   System Operators -to remove the alarm from their displays: DELETE / PURGE alarm.
10. ALARM - Deletes the alarm from its database (ALARMLST), records the operator action.
         •   No notification of DELETE to client - (by design) only effect is within ALARM.
         •   If the client wants some DELETE behavior, client software has to perform that.

PROXYSRV Databases
The PROXYSRV application uses its own databases, called “PROXYSRV” and “PROXYLOG”.
• PROXYSRV - Contains connection parameters for handling and managing connection
  requests. It also contains parameters for processing Alarm data.
• PROXYLOG - PROXYSRV log database.

PROXYSRV Savecases
The only savecase associated with the PROXYSRV application is called “PROXYSRV”, and it
is present in the PROXYSRV codeset.

PROXYSRV Tasks
The PROXYSRV application performs the following primary functions:
• It processes connection requests from its clients using TCP/IP, and it manages and
  administers the established connections.
• It allows clients (applications) to exchange data using the InterSite Data (ISD) protocol.
• If enabled, it receives alarm messages from alarm server, formats the alarm data, and
  then posts the alarm message.

Exception
A database object that has changed to an abnormal or alarmable state. It
remains an exception as long as it is either in an abnormal state or has not
been acknowledged.

Exception Definition
The set of attributes attached to an exception. The reference to the message
displayed in the lists and logs is modeled in the exception definition.

Notes:
• There is just one AreaOfResponsiblity table in e-terrasource, and it is
  found in the Network Reference Tables folder (even if this is a SCADA-
  only system).
• As each object may have up to five AORs, the AreaOfResponsibility
  records in e-terrasource have properties that map to five different
  PERMIT Areas.
• Areas in Permit are associated with Modes that are assigned to the
  User, and therefore, each User may have a unique set of AORs.
• The Permit database is modeled online. See the Permit User’s Guide
  (permit_ug.pdf).

Note:
SCADA global flags PRMCLEXC and PRMDAEXC control how Areas affect
SCADA data acquisition and supervisory control.
• A PRMCLEXC “TRUE" setting indicates that Execute permission is
  required for Supervisory Control activities. This flag is defined on the
  Miscellaneous tab of the SCADA Parameters/Model Parameters e-
  terramodeler form.
• A PRMDAEXC “TRUE" setting indicates that Execute permission is
  required for Data Acquisition activities such as removing substation
  records from service, inhibiting alarms, manual replacement, etc. This
  flag is defined on the Control Defaults tab of the SCADA
  Parameters/Model Parameters e-terramodeler form.
If these flags are not set, then the user needs only WRITE permission for
the SCADA application and the appropriate Area(s) in order to execute
the respective commands.

• When “Inhibit” is set by the operator, the restriction on exception
  reporting is based on the inhibit definition:
      • Logging & Alarm List - No alarm issued.
      • Unacknowledged Alarm List - Issued as pre-acknowledged.
      • Abnormal for Alarm - Abnormal flag is not propagated to
          Alarm.
      • Abnormal for SCADA - Abnormal flag is not set in SCADA
          database.
      • Audible Tone - No audible tone is sounded.
• “Initially Inhibit” being set causes the point to begin as inhibited the
  first time the measurement is put in service or “Commissioned.”
  Thereafter, the status as set by the operator persists via Selective
  Copy when a new database is put online.

• Auto-Acknowledge (on Return-to-Normal): If an object is using the
  same EXCDEF for abnormal & normal transitions (and therefore Alarm
  processing cannot distinguish between normal and abnormal) and it
  returns to normal via a control operation, the alarm can be issued
  auto-acked by SCADA.
• Auto Ack and Delete Alarms: Alarm is issued both auto-acked and
  auto-deleted on successful return to normal condition due to:
     • Control operation
     • Manual entry
 Note that this “alarm” will only be visible on the System Activity
 displays.

Task 2: Setting Inhibit Definitions
      The SCADA database models what operator inhibit activity will accomplish.
      Remember there are two sets of five flags that control this: one set to
      permanently inhibit alarm processing, and one set that allows the operator a
      binary control of SCADA alarm processing (inhibit/un-inhibit).
      Setting the global Configuration values of these five flags defines the default
      behavior of how e-terrascada posts events to Alarm. These flags can be
      overridden on an object-by-object basis, which we will learn how to do in later
      units. The five global flags are:
         •   Default Inhibit Logging: When selected, an inhibit action by the
             operator will prevent any events from being reported to Alarm by the
             e-terrascada client. This will cause loss of history while the data object
             in question remains inhibited. This implicitly prevents tones from being
             issued as well.
         •   Default Inhibit Unacknowledged Condition: When selected, the
             e-terrascada client issues alarms on the inhibited object as pre-
             acknowledged.
         •   Default Inhibit Alarm Abnormal: When selected, the e-terrascada
             client issues alarms on the inhibited object without any indication that
             the object is in an abnormal condition. (The Alarm Server will not
             recognize an object moving to an abnormal condition.)
         •   Default Inhibit SCADA Abnormal: This is a client-only behavior
             modification. When selected, if the e-terrascada client issues an alarm
             on an inhibited object, the object does not get classified as abnormal,
             thereby keeping the object off the exception list.
         •   Default Inhibit Tone: When selected, the e-terrascada client
             suppresses the issuance of audible tones when issuing alarms on an
             inhibited object.
      YOUR TASK: Assume that your manager has told you that in general, he wants
      the operator’s inhibit action to NOT prevent abnormal objects from appearing
      on the SCADA exception list.

Task 3: The SCADA Exception Lists
The e-terrascada client keeps its own view of its alarm situation (completely distinct from
the Alarm Server view) in what is called its exception list. The displays associated with this
SCADA exception data (other Alarm clients do not participate) are intended to give the
operator a summary view of current conditions relative to SCADA data objects.
The data that appears on the exception displays is filtered and shows data objects that
currently are in an abnormal condition, and/or have alarms that are unacknowledged.

Your Action                                      System Response

1. If needed, use the icons in the HABITAT       Start HABITAT Applications will run the
   shortcut directory to                         Habitat PROCMAN.
   • “Start HABITAT Applications”
   • Start the “WebFG Viewer” and log in
       as DTS.
2. From the SCADA substation tabular                     Hint: Substation tabular is called up
   display, click Related                                from the SCADA Applications menu.
   Displays>Exception                            Displays all exceptions, ordered from newest
   Summaries>Point/Analog Exceptions:            to oldest.


Note: This list enables the operator to acknowledge alarms, which may remove the item
from the exception list, take the data object in/out of service, and inhibit/un-inhibit the data
object for alarming. Also, the tabs allow the operator to navigate through different sortings
and filterings of the exceptions.

   The Alarm server and the real-time e-terrascada client exchange data such

   for resolution. In this unit, you were exposed to the interaction between alarm
   client and alarm server, with particular emphasis on the e-terrascada client
   and the data needed to support the posting of events by e-terrascada.

1.    Status points return one, two, or three bits, allowing the following types of
      reports:
       A.     2 State (on/off, open/closed, etc.)
       B.     3 State (open/in-between/closed)
       C.     4 State (open/more than half-open, less than half-open/closed)
       D.     Momentary Change (two or more changes since last scan)

2.    Status points have   type and       name that determine the way e-
      terrascada processes them for reporting.
3.    Points have an extra bit called “M” that signals multiple state changes
      between scans.

            Lab 3: SCADA Status Point Modeling
Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
        •    Alter a Status Point Record
        •    Enable MCD (Momentary Change Detection) processing for a status
             point model
        •    Modify an Inhibit Definition for a particular status point in your model
        •    Create a conditional alarm based on a status point value
        •    Save and validate your work
     In order to cover these points, assume your manager has given you the
     following information:
     The two-state line switch 3032 at the Lakeview substation is being replaced
     with a three-state motor-operated switch, and the relay at the RTU being used
     is capable of sending MCD (momentary change detection) information for
     alarm purposes.
     Although the global inhibit definition for a SCADA point allows the operator to
     inhibit all portions of the alarm processing (except for preventing abnormal
     objects from appearing on the e-terrascada exception list, as you completed
     in Lab 2), for this new switch, the operator is not to be permitted to inhibit the
     issuance of the alarm.
     The alarming for this line switch needs to be made conditional on the position
     of the other line switch at the station (LS 2931). An alarm should not be issued
     on switch 3032 unless switch 2931 is OPEN (bit position 00).

Notes:
• Upper and Lower Threshold are the default effective values for the limits.
  Note that they are flagged as SelCop’ed (+), and any Alternate Limit or
  operator-entered limits will replace them online.
• High and Low Default Limit Values are used for restoring manually-
  entered limits, if there is no Alternate Limit modeled. Whether they are
  SelCop’ed is an operational choice. If they are not, then the operators
  cannot make permanent changes to the default High and Low limits.

Note about e-terrasource modeling:
• The Analog Limit Set, under which any Analog Limits or Analog Rate
  Limits are grouped, is always named SCADA.
• Analog Alternate Limits (which reference Alternate Limit Sets) are
  displayed as children of Analog Limits in the SCADA Model tree, and their
  property sheet can be called up from there. Another efficient way to view
  them is to select “Show Children” from the property sheet of the Analog
  Limit.

[Instructor solution - Invisible in printed version]


1.    Analog measurements are telemetered similar to points
      ( RAW, PREP, & DIS values).
2.    REASONABILITY limits are checked:
       a)      For raw data from the RTU.
       b)      For converted ENGINEERED (PREPARED) values.
3.    Additional operational limits are used for alarm generation:
       a)    INTERVAL LIMITS (HIGH, LOW, or FORBIDDEN)
       b)    RATE - OF - CHANGE (for ramping analogs).
4.    Predefined limit replacement values can be substituted for MODELED or
      Interval limits.

              Lab 4: SCADA Analog Modeling
Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
        •   Copy a transmission line and its children to another part of the SCADA
            Model
        •   Add line switches to line ends.
        •   Understand the data provided by the Limit Name
        •   Understand the difference between reasonability, rate-of-change, and
            operating limits
        •   Insert a limit record for both an analog and a rate-of-change limit, and
            enter the appropriate data for both
     In order to cover these points, assume your manager has given you the
     following information:
     Your organization is putting a new 345-KV line (#34561) between the
     LAKEVIEW and DOUGLAS substations. It is to be very similar to the 345-KV line
     #34562 that runs between LAKEVIEW and the HEARN substation. It will be
     tapped into the existing buses with a motor-operated line switch, such as the
     one you created in the previous lab.
     The differences between the new 34561 line and the existing 34562 line, other
     than the end-points, are as follows:
        •   The manager would like a rate-of-change limit on the MW
            measurement for the new line.
        •   The manager would like three levels of limit alarms on the MVA analog
            measurement of line 34561, rather than the two that are on 34562,
            with the third limit creating an interval midway between the two
            existing limit intervals found in line 34562’s MVA measurement.
     The diagram on the following page shows a picture of the devices you will be
     adding and the two substations involved.

     the Network Model tree and the Scada Model tree.

                       EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


Note that on the Network Model view, you model equipment characteristics that have
meaning to the network applications – connectivity, measurements, and Network
Operational Limits.
The Line record will be found in the SubGeographical area that contains the near end
of the line – the AC Line Segment Near. The AC Line Segment (or segments, if it is a
multi-segmented line) will be a child of the Line device. And the AC Line Segment will
be displayed in the terminating substations as “AC Line Segment Near” and “AC Line
Segment Far.” The Near (N) and Far (F) Terminals are shown with both the “Near” and
“Far” line segments. Note that there is only one record for each AC Line Segment and
each Terminal, but because of the relational nature of e-terrasource, they can be
displayed in several locations.
On the Scada Model view, you see the same AC Line Segments at the near and far
substations, with their relationship to LN Equipment Groups (DEVTYPs). The terminals
at both ends of the line segment will be shown at the substation, but the
measurements will be shown only on the terminal that is native to that substation (as
reflected by the Scada Composite ID in brackets). On the SCADA view will be additional
modeling information that is specific to SCADA, for controls and calculations.

Notes:
About Time Models: The time models are entered in the standard date/time
format. If you want the read to be done on the hour, enter a period of 3600
seconds, and a time like 01-JAN-1986 00:00:00, which is an even hour time.
SCADA is not concerned with whether the date is the past or present, just
when the time starts during the day.

[Instructor solution - Invisible in printed version]


1.    Pulse accumulator totals are telemetered into COUNT or Accumulator
      records.
2.    Pulse accumulators can be:
       RESET periodically,
       or
        read as a TOTAL count. (running count or delta)
3.    Accumulator rollover is handled by SUBTRACTING previous reading from
      NEW (current) reading and adjusting cumulative total (Adding Rollover
      value).
4.    Raw integer count values are converted to floating point and INTEGER.

         Lab 5: SCADA Accumulator Modeling
     In this lab, you will familiarize yourself with the SCADA model attributes that
     affect the processing of accumulator (COUNT) objects.

Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
        •   Describe how accumulator measurements are acquired from the field
        •   Explain how accumulator data is stored on the SCADA host
        •   Handle accumulator rollover from the measurement device
     In order to cover these points, assume your manager has given you the
     following information:
     On the generator at LAKEVIEW, you are presently measuring net MWH output
     from the generator with a pulse accumulator. Your organization is making a
     wiring change out at the RTU, so there will be another accumulator that is
     measuring gross output from the generator before the station service is
     deducted.
     This new accumulator is a Landys & Gyr protocol device, and as such, it is
     freezable and has a maximum count of 4095 before rollover. Every 100 pulses
     represent one MWH.
     The new accumulator will be telemetered from the same scan group as the
     net MWH accumulator. Your manager would like to display only a whole
     number MWH to the operators.


                            Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       6-19
                              Pulse Accumulator Modeling

NOTES:
• Also for Controls - DO or SBO control is modeled on the parent
  ScanGroup record of the Control Data Item.
• The “Normal Value” parameter is oddly named. What it indicates is
  whether the controlled Discrete after this Control should be Closed (0) or
  Open (1). This is exported as the SCADAMOM field CTRLFUNC_CTRL.

                Lab 6: SCADA Control Modeling
Lab Objectives
 After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Add a CARD with RELAYs to the RTU subtree
  •   Add CTRL records to a status point
  •   Assign telemetry to CTRL objects
  •   Create a digital control lock
 In order to cover these points, assume your manager has given you the following
 information:
 The three-state, motor-operated line switch 3032 at the LAKEVIEW substation is
 being wired on the existing RTU for digital TRIP and CLOSE relays. Since there are no
 existing control relay cards modeled for the LAKEVIEW RTU, you have been asked to
 provide one at ADRS G5. The protocol-specific RTU issues have already been
 resolved, and the type of RELAYs used are exactly like those for the motor-operated
 switch that has been set up in the TEST_RTU, which is already in your model.
 Once you have the controls and associated telemetry in place, you are to create a
 digital control lock so that the switch to which you are adding controls cannot be
 opened unless the line switching device 2931 is closed.

 Task 2: Add Command Objects
        You now need to add the Command (CTRL) objects that represent OPEN and
        CLOSE to the Discrete object that represents the motor-operated switch.

Your Action                                     System Response

1. From the Scada Model tree, find the          Command record is inserted, and the property
   LAKEVIEW MOS 3032 Switch and                 sheet displayed on the right.
   locate its MOS Discrete record.
   Right-click the record and add a new
   Command object.
2. Name your new Command OPEN by
   making the association with the
   corresponding Command Name.
   <Save>.


3. In the General parameter group of
   your OPEN Command, specify the
   following:
   • Sort Order: 10
   • Normal Value: Open
       Note: On transformation, the Normal Value will be
       mapped to the CTRLFUNC_CTRL flag.
   •   As your expected bit pattern resulting from a successful
       trip is 00, set the parameters for both Expected Status
       and Expected Extended Status to No, (the host will
       compare the response from the RTU with these
       expectations to decide on the success of the operation).
   •   Time Out: 20
       This represents a 20-second timeout for non-response
       from the RTU before considering the operation a failure.
   •   Operation Time: 30
       This represents the number of milliseconds the signal
       must be applied to the RTU address to obtain the
       required RTU response for the control (protocol-
       dependent value).
   •   Wait Time: 10
       This represents the number of seconds that the
       operator must wait between successive controls to the
       device.


                                Proprietary – See Copyright Page                    7-30
                                       Controls Modeling

       Now you are ready to satisfy the last spec for these controls, namely, to insure
       your controlled switch 3032 is not opened unless the line-switching device

   MOS Switch 3032’s OPEN Command object.

   Insert/Command Lock.                                  calls up the property sheet on the
                                                         right.

   The only restriction is that it must be unique
   under this Command record. <Save>

                                     Controls Modeling

5. Expand the Scada Model tree to also show the
   LS 2931 Switch’s Discrete children.
6. Drag and Drop the LS 2931 STTS Discrete into
   the Measurement Association field on the
   Command Lock record.


   Note: There are only a few enterable fields on the LOCK record:
          •   Lock Name: This must be unique within a single control.
          •   Alias Name: The EMP60 convention is that this would be “Switch
              NEPOOL EAST LAKEVIEW LS 3032 MOS,” but it can be any unique value.
          •   Assigned to Analog: Set this to No, as the association is to a Discrete.
          •   Invert Lock: When selected (Yes), this specifies that the interlocking
              status point must be “clear” (e.g., Open) for the control to be allowed.
              Since you want the 3032 TRIP control to be allowed only when Discrete
              2931 is “set” (e.g., Closed) open, set this to No.
          •   Can Override Lock: If this is set, the Operator may choose to override
              the locking condition. Set this property to No.
          •   Lower and Upper Limits of the Valid Range: Data would be entered
              here only if this lock were assigned to an ANALOG. The values entered
              would specify the valid range of the analog measurement that would
              allow the trip of 3032.
              -   Leave these properties blank.
      For Setpoints, the SetPoint Lock records are configured in the same manner.
7. <Save> your changes.

Summary
       A SCADA model can contain CTRL objects for status points, ANALOGS, and
       SETPNT objects for ANALOGS. These objects contain parameters that describe
       the way the e-terrascada front-end processor communicates with the RTU to
       activate a given relay, or pulse an analog to change its measured value. In this
       unit, you gained experience in modeling digital output controls and assigning
       them to appropriate telemetry.

Tagging
Tagging enables operators to label a device such as a breaker for
maintenance purposes, to constrain operation of the device, or to alert
operators of special conditions in the power system. Tags are typically
placed on devices and records in the SCADA database, but can be
configured for any data source.
The Tagging database provides a standard set of tag types that can easily
be expanded and customized to match specific requirements.
For more information about Tagging functionality, see the e-terrascada
Operator's Guide, Section 5 “Tagging Procedures.”


                            Proprietary – See Copyright Page          8-4
                                         Tagging

NOTES:
• Calculation records exist in the e-terrasource database for Function-type
  MEASes only.
• Other MEASes are defined by the MeasurementGrouping field on the
  Discrete, Analog, or Accumulator record, which is shown in the tree view
  [Meas Group: XXXX].
• Each of the Calculation’s children corresponds to an argument of the
  Calculation Function.
• If the argument references a record that will not be a child of the
  Calculation MEAS in SCADAMOM, the ReferenceFlag will be Yes, and a
  “REF” record (ALGREF, PNTREF, etc.) will be modeled as a child of the MEAS
  record after export.
• If you want the referenced Analog to be exported as a child of the
  Calculation MEAS (as is often the case with output arguments), then the
  flag will be No.

For Simultaneous controls:
• Operator requests one breaker to change.
• SCADA executes that single control.
• SCADA expects a pre-defined list of status POINTs to change to a pre-
  defined set of statuses.
For full example, see ESCA60: SUBSTN=TEST_RTU, DEVICE=SIM_TRIP_1...

The CalculationArgument’s Order Number determines which of the two
referenced controls is the “master.”
The Calculation record’s Control Type parameter is exported as two fields in
SCADAMOM:
• TYPE_MEAS = MBO1 (labeled Function Type on Online Editor)
• CONT_MEAS = True (“CTRL” in the Online Editor’s Operation combo box)

NOTE:
• Operator issues ONE control to the one point. Because of wiring in the
  field, other devices also change state.
• When the devices change state in the field, SCADA correctly detects that
  they were due to operator action.

For Multiple Controls:
• Operator requests one (dummy) breaker to change.
• SCADA sends controls to a pre-defined list of breakers.
• SCADA expects each status POINT to report change.
For full example, see ESCA60: SUBSTN=TEST_RTU, DEVTYP=LS,
DEVICE=MULTIPLE_TRIP...

Note 1: There are only two arguments necessary for the ADD implementation of the
ANALOG_ADDITION Subroutine: one input (READ attribute) and one output (WRITE attribute).
The input argument is both a trigger and open-ended, which means you can assign as many
values to the input as you need, and each of them will cause the calculation to be made
when they change in value.

Note 2: Because ARG1 is open-ended, the description for this function might be more
accurate if it were:

       ARG2 = 0
       Do WHILE ARG1 not NULL
         ARG2 = ARG2 + ARG1
       End Do

Note 3: For help on functions, press <Ctrl F1> while viewing any function to bring up the
Online Help dialog, open to the EMS Modeling guide. You can locate the general descriptions
of all available subroutines in the SCADA Modeling/SCADA Model Details/Calculation
Functions section.

Summary
  A SCADA model can contain calculated measurements that represent a known algorithm
  being applied to one or more existing measurements, to produce one or more new output
  measurements. This involves adding a record of the type calculation, adding the input and
  output arguments for the referenced function to the calculation, and assigning these
  arguments to the desired measurements. In this unit, you gained experience in modeling
  calculation that combined MW measurements into a total MW value through an open-ended
  addition function

Note on modeling Nodes in e-terrasource:
In SCADAMOM, nodes are named in fields on the measurement and device
records.
In e-terrasource , nodes are explicitly modeled as ConnectivityNode
records in a particular substation. Devices have one or two Terminal
children that are associated with the ConnectivityNodes. The export logic
will ensure that the node fields are filled in appropriately in SCADAMOM.


                            Proprietary – See Copyright Page                11-14
                                    SCADA Topology


<!-- salto de página -->

                      EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


Note on modeling Lines in e-terrasource:
SCADAMOM: When a Line device spans substations, the Near and Far
Nodes, and the Far Substation name must be modeled on the Device
record. A physical line will be represented by Devices in both Substations,
each modeling the Near and Far Nodes, and the name of the remote
station.
e-terrasource : Nodes are explicitly modeled as ConnectivityNode records
in a particular substation. Devices have one or two Terminal children that
are associated with the ConnectivityNodes. Therefore, a Line-type Device
can have one Terminal that is associated with a ConnectivityNode in the
“near” substation, and a second Terminal association to a
ConnectivityNode in the “far” substation. The export logic will ensure that
the node and substation fields are filled in appropriately in SCADAMOM.

                                     SCADA Topology

Notes:
When databases are imported from existing HDB clones, both the
“Network” Terminal (which is associated with a Connectivity Node) and the
SCADA Connectivity Node may be populated. But when a device is inserted
in e-terrasource, SCADA Connectivity Node will be null (and thus will default
to the nodes defined by the Terminal). If the nodes are different, the “For
SCADA” and “For Network” flags must be modeled.
For a SCADA-only substation, the Connectivity Nodes will be populated on
import, and the SCADA Connectivity associations are made directly from
the measurements or Devices to those nodes. There will be no Terminal
records as children of these Devices.

[Instructor solution - Invisible in printed version]


1.    SCADA Topology determines ENERGIZATION and CONNECTIVITY of
      electrical devices in order to drive alarmable events, map boards, and
      dynamic one-line displays.
2.    SCADA Topology runs on switching device state change AND periodically to
      catch ANALOG drift.
3.    Devices and substations over a modeled voltage level can be given the status
      of:
       a)    LIVE – voltage - trusted
       b)    DEAD – no voltage - trusted
       c)    AMBIGUOUS – contradictory measurements - untrusted
       d)    UNKNOWN – no measurements available - untrusted

                                         SCADA Topology

Task 4: Enable and Tune Topology Processing
   All of the topology modeling you have added so far will not be used unless SCADA
   Topology Processing is enabled in the model. On the SCADA Parameters page, you can
   tune the behavior of SCADATOP, as well as enable its processing.


Your Action                                    System Response

1. From your e-terrasource client,
   select Telemetry/ Scada Global
   Parameters.
2. Right-click on the single item in the          The property sheet will have a number of
   resulting grid and select Properties.          property groups.
3. Select the ScadaTopology
   Parameters group, and ensure/note
   that:
       •   Topology Enabled = Yes
       •   Substation Voltage Alarm Category and Substation Voltage Area Of
           Responsibility (both associated with topology alarms) are configurable.
       •   You may choose to process connectivity at two different levels:
           -      ScadaTopology processing only = No: At the system level (connectivity is
                  calculated across substations)
           -      ScadaTopology processing only = Yes: At the substation level only (buses
                  end at the devices that have Far Station identifiers)
           •   Topology Minimum SCADA Voltage Level - The minimum voltage level of the
               KV measurements to examine during processing.
           •   Percentage Agreement for Live/Dead State – Percentage agreements for
               LIVE and DEAD calculations for buses. (You can ensure that no bus
               measurement is AMBIGUOUS if you insure both these parameters are greater
               than 50.)
           •   Topology Drift Rate (Minutes) – How often to process topology in the
               absence of a triggering switching event.
           •   Delay after Status Change – How many seconds to delay processing after
               the initial triggering switching event (to capture many associated status point
               state changes in a single topology processing run).
       Note: You can also configure which events the SCADATOP client will report to the
       Alarm Server.

Summary
    SCADA topology is used to monitor connectivity and energization at modeled
    locations throughout your SCADA model. Normally, KV analog measurements are
    added to devices and specified as measurement nodes. These measurement nodes
    are linked together from device to device by entering local/near node specifications
    and far node specifications for the devices involved. Devices that span substations
    between the measurement nodes are given a far station as well.
    A correct topology model will allow the SCADA topology processing to alert the
    operators to islands and dead power equipment.

 Task 3: Configure HDR Files
    HDR files are found in two locations during operations:
        •   A recording directory, specified by the environment variable
            HABUSER_HDR_RECORDING
        •   A reconstruction directory, specified by the environment variable
            HABUSER_HDR_RECON
    The system records its data in the recording directory, and the operator reconstructs, or
    plays back history, from the reconstruction directory. If these locations are not the same,
    then it is up to the user to create his or her own mechanism for making the recording files
    available to the operator for reconstruction.
    From a modeler perspective, you have control over how the recording directory is
    managed by e-terrascada.


 Your Action                                   System Response

1. From the SCADA Configuration
   property sheet, Scada HDR
   Parameters group, in the Data File
   Information area, you are able to:


    •   Specify the Optimal HDR File Count, which will serve as a warning to the operator that
        the recording directory is becoming full, and that recording may stop.
        How many files will be closed before your operators receive an alarm?
        _________________


                              Proprietary – See Copyright Page                    13-31
                                       SCADA History


<!-- salto de página -->

                            EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


    •   Specify the Maximum HDR File Count, which will determine the number of files, and
        thus the amount of history, that will be kept before recording stops.
        How many files will your system store in the recording directory?
        _________________
    •   Specify Maximum Time recording file allowed to be open, which, along with the
        number of measurements chosen for recording, helps determines the size of each file
        in the recording directory.
        How much data is contained in the files on your system (time frame)?
        _________________


    To keep a rolling window of history, the modeler can specify auto-deletion of older
    recording files, so that recording is continuous and does not stop when the maximum file
    number is reached. System operators also have the ability to delete recording files on
    demand to make room in the recording directory.
2. Also in the Scada HDR Parameters
   group, note that you are able to:
    •   Ask the system to Purge old HDR files to make room for new file and Log auto-
        deletion of HDR files. This will keep a rolling time frame of history whose size depends
        on the parameters set above, and report an event to the Alarm Server when a
        recording file is deleted due to the automatic purge.
    •   Specify Log HDR File deletion by Operators, which will result in the reporting of an
        event to the Alarm Server when a recording file is deleted by a system operator.

Summary
   SCHIST and HDR are auxiliary functions of e-terrascada that allow for capturing a
   historical record of SCADA operations, such that it can be used for viewing online or for
   reconstruction for playback or historical measurement comparisons.
   The SCADA model contains global parameters to control how HDR manages its work,
   measurement level parameters to indicate which measurements are recorded for SCHIST,
   and how frequently, as well as which measurements are written to files by the HDR
   function.

1.    Remote SITEs can be modeled to serve as PRIMARY, SECONDARY,
      TERTIARY, or QUATERNARY sources of SCADA measurements.

   exchanged between sites.

   remote site upon SITE Communications failures.

                     Lab 11: SCADA ISD Modeling
Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
        •   Explain the importance of the various ISD processing parameters
        •   Add a new FEP site, and modify its attributes
        •   Assign measurements to a new site
     In order to cover these points, assume your manager has given you the following
     information:
     Your organization is putting a new pair of front-end processors (FEPs) that will be
     obtaining the data for the new measurements on the transmission line you have
     placed between the LAKEVIEW and DOUGLAS substations.
     This FEP site will have to be added to your SCADA model, and the measurements on the
     transmission line set, so that the data acquisition process polls for them.
     Note: The tasks in this lab only add the new FEP2 SITE record and assigned some
     measurements to it. At a later date (after the new e-terracontrol front end and the new
     RTU have been configured, for instance), the CFE and RTU records will also need to be
     modeled, and the measurements assigned to scan addresses and cards.


Task 1: ISD Processing Parameters
     As with many other e-terrascada features, ISD processing must be enabled from the
     SCADA Configuration. In this section of the lab, we will view the parameters and
     comment on their importance.

  modeler know which measurements are internally generated (e.g., calculations) rather

In the General group:
   •   System Name: Call this FEP2. This field will be used to resolve the %SYSTEM%
       proxy that is often used to create unique network object names for sites.
   •   SCADA Front END: Set this to Yes. This is a local FEP and not a remote control
       center. It gives the operator navigation techniques for moving to FEP to see
       data about the communications for measurements from this site. Also permits
       demand scans to this site and enables the more-efficient Proxysrv connection
       to it.
   •   Front End Primary IP Address: In a real system, this would be the IP address or
       node name of the front end host computer. In our test system, enter
       000.000.000.000 to allow it to connect to any system.

Other General group Site parameters that can be left as is, since this is a copy of an
existing FEP site:
   •   Not in Service: Make the operator manually put this site into service at run-time.
   •   No Polling of Remote Site: This is a sending-only site and cannot poll us.
   •   Log Controls: If InterSite controls are attempted from this site, log it in the
       SCADA log.
   •   Suppress Rate of Change: If the remote site is issuing InterSite controls, do not
       issue rate-of-change alarms to the local operators.
   •   Enable InterSite Tagging/Notes: Allow exchange of tags with this site (obsolete
       on this system; used with e-terrascada 2.6 only).
   •   URL of WebFG Display, (and the associated Title for WebFG URL Callup): Give
       operator recognizable URL to go to when this site shows up on the exception
       list.
   •   Polling Rate (Milliseconds): Override of ISD Scan Rate parameter for this site.
   Finally in the General group, note the four network object names, with which the
   data acquisition process will attempt to open a connection. (Because of the use of
   proxies or tokens, we will not have to change these values either.)
   •   Data Acquisition InterSite NETIO Object Definition: The object to connect to
       for measurement/quality polling and response.
   •   Control InterSite NETIO Object Definition: The object to connect to for sending
       and receiving controls.
   •   Tagging InterSite NETIO Object Definition: The object to connect to for
       exchanging tags. (Obsolete on this system; used with e-terrascada 2.6 only.)
   •   Front End Download InterSite NETIO Object Definition: If you were configuring
       an Online Incremental Update of the front-end sites, you would use this object.

Summary
   ISD is another auxiliary function of e-terrascada that allows native SCADA sites to pass
   measurement information to polling sites that have these measurements modeled.
   The SCADA model contains global parameters to control how the ISD function manages its
   work, as well as measurement level parameters to indicate which measurements are
   polled for from, or delivered to, a remote site, as the result of a poll.

        Lab 13: Efficiently Developing the Model
Templates are a very powerful tool for building models. A template is a group of
related records that represents a reusable modeling pattern. A template can be
repeatedly instantiated to quickly build a model. For example, templates can be used
to represent a prototypical substation, an equipment group or bay, or a single switch.
Templates can also have parameters associated with them. When the template is
used to create an instance, the user is prompted to enter values for the template’s
parameters. These user-entered values can be used to derive many of the instance’s
properties. For example, the user could enter an “Equipment Name,” which is used to
populate many of the names of the instance records.
Instances that are created from templates retain information about the originating
template. This information can be viewed at the top of the property sheets


Lab Objectives
       After completing this lab, you will be able to:
          •   Use the Template Management Environment to create and maintain
              templates
          •   Create a template to create a simple template
          •   Use a template to create a device in the model


       In this lab, you will create a template from a breaker defined in the HEARN
       substation along with its whole hierarchy. Then you will instantiate a similar
       breaker in the same substation.


                              Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     16-15
                              Efficiently Developing the Model

Task 6: Defining the Template Parameters
        Template parameters are a powerful feature that can simplify modeling tasks
        for users. In a typical template, there may be many properties on several
        records that are identical (or very similar). For example:
        If a template represents a piece of equipment, there may be many records
        that can have their names derived by a naming convention based on a single
        user-entered “equipment name.”
        Parameters can also be used with metadata calculations to set certain
        properties. A single, user-entered “Voltage Level” parameter could possibly be
        used to derive values for ratings, limits, and alarm categories.
        Judicious use of template parameters can allow you to have a small number
        of powerful templates, instead of having many similar templates that vary in
        small ways.
        Exploring and explaining all the options for defining a parameter is not in the
        scope of this course∗. In the next step of this lab, you will only define a few
        sets of simple parameters for your template to become generic.

Summary
       SCADA topology is used to monitor connectivity and energization at modeled
       locations throughout your SCADA model. Normally, KV analog measurements
       are added to devices and specified as measurement nodes. These
       measurement nodes are linked together from device to device by entering
       local/near node specifications and far node specifications for the devices
       involved. Devices that span substations between the measurement nodes are
       given a far station as well.
       A correct topology model will allow the SCADA topology processing to alert the
       operators to islands and dead power equipment.

                               Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       16-28
                               Efficiently Developing the Model

EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


      Proprietary - See Copyright Page          17-1
 Moving the Model to the EMS SCADA (Review)


<!-- salto de página -->

EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


      Proprietary - See Copyright Page          17-2
 Moving the Model to the EMS SCADA (Review)


<!-- salto de página -->

                     EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


Each sequence has three basic steps, plus some optional ones:
1. Produce CIM/XML that represents the model data in the workspace. The
   CIM/XML Import/Export service creates the CIM/XML using a CIM profile
   called "ETS." The same ETS profile is used regardless of the HDB
   database that is being processed, and it contains all modeled fields -
   nothing is filtered out. So, whether you intend to populate only NETMOM
   or only ALARM, the same profile is used. Refer to CIM/XML Import/Export
   for more information on CIM profiles.
2. Feed the CIM/XML data to the transformation subsystem and produce
   data that can be loaded into an HDB database. For each supported HDB
   database, the transformation subsystem has modules that contain
   instructions on how to convert the e-terrasource data into HDB data (and
   vice versa for imports).
3. Load the resulting HDB data into a clone or savecase.
4. Optionally, e-terraplatform validation programs can be executed, and
5. The savecases can be compressed into a zip archive.


                           Proprietary - See Copyright Page               17-3
                      Moving the Model to the EMS SCADA (Review)


<!-- salto de página -->

                      EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


e-terrasource provides several formats for importing and exporting
data:
•   CIM/XML - CIM/XML files representing a complete model authority
    set can be imported into a workspace or exported from a
    workspace. Also, CIM/XML difference models (incremental files) can
    be exported from projects, or imported into e-terrasource as
    projects.
•   Model Authority Set Dump/Load - e-terrasource has a native format
    for writing out model authority set data to a file. Model authority sets
    can be dumped to files or loaded from files in this format.
•   Project Dump/Load - e-terrasource also has a native format for
    writing out projects to a file. Projects can be dumped to files or
    loaded from files in this format.
•   Excel - The e-terrasource user interface supports the ability to
    export model data to Excel and import changes from Excel.


                            Proprietary - See Copyright Page               17-4
                       Moving the Model to the EMS SCADA (Review)


<!-- salto de página -->

EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


      Proprietary - See Copyright Page          17-5
 Moving the Model to the EMS SCADA (Review)


<!-- salto de página -->

                      EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


The e-terrasource installation predefines one export sequence per HDB
database, as well as a “combined” sequence that can export all
supported HDB databases. These sequences can be modified in the
Administration view.
The files will be exported to the default export directory,
            <drive>:\ETERRA\e-terrasource\export
on the e-terrasource server.

Sequences in the export to e-terraplatform are:
1.    Produce CIM/ XML file representing all of the model data.
2.    TRANSFORM the CIM/XML data into HDBIMPORT- compatible CSV files.
3.    Load the resulting HDB data into clones.
4.    Execute e-terraplatform VALIDATION or Validators.
5.    Create savecases and zip into an ARCHIVE.

                       EMS012 e-terrasource : Building a SCADA Model


Lab 14: Moving the Model to the HDB SCADAMOM
       Models are exchanged between e-terrasource and e-terrahabitat–based
       applications using an extensible transformation subsystem.
       For each supported HDB database, the transformation subsystem has
       modules that contain instructions on how to convert the e-terrasource data
       into HDB data.
       The Project validation sequence is executed upon user request. Project
       validation checks only the validation rules that are associated to the
       requested validation sequence, and also associated either directly or indirectly
       with the change items in a project.
       Validation sequences, modules, and rules are defined in the e-terrasource
       metadata. Refer to the e-terrasource Metamodel Guide for further
       information.
Lab Objectives
       After completing this lab, you will be able to:
          •   Understand the project validation process and perform a validation
          •   Understand the transformation process and execute a transformation
              from e-terrasource to the e-terraplatform SCADA

Summary
Project validation is executed upon user request. Project validation checks only the
validation rules that are associated the requested validation sequence, and also
associated either directly or indirectly with the change items in a project.
Workspace validation is executed upon user request. Workspace validation checks all
of the workspace data against the validation rules that are associated with the
validation sequence that was requested.
Validation sequences, modules, and rules are defined in the e-terrasource metadata.
One of the main purposes of e-terrasource is to supply EMS models to
e-terraplatform. Although the particulars regarding target environments (e.g., test vs
production) and modeling business processes may vary widely from organization to
organization, the basic concept is the same: extract a portion of the model from
e-terrasource, transform it, and place it into an e-terraplatform HDB database.
Imports in e-terrasource simply work in the opposite direction.

Document Conventions
      The following conventions are used throughout this document.


 Pull-down menu       A greater-than symbol ( > ) and italics are used to
                      indicate pull-down menu paths.
                      For example:
                         Analyst Displays>Mode Modeling>Mode Directory


 Soft keys or         Bold formatting is applied to indicate a selectable point.
 buttons on a         For example:
 display
                         Apply


 Physical key on      A box is placed around the text that appears on the
 the keyboard         actual key on the keyboard.
                      For example:
                         Enter


 Text to be entered   The code example style is used, which applies the
 verbatim by the      monospaced font “Courier New.”
 student, or          For example:
 examples of code
                         Host: PC1392
                         Account: Student1
                         Password: escatrain


 <>                   Text enclosed in angle brackets ( < > ) indicates
                      information you must supply.


 []                   Square brackets ( [ ] ) indicate optional qualifiers,
                      arguments, or data.

Netmom records represent various types of equipment and fields represent
attributes of the records.


For example, the NETMOM record LN represents a line segment and the field
R_LN represents the resistance of the Line Segment.

                      Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


A “node” is a point in the power system model to which power system components
are connected to represent electrical connectivity.


Node names can not be duplicated within a station, though multiple components
can be connected to one node.


The nodes reside in the network connectivity model under a Voltage-Level.

                    Lab 2: Explore the Network Model
Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
        •   Navigate the network Model
        •   Switch Between different views
        •   Search and navigate to different devices


Task 1: Find the Network Model Tree View
  1. Click the Network Button in the Toolbar.
  2. Select Network Model from the dropdown list.


  3. By clicking the “>” symbol, explore the Network Model tree view starting
     with geographical regions, e.g. ECAR, NEPOOL, etc.
  4. Using your knowledge of ETS to Network Mapping, how many CO records
     are present in the model? _______ (Hint, What are CO records mapped to
     in e-terrasource?)
  5. What are DV records from Netmom called in e-terrasource?
     ___________________.
  6. How many Substations are within the DV ECAR? ______.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                  2-28
                             Network Model Structures


<!-- salto de página -->

                    Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 2: Find the Switch 6869 in Substation PARKHILL
     1. Navigate to substation PARKHILL under Network Model → NEPOOL
        → SubGeographical Region → NORT → Substation → PARKHILL →
        Voltage Level → 345 → Switch → 6869. Double click on the switch to
        open the property sheet.
     2. Find the same device using the Search Function. You are searching
        for the switch 6869 in the Substation PARKHILL. Add filters to the CIM
        Path Name that contain these.


     3. Right click on the results to open the property sheet for the Switch.


                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       2-29
                            Network Model Structures


<!-- salto de página -->

                    Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


     4. You would typically use the search function to find the equipment you
        want to locate as it is much quicker than navigating down in most
        cases. On large models, the Search button is a lot faster to use than
        the navigation menu


Task 3: Find the Parameters for Various Equipment using
Search.
     A request has come in to identify several parameters for various devices
     in the model. The devices are located in different Substations. The easiest
     way to locate them would be using the search button and adding filters to
     locate the devices using the CIM path name. Remember that you can add
     multiple filters in the search function to locate the devices.
     1. What is the Load Type associated (Look at the property group
        “Associations” in the property sheet) with the Equivalent Load NTP3 in
        the Substation KINCAIRD? _______
     2. What is the Load Type associated with the Equivalent Load 62 in the
        Substation HANOVER? _______.
     3. How many Switches show up in the results when you search for a
        Switch with “68” in the CIM path name? ________
     4. How many of these switches belong to the SubGeographicalRegion
        NORT? ______ (Hint: the CIM Path Name for a switch is of the format
        GeographicalRegion SubGeographicalRegion Substation VoltageLevel
        Switch)
     5. Is the Switch 141143 located in Substation WVILLE of the type
        Normally Open? _______ (Search under Network> Network Others in
        the property sheet).


Task 4: Find the Connectivity Tree View
     1. Click the Network button in the toolbar.
     2. Select Connectivity from the dropdown list.
     3. By clicking the “+” symbol, explore the Connectivity tree view starting
        with geographical regions, e.g. NEPOOL.

        Lab 3.1: Creating Equipment Containers
Lab Objectives
     After completing this lab, you will be able to:
         •   Create a new substation
         •   Create Voltage Levels
         •   Create Lines that are the equipment containers for Line Segments


Task 1: Create a New Substation
  1. Create a new Project xxxx_Containers (where xxxx is a personal
     identifier), and make it your active project. (All the projects currently
     loaded in your workspace are displayed on the home page)


     To make a project your active proect, it should be selected from the
     project drowdown on the toolbar.


  2. Using the Search Tool, search for SubGeographicalRegion EAST.
  3. Right-click on result from the table and click “Show in tree”. Choose
     Network Model.
  4. Right-click on the SubGeographicalRegion and select “Insert Substation”


                           Proprietary – See Copyright Page                      3-39
                              Network Device Modelling


<!-- salto de página -->

                     Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


  5. Change the EMSName for this substation to CLASS. Save your project
     (Ctrl + S).


Task 2: Insert Voltage Levels
  1. Search for the newly created substation CLASS and open it in the network
     model tree.
  2. Right click on the Substation in the tree and Insert a VoltageLevel.
  3. Change the EMSName of this new VoltageLevel to 14.
  4. On the property sheet, under the Associations Property Group, Assign a
     Base Voltage of 14.


  5. Insert another VoltageLevel and change the EMSName to 345 and assign
     a Base Voltage of 345.
  6. Save your project.

                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                  3-40
                             Network Device Modelling


<!-- salto de página -->

                    Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 3: Creating Lines
  1. Search for the SubGeographicalRegion EAST and show in the network
     model tree.
  2. Insert a new Line and set the EMSName to be CLASS_1.
  3. Using the same procedure, insert two new lines CLASS_2 and CLASS_3.
  4. Note that the Line here is merely an equipment container and does not
     have any of the parameters associated with a transmission line such as
     resistance or reactance. Those are properties that belong to an
     ACLineSegment.
  5. Save your project.
     Note how the network model tree appears for SubGeographicalRegion
     EAST


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                3-41
                             Network Device Modelling


<!-- salto de página -->

                     Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


                              Lab 3.2: Creating Equipment
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Add Switches
  •   Add Connectivity Nodes
  •   Add a SynchronousMachine
  •   Add a Transformer


Task 1: Create ConnectivityNodes
  1. Create a new Project xxxx_Equipment (where xxxx is a personal
     identifier), and make it your active project.
  2. Using the Search Tool, search for Substation CLASS and open the
     Substation in the connectivity Tree.
  3. Expand the Substation to open up the VoltageLevel 14.
  4. Right-click on the VoltageLevel and select “Insert ConnectivityNode”


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                  3-42
                             Network Device Modelling


<!-- salto de página -->

                     Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


  5. Change the EMSName for this new ConnectivityNode to 701. Save your
     project (Ctrl + S).
  6. Repeat the process to add Node 702 under Voltage Level 14.
  7. Repeat this process to create nodes 17 and 18 under the Voltage Level
     345.


Task 2: Insert Switches
  1. Search for the Substation CLASS and open it in the network model tree.
  2. Right click on the VoltageLevel 14 and insert a Switch.
  3. Change the EMSName of this switch to 701702.
  4. Save your project.
  5. Right click on this new switch in the network tree view and insert a
     terminal.
  6. Change the EMSName of this terminal to 701702_1 (This is just a
     convention where the near terminal is named _1 and the far is named _2).
  7. On the terminal property sheet, set the Identification property
     “Near/far/primary/secondary/tertiary terminal” to “Near”.
  8. Set Associations properties for Terminal 701702_1. For “Connectivity
     node”, select “NEPOOL EAST CLASS 14 701” from the reference list.


  9. Insert another terminal 701702_2 and set the
     “Near/far/primary/secondary/tertiary terminal” to “Far”. Assign a
     connectivity node of “NEPOOL EAST CLASS 14 702”.
  10. Save your project
  11. Create another switch with EMSName 1718 under the KV Level 345.
  12. Create two terminals, one near and one far using the naming conventions
     and steps outlined above and Assign the near Node as Node 17 and the
     far Node as Node 18.
  13. Save your project.

Graphic Modeler Basics:
The Graphic Modeler component of the user interface provides several schematic views of the
electrical network. This is just a different presentation of the same objects modeled in the tree
and grid views:
•Substation Overview – This overview display shows all of the substations within a
SubGeographicalRegion and the ACLineSegments that connect them. The substations can be
overlaid on a geographical map based on their latitude/longitude.
•Substation Detail – This schematic display shows the detailed model of a single substation
and its connected equipment regardless of voltage level.
•Voltage Level Detail – This schematic display is very similar to the substation detail except
that it displays a single voltage level within a substation.
•SCADA Topology – This schematic display enables the user to maintain mixed network and
SCADA equipment, or SCADA-only topology information.
•DC Line Overview – This overview display shows the DC network within a
GeographicalRegion. Accessed from the Network Model or Network Connectivity trees, it
shows Substations, DCConverters, and DCLineSegments.
Note: While production of FG displays from the Graphic Modeler representation is a nice idea, it
has not yet been implemented.
See e-terrasource User’s Guide, section “Graphic Modeler”.


                                Proprietary – See Copyright Page                           4-3
                                        Graphic Modeler


<!-- salto de página -->

                      Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Substation or Voltage Level Detail:
To view a schematic display of a substation, right-click on a substation name,
point to Graphic Modeler, and click Substation Detail.
To view a schematic display of a particular voltage level within a substation,
right-click on a voltage level name, point to Graphic Modeler, and click Voltage
Level Detail.


The features and functions of these two types of displays are virtually identical.
For the purposes of this discussion, the Substation Detail display is used.


Note that if you hover the mouse over a symbol, its full identification is shown.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                          4-4
                                  Graphic Modeler


<!-- salto de página -->

                        Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Substation Overview:
To display an overview of all substations within a SubGeographicalRegion and the
ACLineSegments that connect them, right-click on a SubGeographicalRegion name on
the Network tree view, point to Graphic Modeler, and click Substation Overview.
The Substation Overview appears in the center pane. Substations and the AC line
connections between them are shown, along with navigation points to adjacent
SubGeographicalRegions. An AC line connection between substations is shown as a
single straight line unless you create Inflection Points.
The overview display has the following features:
• If you hover the mouse over a substation or AC line, its full identification is shown.
• Double-clicking the center of a substation box displays its property sheet in the
   auxiliary pane.
• Double-clicking the button in the top right corner of a substation box opens the
   Substation Detail display in a new tab.
• If you hover the mouse over an AC line and press “J”, the display jumps to the next
   station. Alternatively, you can right-click the AC line, and choose “Jump to Substation
   <name>” from the context menu.
• Double-clicking the name of an adjacent SubGeographicalRegion displays the
   overview for that region.
• Whether or not a map is displayed is controlled by buttons to the right of the
   coordinates (based on availability of Microsoft Virtual Earth).

Graphic Modeler Copy of a single item or a group of items:
• Create a region containing a single item or a group of items.
• Right-click on the selected region, point to Region Edit, and click Copy.
• Choose the desired paste location, right-click on the canvas, point to Edit, and
click Paste.
You can paste multiple times to create multiple copies. The pasted records
remain selected in a region.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     4-19
                                  Graphic Modeler


<!-- salto de página -->

                      Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


The Graphic Modeler supports two methods to perform a deep copy of a
collection of items:
• Database metadata-defined deep copy – The e-terrasource metadata is used
to define the nature and extent of the deep copy. For further information about
configuring deep copy metadata, refer to the e-terrasource Metamodel Guide.
• Client-configured deep copy – This type of deep copy is driven by a query
definition stored in the client’s Graphic Modeler configuration.
Both forms of deep copy allow the user to select a region of connected
equipment, and perform a deep copy using the region’s context menu.
• The Graphic Modeler initiates the deep copy and pops up a Clipboard
Scratchpad view with the deep copy results, where the data can be manipulated.
• When you are satisfied with the collection of objects in the Clipboard
Scratchpad, click the Copy to Clipboard button              on the scratchpad toolbar,
then paste onto a Graphic Modeler canvas and save.

                                 Graphic Modeler

                                    Lab 6 Contingency Model
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Create a contingency and assign a contingent element
  •   Create a contingency group
  •   Assign a contingency to a contingency group


Task 1: Create a Contingency
  1. Create a new Project, name it xxxx_ctg and make it your active project.
  2. Open the contingency tree.
  3. Right-click on any contingency and do a deep copy of the Contingency
     hierarchy.
  4. Right click the contingency tab and paste.
  5. This will open up the new contingency tab. Change the EMSName for this
     contingency to TEST_1. Add a description “345 KV Contingency”. Change
     the sort order and save your project.
  6. You have created a new contingency.
  7. Similarly, create another contingency TEST_2 with a description “138 KV
     Contingency”.


Task 2: Change the Contingent Equipment
  1. Search for this new contingency TEST_1 using the search tool and open
     in the tree view.
  2. The equipment associated needs to be changed. Expand the equipment
     tab and double click to open it up.
  3. In the associations tab, click the ellipsis next to the equipment box to open
     up the dialog to specify a reference.
  4. Search for the ACLineSegment 34532 1, select it and click OK.
  5. Change the sort-order and save your project.
  6. Repeat the process for contingency TEST_2 and the line segment 13822 1.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                    6-17
                              Contingency Modeling


<!-- salto de página -->

                    Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 3: Create a Contingency Group.
  1. Open the Table Explorer and go to Network > Contingencies > CtgGroup.
  2. Right-click on an existing CtgGroup and click on clone n times.
  3. Clone this once and a new contingency group will be created in the list
     with a blank EMSName.


  4. Assign an EMSName of LAB and a description “ALL LAB
     CONTINGENCIES”. Change the Sort Order. Save your project.


Task 4: Assign the Contingency to the Contingency Group
  1. In the table view, open the table for Ctg_CtgGroup.
  2. The top row for this will be empty. In the EMSName, type TEST_1. and hit
     enter.


                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page                      6-18
                             Contingency Modeling


<!-- salto de página -->

                  Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


3. Save the project. This creates the new Ctg_CtgGroup which will be used
   to assign the newly created contingency to the newly created contingency
   group.
4. Right click on the new Ctg_CtgGroup and open the property sheet.
5. Under the associations tab, assign the Contingency Group of LAB and the
   Contingency of TEST_1.
6. Save your project. The TEST_1 contingency has been assigned to the
   new group LAB.
7. Repeat this process for TEST_2.
