           Lab 7: Remedial Action Scheme Model
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Create a remedial action scheme and its child records
  •   Associate the gate input pin and protective actions to network devices


Task 1: Create a RAS
  1. Create a new Project, name it xxxx_ras and make it your active project.
  2. Open the Remedial Action Scheme (RAS) tree.
  3. Right-click on the existing MRAS and do a deep copy of the RAS
     hierarchy.
  4. Right click the Remedial Action Scheme tab and paste.
  5. This will open up the new RAS tab. Change the EMSName for this RAS to
     Class. Add a description “RAS for the new substation Class”. Change the
     sort order and save your project.
  6. You have created a new RAS.


Task 2: Change the Trigger Condition
  1. Expand for this new RAS Class and find the Gate 1.
  2. In the Gate property sheet, change the gate type from lt(less than) to gt
     (great than), change the threshold value from 29 to 100
  3. Expand the Gate 1 and find the PinFlow
  4. In the PinFlow property sheet, select the Equipment association to be
     ACLineSegment Class_ 2_1 and the terminal to be the Near terminal of
     the ACLineSegment.
  5. In the Trigger Condition, check the Gate(Resulting Gate) association.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     7-26
                                  RAS Modeling


<!-- salto de página -->

                     Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 3: Change the Protective Action.
  1. Expand for this new RAS Class and find the PrivateTrigger TG1.
  2. Delete the existing ProtActEngeryConsumer child record
  3. Under the PrivateTrigger TG1, insert a ProtActSynchronousMachine
  4. In the new ProtActSynchronousMachine property sheet, associate the
     SynchronousMachine to Substation Class G1
  5. In the General property group, specify the ReduceBy Percentage=No,
     action value=20, Is reduce to=No, Enable arming=no, action value from
     SCADA=No


Task 4: Save the changes and run the workspace validation
  1. Save all the changes in the active project.
  2. Run workspace validationFull Validation
  3. Correct any errors if there are any until the workspace is valid


Task 5: Export RASMOM and verify the changes in HDB
(optional)
  1. Export workspace->EMS all
  2. Select SCADAMOM, NETMOM and RASMOM related ones in the
     transformation, load/validation step
  3. When the export finishes, check the RASMOM validation is successful or
     not
  4. If export is successful, check the RASMOM export clone, verify that the
     new RAS and its associated Trigger condition and protective actions are
     exported.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                7-27
                                  RAS Modeling

                             Lab 8: Dynamic Rating Model
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Create the dynamic rating topology based model using autogeneration
  •   Create the static temperature model
  •   Create the schedule limit dependency model


Task 1: Create the dynamic rating topology based model
  1. Create a new Project, name it xxxx_dynrtg and make it your active project.
  2. Use search function to find the ACLineSegment with dynamic rating
     flag=False and have operational limit set defined. Set the dynamic rating
     flag be to True
  3. In the Dynamic Rating table view, bring up the property sheet for the
     DynamicRatingConfiguration. In the General property group, select
     AutoGeneration=Yes
  4. Save the changes and run workspace validationDynamic Rating Model
     Auto Generation
  5. Check the validation messages to see if there are any
     SeriesEquipDependLimit and EquipmentLimitSeriesComponent record.
  6. In the dynamic rating tree view, verify that the ACLineSegment is shown
     up there
  7. Under the ACLineSegment, find the SeriesEquipDependLimit and its
     EquipmentLimitSeiesComp as well as the GeographicalRegion_Resource
  8. Add the WeatherStation_Equipment for the ACLineSegment and its
     associated switches (assuming we are using the existing WeatherStation)
  9. In the Network tree view, find the ACLineSegment related substation
     voltagelevel and bring up the graphic modeler view.
  10. Verify that the EquipmentLimitSeiesComp for that ACLineSegment is
      correct based on the topology.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                   8-32
                            Dynamic Rating Modelling


<!-- salto de página -->

                    Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 2: Create the static temperature model
  1. Find the ACLineSegment 34591 1 in the Dynamic Rating Model tree view.
  2. Deepcopy the three Temperature Depend Limit Tables to paste that under
     the new ACLineSegment participated in the dynamic rating. Note that the
     three TEMPMDL3 need to be deepcopied one buy one.
  3. For the new TEMPMDL3 property sheet, change the Operational limit to
     the Limit1/2/3 for the new ACLineSegment
  4. For the child record TemperatureLimitTablePoint, adjust the LimtValue
  5. Save all the changes to the active project and run workspace validation -
     >Dynamic Rating Validation


Task 3: Create the schedule limit dependency model
  1. Under the new ACLineSegment Dynamic Rating Model tree view, insert a
     ScheduledLimitDepedency. In its property sheet, specify which
     OperationalLimit it is applied to.
  2. Under the ScheduledLimitDepedency, insert the ScheduledLimitValue
  3. In the ScheduledLimitValue, enter the value and select the season Spring
  4. Clone this ScheduleLimitValue three times, and change the value and
     season for Summer, Fall and Winter.
  5. Save all the changes to the active project and run workspace validation -
     >Dynamic Rating Validation

                  Lab 9: Study Other Network Tables
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Create a new BaseVoltage
  •   Add Special Measurements
  •   Add a linkage between a measurement and a special measurement


Task 1: Add Base Voltage
  1. Create a new Project xxxx_Other_tabs (where xxxx is a personal
     identifier), and make it your active project.
  2. Click the Table button in the toolbar.
  3. In the Table Explorer window, expand Network → Network Reference
     Tables → BaseVoltage.
  4. In table BaseVoltage, add a new BaseVoltage record with name 135. Set
     “For Network” to Yes, and set “Nominal Voltage (KV)” to 135.


Task 2: Add Special Measurement
  1. Click the Table button in the toolbar.
  2. In the Table Explorer window, expand SCADA → Measurements/Limits →
     SpecialMeasurement.
  3. In table SpecialMeasurement, add a new SpecialMeasurement record with
     name CLASS.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page              9-13
                              Network Auxiliary Tables

Measurement
  1. Click Linkages icon (    ) in the toolbar, select Network from the drop-
     down list, then select Special Measurement from the Submenu.
  2. In Linkages window, select HEARN substation from the top-left picklist,
     then select Discrete from check boxes.
  3. Click and hold to drag a Measurement from the left to the Linkage cell of
     Special Measurement CLASS to form the Linkage.

                Lab 10: Study Validation and Export
Lab Objectives
  After completing this lab, you will be able to:
  •   Understand Network Model Validation
  •   Generate a netmom case from ETS.


Task 1: Change Substation EMS Name
  1. Create a new Project xxxx_Validation (where xxxx is a personal identifier),
     and make it your active project.
  2. Call up the Network Model tree view.
  3. Expand the tree nodes by clicking the “>” symbol in the following
     sequence: Network Model → NEPOOL → SubGeographical Region →
     EAST → Substation → CLASS.
  4. In the Identification properties of substation CLASS, try to enter
     CLASS_TEST in the “EMS Name” field. Can you enter more than 8
     characters?


Task 2: Change Base Voltage EMS Name
  1. Call up the Table tree view.
  2. Expand the tree nodes in the following sequence: Network → Network
     Reference Tables → BaseVoltage.
  3. Change the Base Voltage 138 EMSName from 138 to 345. Save the
     change you made. What is the pop-up error message?


Task 3: Change the AmpRating for DCConverter
  1. Click the Table button in the toolbar.
  2. In the Table Explorer window, expand Network → Power System
     Equipment →DCConverter.
  3. In the column AmpRating for any DCConverter, change the value to -5.
  4. The box should turn red and there should be an error message. What is
     it?


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                 10-14
                    Network Model Validation and Interface to EMS


<!-- salto de página -->

                     Building a Network Model with e-terrasource


Task 4: Delete Child Record for Line
  1. Click the Network->Network Model in the toolbar.
  2. Locate a line and remove all of its child record.
  3. Save the changes to an active project
  4. Run Workspace Validation>Network Validation. What is the error
     message?


Task 5: Export Netmom Case to EMP
  1. Reset your workspace.
  2. Load the EMP60 MAS v1 into your workspace.
  3. Create a new project xxx_Export.
  4. Navigate to the Substation HEARN and change the EMSName to
     ETSTEST.
  5. Click the export icon from the toolbar, and select Export Workspace.
  6. In the popup window, select EMS Export – Netmom, select the right EMP
     version,then click Finish button to start the export process.
  7. After the export process is successful, use HDBRIO to check there is a
     substation named ETSTEST.

                    Network Model Validation and Interface to EMS

 Soft keys or         Bold formatting is applied to indicate a selectable point.
 buttons on a         For example:
 display
                         Apply


 Physical key on      A box is placed around the text that appears on the
 the keyboard         actual key on the keyboard.
                      For example:
                         Enter

 verbatim by the      monospaced font “Courier New.”
 student, or          For example:
 examples of code
                         Host: PC1392
                         Account: Student1

 <>                   Text enclosed in angle brackets ( < > ) indicates
                      information you must supply.


 []                   Square brackets ( [ ] ) indicate optional qualifiers,

                                                      Network Analysis


                  Applications in the network subsystem

          Network applications using real-time data :
                   − RTNET estimates the real-time network state
                   − RTCA calculates contingent network states
                     w.r.t RTNET solution
                   − RTSENH optimises the real-time network state
                     and the contingent network states with the goal
                     of relieving violations.
                   − VVD optimises the real-time network state
                   − RTSCT analyses the effects of short-circuit faults
                   − OLNETSEQ coordinates the execution of these
                     applications

Network Analysis | Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW | 22


                                 Proprietary – See Copyright Page                                             1-22
                            Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                          Network Analysis


     PWRFLOW features

    Supports a wide variety of problem definitions including diverse voltage
      levels and multiple islands
    Provides load scheduling capability through load profiles and load
      distribution coefficients
    Models regulations :
       − Voltage regulations (AVR) by generators, transformers, circuit
         breaker operation (capacitor/reactor connection status)
       − MW flows regulations by AWR phase shifting transformers
       − AGC model for area interchange control and load + loss coverage
    Provides both standard and expert operator interfaces
    Uses the full Jacobian Newton-Raphson solution method to calculate
      voltages at all buses


     Network Analysis | Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW | 23


Notes:


                                      Proprietary – See Copyright Page         1-23
                                 Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


                      Basic network model ASSUMPTIONS

      • 3-phase balanced system ( implies transposed lines)
      • mutual admittances are negligible (except in SCT)
      • branch equivalent PI model
      • shunt conductances neglected (corona effect negligible)
      • impedances defined at nominal frequency


Network Analysis | Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW | 24


                                 Proprietary – See Copyright Page       1-24
                            Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                          Network Analysis


                  Automatic network functions


          Automatic Voltage Regulation (AVR)
                  − Adjusts unit MVAr outputs, SVS, transformer taps, and capacitor connections
                    to regulate bus voltages.
          Automatic Watt Regulation (AWR)
                  − Adjusts the phase shifter taps to regulate the MW flow through the phase
                    shifters.
                  − Brings net area interchange to schedule through area AGC control.


     Network Analysis | Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW | 25


Notes:


                                      Proprietary – See Copyright Page                         1-25
                                 Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                          Network Analysis


     Automatic network functions : Voltage regulation

     Automatic Voltage Regulation (AVR)
           − Regulates bus voltage by adjusting :                                       MVAr
                  • unit MVAr output
                  • SVS MVAr output                                               G               G
                                                                                        G   G
                  • transformer tap positions
                                                                             Bank regulation by units :
                  • capacitor / reactor connections                          MVAr need is shared in proportion
           − Priority by type (1, 2, 3, 4)                                   of remaining MVAr capability
           − Priority can be overridden by component

           − Bank regulation by transformers :
                  • master / follower
                  • current balancing flag

     Regulation is abandoned when regulating variable reaches limit
     Network Analysis | Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW | 26


Notes:


                                      Proprietary – See Copyright Page                                 1-26
                                 Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                          Network Analysis


    Automatic network functions : MW regulation

   Automatic Watt flow Regulation (AWR)
       − Adjusts the phase shifter taps to regulate the MW flow through the phase
         shifters
       − Regulation is abandoned when regulating variable reaches limit
   Area interchange control and load + loss coverage
       − Area interchange :
            Sum of tie MW flows = scheduled net interchange
       − Area balance equation :
            GENERATION + IMPORT = LOAD + LOSSES + EXPORT
       − Adjusts MW generations through model of area AGC :
           • Single slack bus Î multiple slack generators
           • base generation + participation factors

         − Area in which MW balance cannot be established is DEAD
         − Interchange is not regulated in areas split by islanding
         − One angular reference per island

                                                     Network Analysis


               Bus load model

  Specifies where, when, and how much power is
    extracted from the network
  Distributes system MW load onto bus loads
                                                                                              PL + j QL
          − Bus load = baseload + fraction of (system
            load)
          − “fraction” parameters (distribution factors) are
            updated by an adaptive algorithm using “observation
            points” provided by each run of the state estimator

  A more complex hierarchical model of bus loads can
    be setup. For example :
          − System load
                  • Geographical area load (East, West, ...)
                          − Sectoral subdivision (residential, industrial, commercial, ...)
                                   • Bus loads

                                                     Network Analysis


                 Summary of MW load model characteristics


     Time dependence only at LDAREA level
            − Thus, load profiles can only be defined at this level
            − Avoid too many hierarchical levels (multiplying profiles)
   Magnitude of base portions are not proportional to the parent area
    load
   Base portion of loads can corrupt the load distribution mechanism if
     not consistent upwards
            − Group all bases of similar behavior together in a loadarea with the
              desired profile (schedule)
   Base portions of loads are not updated by RTNET

<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


                         Time dependence of loads

              Week subdivision into WEEK SEGMENTS
                     − From SUN                00:00               to   MON   12:00   Day seg : WE
                     −    From MON             12:00               to   FRI   12:00   Day seg : WRK
                     −    From FRI             12:00               to   FRI   24:00   Day seg : FRI
                     −    From SAT             00:00               to   SAT   24:00   Day seg : WE

              Day subdivision into a set of DAY SEGMENTS
                     − WE day segments :
                           • 00:00 - 08:00 - 09:00 - 11:00 - 17:00 - 19:00 - 23:00
              A set of day segments is assigned to each week segment
              Day segments repeat themselves within the same week
                segment
              Load characteristics are constant within a day segment

                                 Network Analysis


            Lab: Evaluating a Network State Using
                                      PWRFLOW
Objectives
     This module discusses the features and uses of PWRFLOW, and reviews
     how PWRFLOW models network behavior.
        •    PWRFLOW overview
        •    Setting up the input data
        •    Running a powerflow solution
        •    Viewing and changing the network state
     In this lab, you will use the PWRFLOW application to evaluate a network
     state before and after a line outage.
     Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to:
        •    Install your PWRFLOW clone
        •    Initialize PWRFLOW with data.
        •    Run a powerflow study and view the results.
        •    Create a savecase of the powerflow results.


Task 1: Initialize PWRFLOW with Data
     You can retrieve data into pwrflow in several ways :
        •    Via the Data Retrieval popup when importing data from another
             application
        •    Via the Savecase Directory display when retrieving PWRFLOW
             savecases.
     You will use this last method to retrieve this PWRFLOW savecase :
        •    the TRAIN_NET_FEATURES savecase of the NETMOM type
     Proceed as follows :
     1. Call up the Powerflow Study display ; this is the master display of the
        PWRFLOW application in study mode.
     2. Select the     Data Retrieval       button.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                 1-62
                     Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW


<!-- salto de página -->

                                 Network Analysis


     3. Notice that buttons with black text lead you to another display and that
        buttons with red text command a task to execute.
     4. Select the     Savecase Directory           button
     5. Look in the list of PWRFLOW savecases for the desired type with the
        desired title.
     6. Retrieve the desired savecases using the provided facility (Right click
        on the savecase name and select “Retrieve”).
     7. Use the Previous Display command to get back to the PWRFLOW
        master display.
     Note: Examine the Network Copy Uti lity that supports the second
     method        of initializing      PWRFLOW             with data :
     click on th e     Data Retrieval…   button. This will popup a dialog box
     (Network Copy Utility) that allows you to command network data to be
     copied to y our PWRFLOW clone, eit her by direct database copy (Copy
     Clone …) or by savecase retrieval (Retrieve Case…).


Task 2: Run a power flow study ( = solve the power flow)
     1. Call up the Powerflow Study display.
     2. Select the Start Process button to activate PWRFLOW. Note that the
        Process Status changes from DOWN to ACTIVE.
     3. What is the load of the ESKOM area ? ………………… MW
     4. Select the    Run Powerflow Solution         button to solve the power
        flow.


Task 3: Review the Network State
     1. Use the Island Summary display to see the general balance of the
        network :
        Generation           = …………….. MW
        Load         =         …………….. MW
        Loss         =         …………….. MW
     2. Use the Area and Company Summary display, Company Summary
        view, to examine the generation, load, and losses for the internal
        company and divisions.


                          Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       1-63
                     Evaluating a Network State using PWRFLOW

                               Network Analysis


AREA, Company &      GENERATION                   LOAD         LOSSES
 Divisions Names
                    MW        MVAr        MW         MVAr     MW      MVAr


     3. Use the Bus Summary display, Bus Symbolic view, to examine the
        generation and load data for a selected station (say KARIBA SOUTH
        – KAR11013).
     4. Station Name: …………………………………..
        Generation : ………………… MW and ……………… MVAr
        Load data : ………………… MW and ……………….. MVAr.
     5. Use the Bus Summary display, Bus Symbolic view, to examine the
        line flows for a selected line (Say one of the line from ALA11023 to
        KAR11013)
     6. Line name: ……………………….
        Line flows : …………………… MW and ………………..MVAr.
     7. Use the To Station … button to navigate to the other end of the
        line;
        Note the flow values : ……………… MW and …………..MVAr.
     8. Calculate the line losses : …………… MW and …………..MVAr.
     9. Use the To Station … button to come back.

         Note the flow value : ……………… MW and …………..MVAr,

         Line losses : …………… MW.

Task 4: Save power flow results (optional)
     1. Call up the Powerflow Study display.
     2. Enter a description in the Network Data Description field ( this is
        usually to identify your modifications…)
     3. Select the Data Retrieval button.
     4. Select the Savecase Directory button.
     5. Enter a NETMOM savecase title (TRAIN_BASE_your initials) in the
        entry box above on the right of the window. Select the
         Save button next to NETMOM. test
     6. Observe the list of savecase now includes your savecase.
     7. Delete this savecase. (Right click on the savecase name and select
        delete).


Task 5: Modify the network topology and run PWRFLOW
     In this lab, you will disconnect a line, and observe the effect on power
     flows.
        •   Line name (say one of the line between ALA11023 and KAR11013
            but not the previous one):……………………….
     You can disconnect a line by using the “Remove/Restore” features of
     lines.
     1. Call up the Bus Summary Display.
     2. Disconnect the chosen line by using the “REMOVE” facility in the Bus
        Symbolic display from either one of the 2 substations.
     3. Notice the R at the line connection point in each substation.
     4. Solve the power flow.
        Notice that a symbolic switch opens when solving the power flow in the
        Bus Symbolic display, but the switch position on the Breaker
        Summary display is not modified. Notice also that line flows are zero.
     5. Repeat the line reconnection by using the “RESTORE” facility for the
        line in the Network bus summary display .
     6. Solve the power flow.
     Note: You also can remove the line from the Network Line/Transformer
     Summary Display by ticking the remove flag.

     Component displays those Summary displays that you have not used

        •   Identify which generators regulate voltage (V in the circle)
        •   Click on the information symbol near the station name to see
            station details.
        •   Etc.
     Many of these displays are also used for the other network applications.

                                                        Network Analysis


      Violation reporting in case of multiple limits

           Multiple voltage limits can apply at a bus if it contains nodes
             for which separate limits have been defined (NDLIM
             records have been inserted for some of these nodes)
           NON-default assigned limits will be reported separately
                   − For defined NDLIM limits where they exist
                   − For VLIM limits at other nodes
           Default assigned limits will be reported separately except if
             limits are the same

                         Alarm and warning tolerances

                                                                                      Alarm exists


                           Alarm limit RV * AT                                                         Violation exists
Rated value = RV
(Nominal limit)                                                         RV * AT* DT
Warning limit RV * WT
                                                                                 Return from violation limit
                                                                                 RV * DT

                                                            Warning exists                           RV * WT * D

          AT = alarming tolerance                                    = 1.08
          WT = warning tolerance                                     = 0.96
          DT = deadband tolerance                                    = 0.90 ( applies to each effective limit )

          Voltage drop = V0-Vi ( ignored if negative ; treated just as any other upper limit )

       Lab 1: Monitoring Limit Violations using
                                    PWRFLOW
Objectives
     This module reviews EMP facilities to monitor variables of the power
     flow solution (the network state) and compare these variables to their
     limits using PWRFLOW. This includes :
        •    Specify the monitored elements (that is : the components and the
             types of limit to be monitored)
        •    Get familiar with the concept of monitored group and observe how
             monitored elements are assigned to monitored groups
        •    Modify monitored group parameters
        •    View network state violations
     Students will also observe how voltage limits are specified globally for
     each voltage level in a company/division (by Voltage Limit Sets) and gain
     an understanding as to how components are assigned to Voltage Limit
     Sets.
     In this lab, you will use the PWRFLOW application to monitor limit
     violations in the network state.
     Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to :
        •    Control system monitoring from the monitored group level
        •    Use PWRFLOW to perform system state monitoring

     you would need to retrieve the savecase that you made in the previous
     lab. This is how you would proceed if necessary:

     4. Use the retrieval option part of the popup to retrieve directly the
        training savecase (retrieve case from application “ PWRFLOW” ,
        casetype “ NETMOM” , title “ TRAIN_NET_FEATURES)

 Lab 2: Controlling Voltage using PWRFLOW
                                   (Optional)
Objectives
     This optional module reviews the PWRFLOW capabilities of controlling
     voltages using generating units or transformer taps.
     Students will learn how voltage targets can be specified.
     They will observe how PWRFLOW recognizes the impossibility to continue
     regulating the voltage when the controller reaches a limit.


     In this lab, you will use the voltage regulation features of PWRFLOW to
     modify the voltage profile in the network.
     You will also understand that PWRFLOW abandons regulation when the
     regulating variable is pushed to one of its limits.


Task 1: Modify the Voltage Regulated by a Unit
     1. Using the Unit Summary display, MVAr and Voltage Regulation Data
        view, locate a generating unit

     6. Enter a higher voltage set-point : 1.040 perunit
     7. Set the regulation tolerance (acceptable deviation) to 0.002 perunit
     8. Solve the power flow
     9. Check whether the unit still regulates voltage : YES or NO
     10. Note the MVAr generation value : ………………. MVAr, and the upper
         limit : ……………. MVAr

      Powerflow Options –
      Problem Definition Options (1)


          Load Dist:
                   − NORMAL: The load calculation will use the base and parent
                     fraction values specified in the network load model.

                   − RTNET: The load calculation will be initialized with load data from
                     the latest successful RTNET solution. This usually generates new
                     parent fractions, internal loadarea scaling factors, and load
                     schedule adjustments.

                                                  Network Analysis


                       Basic network model ASSUMPTIONS

      3-phase balanced system ( implies transposed lines)
      mutual admittances are negligible (except in SCT)
      branch equivalent PI model
      shunt conductances neglected (corona effect negligible)
      impedances defined at nominal frequency

             Line flow equations


          Since                                   93 Ikm = Vk BSkm          + ( Vk − Vm ) / Z

          the total power into branch km is :

                            Skm                   = 3 Uk I*km = 93 Vk I*km

                                                  = V2k BS*km + Vk( Vk − Vm )* / Z*


          This shows that the total 3-phase power is
          calculated with phase-to-phase voltage and the
          admittances of one phase of the line.

                                                   Network Analysis


Contingency Analysis features

          Flexible contingency definition :
               − defined by selecting components in a software prepared list
               − any combination of component outages and breaker switching is
                  allowed
               − any bus structure allowed
          Very fast solution :
              − Contingency screening
              − Well-developed power flow algorithms for :
                    • ultra-fast approximate solution ( for contingency screening )
                    • full accurate power flow solution (DPF or NPF) for definite
                      assessment
          Accurate modeling of the power system behavior:
              − Automatic controller response modeling
              − Conditional contingencies for simple relay modeling

                                                   Network Analysis


Conditional contingency

              Primary contingency (standard)
              Condition:
                       − specify a component (node or branch)
                       − Specify the condition:
                                • Node voltage > or < some threshold
                                • Branch flow > some threshold
              If condition is true in the result of primary contingency,
                  implement a secondary contingency
              Report violation only if some exists in the result of the
                secondary contingency
              Report if condition was true

                                           Contingency Analysis (CA)


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                   Network Analysis


CA : Specifying
       contingency ranking parameters
   Contingencies are ranked in screening phase based on :
            − The magnitude of violations they cause
            − The level of limit being violated ( 1 2 3 )
   A ranking number is calculated for each type of violation :
                   RANK = (level violated) * WT1 + (percent violation) * WT2
                   user specified


                   • WT1 : Weighting of violated level in contingency ranking
                   • WT2 : Weighting of violated percentage in contingency ranking

                  user specified


Network Analysis | Contingency Analysis (CA) | 9


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page            2-9
                                           Contingency Analysis (CA)


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


        CA : Contingency selection parameters

Selection uses the contingency severity rank:
       −    User specifies the max number of potentially
            harmful contingencies to be retained for full
            analysis
       −    Separately by constraint violation type : N1
            N2 N3 N4
Selection also uses the contingency occurrence
probability:
       −    Low probability = probability < 0.5
       −    User specifies the maximum number of low
            probability contingencies to be retained for full
            analysis
       −    Separately by constraint violation type : P1

Task 3: Define a New Contingency
     1. If necessary, select the Start Process                       button in Contingency
        Analysis Study Main Display.
     2. Call up the Contingency Definition display.
     3. Click on the Reset Work Area button to prepare for a new
        contingency definition
     4. Enter a contingency identifier (for instance LG01) in the Define/Update
        Contingency field provided near the directory symbol.
     5. Select the Define New Contingency button.
     6. Select the Outage Selections button to navigate to the list of
        components that can be part of a CTG definition
     7. Select a primary component to be outaged for this contingency (for
        instance a generator): Click in the Select column on the button next to
        the component that you want to outage in the contingency.
     8. Repeat the above step to select other components if desired (for
        instance a Load).
     9. Select the Return to Definition Work Area button to return to the
        Contingency Definition display.
     10. Select the Save/Update Outage Selections button.
         Observe that your selections of primary components are shown in the
         lower part of the display.
     11. Enter text into the Contingency Description field.
     12. Enter other parameters as appropriate:
         - For instance, you would force the Process Type to be WIDE
         screening for this significant disturbance
         - You can also specify a probability of occurrence (the contingency will
         be declared high probability if the probability that you specify exceeds
         the low probability threshold (0.5)). As an Engineer/Analyst, you
         specify in the CA Analysis Control display how many low probability
         contingencies can be retained for full analysis.
         - You can also specify a maximum amount of load and generation in
         MW that the contingency could disconnect without declaring it harmful
         (if the contingency does not cause any violation, of course).
     13. Validate your entries
     14. Select the Save/Update Outage Selections button.
     Notice that your contingency has been recorded in the directory, but it is
     not active because ....................................……….....................
     ......................................................................................................

Task 4: Assign the Contingency to a Contingency Group
     1. Call up the Group Definition view of the Contingency Definition
        display.
     2. Select the directory symbol.
     3. Select the contingency group button you want (for instance : LINE).
     4. Right click on the +/- button next to an existing CTGGRP record and
        select Insert Contingencies in Group on the pull-down menu.
     5. Enter the ID of the contingency you want in the contingency group (for
        instance : LG01).
     6. Validate your definitions. This will check your definitions, insert the
        contingency in the selected group, display the contingency description,
        and update its activation status (check it in the contingency directory;
        refresh the display if necessary).


Task 5: Create a New Contingency Group and Assign a
Contingency to that Group
     1. Call up the Group Definition view of the Contingency Definition display.
     2. Click on the directory symbol to see the list of groups and select one of
        them. Your new contingency group will be inserted after the group that
        you have selected.
     3. Right click on the +/- button next to the CONGRP record of the group
        that you have selected and select Insert Contingency Group on the
        pull-down menu. This will insert a new contingency group after the one
        you selected.
     4. Scroll down until you find this new contingency group
     5. Enter the ID of the contingency group you want to create
        (for instance: LAB). Validate.
     6. Insert the contingency you want in the contingency group
        (for instance: LG01).
        Validate; notice the appearance of the CTG name along with the CTG
        description and Process Type.
     7. Activate whatever should be active and validate to make the
        contingency active.
     8. Notice the check mark for this active status.
     9. Verify in the Contingency directory that LG01 is now active.

RAS / RAP Overview

What are RAS/RAP?
       − These are a set of protection schemes to implement in order to
         prevent overloads or loss of equipment.
       − These schemes are either:
                • RAS (Remedial Action Schemes): Automatic actions taken in the field
                • RAP (Remedial Action Plans): Preventative actions executed manually
Why simulate these Schemes in Network Applications?
       − Allows the user to verify the effectiveness of RAS/RAP schemes
         using a study power flow
       − More accurate results from Contingency Analysis, VSAT, and TSAT
         when they model RAS/RAP
       − DTS Events can benefit by importing these schemes
       − Market impacts (SFT & identifying valid constraints)

RAS / RAP Triggering Conditions


Triggering conditions involve testing boolean combinations of the
   following:
    − Switching device status (open/closed)
    − Branch energization (either end of branch open or both ends
       opened)
    − Path flow (a set of branches defined as an interface in
       NETMOM)
    − Branch flow
    − Node voltage
    − Flow on DC Line
    − SCADA Analog & point (arming status)
    − Reactive Reserve

                                                  Network Analysis


Multithread Contingency Analysis


• CA is resource-consuming application by nature
       − Network models getting larger and larger
       − Number of contingencies growing
       − Power flow computation needed
• Good Candidate for Parallel Processing
       − Distribute contingencies to computational threads
• Multi core CPU widely available
• Multi Thread vs. Multi Process
       − Ease of configuration
       − Optimized overhead distribution cost (no data transfer)
       − Easy support of conventional Hot/Standby configuration

Contingency Analysis with Newton Powerflow


•       Features Of CA Newton PF
           − Solves Newton PWRFLOW (NPF) for basecase / contingencies if DPF fails to converge. The
             switch to NPF from DPF is automatic.
           − Ability to force Newton PWRFLOW without attempting DPF first for basecase /
             contingencies.
           − NPF used only for CA full processing. Screening still employs single iteration methods with
             decoupled matrices.
           − Minimal UI changes - software auto converts NPF iterations to DPF iterations for display on
             the standard Contingency Iteration displays.

        threads?

                    Lab: CA using Newton Powerflow
Objectives
     In this lab, you will configure Contingency Analysis in study mode to run
     using Newton Powerflow
     Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to:
        •    Specify CA to run with Newton Powerflow
        •    Examine CA results to determine contingencies are processed
             using Newton Powerflow.
     For this lab, you will need a clone of the STCA application.


Task 1: Configure CA to Run with Newton Powerflow
     1. Call up the Contingency Analysis Study display.
     2. Start the process
     3. Call up the Decoupled Powerflow Analyst Parameters display and
        navigate to the DPF Solution Flags tab.
     4. Check the options to Enable Newton PF and Force Newton PF for
        CTG.
     5. Go back to the Contingency Analysis Study display and run CA.


Task 2: Review Contingency Analysis Results
     1. Call up the Contingency Solution Results display (Result Summary
        view) to see, by the # symbol, which contingencies were solved with
        Newton Powerflow.
     2. Go back to the Contingency Solution Iterations display to verify the
        iterations are marked with “N” for the contingencies.

                                                        Network Analysis


                  State estimation


       Purpose
                − Use real-time measurements (analog & status) to maintain a comprehensive and
                      consistent description of the current state of the network:
                         • topological state (connectivity / energization)
                         • electrical state (voltages, taps -> power flows)
                − Warn about constraint violations:
                         • voltage limits
                         • branch limits
                         • interface limits
                         • node-pair limits
                − Monitor the reactive reserve by zone and by company
                − Help to:
                                  •    maintain the measurement system
                                  •    detect modeling errors

                                        Proprietary – See Copyright Page                         3-2
                                      Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                        Network Analysis


RTNET functions

           Determine the network state given :
                    − the network model (equations and parameters)
                    − the network topology (derived from status measurements)
                    − available analog measurements
                    − models of load and generation bus injections
           Inform about possible violations of operating constraints
           Identify anomalous measurements
           Calculate measurement error statistics
           Identify modeling errors
           Improve modeled information
           Calculate loss sensitivities

                                                        Network Analysis


State Estimator variables

    State vector X
             − State variables [X] consist of a subset of the variables
               characterizing the electrical state of the power system.
               They are explicitly solved by the state estimation algorithm.
               Basically, X = complex voltage vector.
             − The remainder of the power system variables are deterministically
               dependent on the state variables :
                           Y = h (X)
               Basically, Y = complex power flows.
    Measurement vector Y
             − Bus voltage magnitudes
             − MW and MVAr flows in lines, transformers, and bus injections
             − Transformer tap positions

                                   Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features

                                                        Network Analysis


State Estimator variables (Cont.)


             Other variables or parameters in RTNET not related to the
               current electrical state of the system :
                      − Measurement bias and standard deviation
                      − Measurement weights which reflect the level of
                        uncertainty we want to associate with each measurement

                                                        Network Analysis


State Estimator equations

     Bus balance equations (First Kirchhoff law):
              − Require the sums of real power flows and reactive power flows
                into a bus to be zero.
              − Zero injection bus equations are associated with relatively high
                levels of confidence (low uncertainty).
     Measurement equations relate a measurement to :
              − either directly a solution variable (voltage magnitude)
              − or an implicit value calculated from solution variables (power
                flows)
     Network parameter equations in which uncertainty is associated
       with a network component parameter rather than a network
       variable
       (example : tap positions as variables instead of parameters).

                                                        Network Analysis


Least Squares State Estimation

          zThe measurement equations are :

                                            Y = h(X) + V
                   where                    X = column-vector of state variables
                                            Y = column-vector of measurements
                                            V = column-vector of measurement errors
                                                (zero mean, uncorrelated, gaussian)

          z This is an over-determined powerflow problem
                   Î using the information from M independent measurements
                           Y = { yj }
                   Î to solve for N unknowns (state X or solution variables),

                   Î where M is greater than N ( M-N = degree of freedom )


Network Analysis | Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features | 7


                                     Proprietary – See Copyright Page                 3-7
                                   Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features

                             Network Analysis


Weighted Least Squares (WLS )

The best estimate of the state variables X is obtained by the Weighted
   Least Squares (WLS) method. The objective is to minimize the sum of the
   squares of the weighted deviations of the estimated measurements from
   the actual measurements:

        Min J(X) = Sumj { [ yj - hj(X) ] / σj }2

   σ reflects the measurement uncertainty
    The value of J is called the “cost” of the solution.
In matrix notation,
                  J(X) = [y-h(X)]T W-1 [y-h(X)]
     W is the covariance matrix of measurement errors, which reflects
     the measurement confidence. In the case of independent
     measurement errors, W-1 is diagonal with
                                                    w|jj8 = 1/σj2
Network Analysis | Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features


                    Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     3-8
                  Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                        Network Analysis


                                      Weighted Least Squares (WLS )

                                 J(X) = [y-h(X)]T W-1 [y-h(X)]
Minimization of the cost is achieved by solving:
                  ∂J(X) / ∂X = 0
Since J(X) is non-linear, the solution is obtained iteratively.
The method uses the Taylor’s series expansion for the function h:
                                   h(Xk+1) = h(Xk) + H(Xk) ΔX
     with H : Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives of h wrt X,
        Xk : estimate of X at iteration k,
At each iteration k:
                                 [ HT W-1 H ] ΔXk = HT W-1 [Y- h(Xk)]

                 ΔX = Xk+1 - Xk = [ HT W-1 H ]-1 HT W-1 [ Y - h(Xk) ]
Network Analysis | Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features | 9


                                     Proprietary – See Copyright Page      3-9
                                   Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                        Network Analysis


                                       WLS iteration types

                                                               Normal
                                                                           RHS
                                                               matrix
                       Xk+1 - Xk = [ HT W-1 H ]-1 HT W-1 [ Y-h(Xk) ]

            X FACTOR :
              Full rebuild of all matrices and factorization of the normal matrix
              with optimal reordering ( in case of topology change or change
              in the set of available measurements )
            X REFACTOR :
              Same without revising the factorization order
            X REPEAT :
              Recalculate only the RHS and use the same normal matrix
              inverse to update X
            X RHS :
              Repeat with updated W for de/re-weightings

Estimating injection components

                                                                           Gmeas=100 ; sigma2=0.3


                                                               Est =38
                                                                                      Est =53
Branch flow estimates yield net injection estimate
     − NIest = 38 + 53 = 91
                                                                           Dmeas=12 ; sigma2=1
Measured net injection = 100 – 12 = 88

Measurement error = 91 – 88 = +3 Î injection component estimates must be further apart than
  measured values

Allocate correction to injection component in proportion of their variances :
      − Gest = Gmeas + 3 * (0.3 / 0.3 + 1) = 100 + 0.69 = 100.69
      − Dest = Dmeas - 3 * (1 / 0.3 + 1) = 12 – 2.31 = 9.69
In this process, pseudo-measurements and their variances are used in case of lacking measurement(s)

                                                        Network Analysis


          Measurement weights : accuracy classes


       The sigma value is based upon :
                − engineering judgment, or
                − any other available information on the possible values of the
                  errors [v] under normal conditions (for instance : instrument
                  precision ratings and branch parameters accuracy).
       RTNET uses uncertainty models to determine the relative accuracy of the
          measurements:
                − An accuracy class is assigned to every measurement
                − Accuracy classes contain parameters that allow RTNET to
                  calculate the standard deviation “sigma” for each
                  measurement
       RTNET uses the measurement standard deviation SIGMAj to calculate the
          measurement weight wjj.

     Measurement-Observable (or strictly speaking : “observable”)
            Portions of the network where RTNET can estimate the state using only actual
            measurements.
     Observable (or strictly speaking : “solvable”)
            Portions of the network where RTNET can calculate the state using available
            measurements, complemented by pseudo-measurements (based on modeled
            information).

                                                        Network Analysis


RTNET : Network observability

       The network observability function determines which state variables, and
          which measurements (and the associated equations) will constitute the
          state estimation problem formulation.
       The availability of usable measurement from SCADA and model injection
          information determines which equations can be used.
       The determination of the extent of “measurement observability” itself is
          based directly on two basic rules which are repetitively applied:
           − A branch flow is “known” if the buses at each end are in the same
              observability island.
           − If all “unknown” branches incident to a measured injection bus
              terminate in observability island X, then the injection bus is also in
              observability island X.
           − In addition, there must be a least one known voltage magnitude in
              an observability island in order for it to be observable.


Network Analysis | Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features | 15


                                     Proprietary – See Copyright Page                  3-15
                                   Real Time Network (RTNET) - Features


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                        Network Analysis


        RTNET : unified solution
                for observable and unobservable

           Pseudo-measurements are used to complement actual measurements in
              order to allow full network solution
           Pseudo-measurements are generated from :
              − MW generation from economic dispatch / commitment
              − MVAr generation from voltage regulation schedules
              − MW / MVAr load models and schedules (updated from past
                records)
           Above information translates into a single type of pseudo-
              measurement: unit and load injections
           Measurement vector Y is extended to include minimal number of
             pseudo-measurements
           Pseudo-measurements are given greater uncertainty than actual
              measurements

                                                             Network Analysis


     RTNET’s checks on input data

                 SCADA performs a quality check before passing data to
                   RTNET
                 RTNET uses SCADA’s quality evaluation to determine
                   whether or not to use the data
                 RTNET performs elementary coherency checks to ignore
                   measurements in gross error :
                         − voltage on de-energized nodes
                         − flows across open switches
                         − Flows exceeding a multiple of the branch limit
                         − MW or MVAr generator flows exceeding the MVA rating of
                           the unit
                         − MW or MVAr loads exceeding the load limits
                         − Measurements outside reasonability limits

                                                             Network Analysis


     Accuracy classes

         An accuracy class specifies the magnitude of possible errors in a
           given type of input data :
                 − Acquisition system accuracy = errors in measurement equipment
                   chain :
                          • Potential transformer (PT)
                          • Current transformer (CT)
                          • Transducer
                          • Analog to digital converter
                 − Modeled data accuracy (for pseudo-measurements):
                          • uncertainty on load model
                          • uncertainty on regulation targets, cost functions, limits
         Accuracy must reflect indirect uncertainty:
                 − line, and transformer parameters
                 − switch positions ( topology )
                 − non-coincidence of the measurements
     Network Analysis | Obtaining a Network Solution with RTNET | 24


Notes:


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page               3-24
                                      Obtaining a Network Solution with RTNET


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                        Network Analysis


Accuracy classes : parameters

 SIGMA is derived from :
     − Maximum error (in percent of BASE) for :
                            − potential transformer
                            − current transformer
                            − transducer
                            − analog-to-digital converter
                   • Total max error percentage = sum of the above
          − User specifies for each class the number “n’ of SIGMAs corresponding to
            the maximum error ( usually : n = 3 )
          − SIGMA = [ max_error_percentage * BASE / 100 ] / n
          − BASE =
                   • MVA capacity of branch / unit for MW and MVAr measurements
                   • 100 for zero injection buses and the bus balance equation (KCL)
                   • (Base + Fraction) for load measurements
                   • Voltage base for voltage measurements
 User can specify an additional STDV to be added to SIGMA

                                                                Network Analysis


     RTNET’s state estimate is not the true state

                 RTNET estimates the network state based on the following :
                    − field data from SCADA (measurements)
                    − injections pseudo-measurements derived from the network
                       model for those portions of the network where measurements
                       are not available
                    − bus constraints (Kirchhoff’s power balance equation)

                 RTNET’s state solution is an estimate of the network state, not the actual
                   true state (always unknown)
                    − the network model is not an exact reproduction of the actual
                       system
                    − measurements provide redundant but possibly inconsistent
                       values
                    − measurements are collected for only parts of the modeled
                       network


     Network Analysis | RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis | 38


Notes:


                                      Proprietary – See Copyright Page                    3-38
                                RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                           Network Analysis


State estimation ASSUMPTIONS (1)


     Basic network model assumptions
         − 3-phase balanced system
         − mutual admittances are negligible (except in SCT)
         − branch equivalent PI model
         − shunt conductances neglected (corona effect negligible )
         − impedances defined at nominal frequency
     Specific assumptions for the state estimator : correct impedances
         − correct topology
         − correct line parameters R, X, BCH
         − correct transformer models:
               • Losses (iron, copper)
               • Magnetization susceptance
               • Saturation
               • Tap:
                   − position
                   − model (sign, step, impedance effect)
Network Analysis | RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis | 39


                                 Proprietary – See Copyright Page             3-39
                           RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                           Network Analysis


State estimation ASSUMPTIONS (2)

            Special assumptions for measurements:
                − correct measurement location (point-to-point tests)
                − no bias
                − correct weight ( = correct measurement error variance)
                − uncorrelated ( = no covariances)
            Special assumptions for pseudo-measurements:
                − Adequate load model
                − Adequate model of MW generation:
                     • generation cost
                     • generation limits
                     • interchanges
                − Adequate model of voltage regulation:
                     • voltage targets
                     • limits to voltage regulation device
                − Adequate weight ( = uncertainty)
Network Analysis | RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis | 40

                           RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                                Network Analysis


     Error detection


     Error detection
         − Based on CHI-square test:
              • the solution cost “J” follows a CHI-square distribution with M-N
                 degrees of freedom
                 ( M-N = number of measurements – number of state variables).
              • J will be larger than expected in the presence of bad measurement
                 data
     Error identification
         − Based on equation residuals evaluated at the calculated network state:
               • Residual = estimated value - measured value
               • Large residuals generally indicate that the associated measurement
                 (or bus equation) is grossly in error or anomalous


     Network Analysis | RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis | 41

                                      Proprietary – See Copyright Page              3-41
                                RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                           Network Analysis


Error processing with weight changes


            Error processing
                      − Analyze individual equation residual whose value is larger than
                        expected and propose weight adjustment to reduce the influence of
                        those measurements upon the solution
                      − Perform sensitivity analysis of equation residuals to the proposed
                        weight adjustments
                      − Select and implement weight changes
                      − Re-solve WLS to obtain new state solution
                      − Check total cost and equation residuals again:
                          • If acceptable, solution is valid
                          • If not, repeat error processing and weight change steps

     Causes of poor estimate quality

                   Topology / model errors in the vicinity of the problem :

                   Error smearing from analog errors

Task 3: View State Estimator Residuals and Mismatches
     Reminder and terminology clarification :
        •   Mismatch = violation of the first Kirchhoff law when calculating the
            network flows from the considered voltage vector = balance of the
            power flows at a bus. This balance is zero for an exact network
            solution (satisfying exactly the 2 Kirchhoff laws). Any network
            solution in which the maximum mismatch is less than a user-
            specified tolerance is considered valid. The mismatch is a power
            flow concept.


                        Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       3-63
                  RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                             Network Analysis


   •   Residual = difference between a measured value and the
       corresponding estimated value. The residual is a state estimation
       concept.
   •   In principle, the state estimator does not know the concept of
       mismatch. Indeed :
       -   The primary result of the state estimator algorithm is the
           estimate of the voltage vector.
       -   This voltage estimate is used to calculate the estimate of line
           flows.
       -   These line flow estimates allow to calculate the net injection
           estimate at each bus as the balance of line flows.
       -   The difference between the net injection estimate and the
           measured net injection is distributed over the injection
           components (generation and load) in proportion of their
           variances by pushing them further away from each other or
           closer to each other until obtaining a net injection equal to the
           estimated net injection (note that in this process, the model
           value is used in absence of measured value)
       -   With this procedure, the state estimator solution never shows
           any bus mismatch.
       -   There are however 2 exceptions :
            In case this procedure yields a generation estimate outside
              the generation limits, the estimated generation is moved to
              the violated limit
            In case this procedure yields a load estimate outside the
              load limits, the estimated load is moved to the violated limit
       -   Both corrections will generate a mismatch that will be listed to
           draw the user attention on the problem.
1. Call up the Bus Mismatch view of the Real Time Network Solution
   Analysis display. Observe the tolerance. Note whether there are bus
   mismatches exceeding the tolerance :
   ……………………………………………………………………
   ……………………..…………………………………………....
   The existence of excessive mismatch is an indication that some of the
   input data still show some inconsistency.
2. Look at the Measurement Mismatch display to see Measurement
   Mismatches in excess of some threshold. Measurement mismatch
   can be calculated when all injection components are measured. Note
   that for the measurement mismatch calculation , if a branch
   measurement is not available at the near end of the branch, the far
   end measurement (if available) will be used. Observe the mismatch
   tolerances. Reduce the mismatch tolerances to 1.0 and run the online

                    Proprietary – See Copyright Page                        3-64
              RTNET Solution Quality Evaluation Error Analysis


<!-- salto de página -->

                                 Network Analysis


        network sequence. Observe the list of excessive measurement
        mismatches.
     3. Look at the Solution Quality view of the Solution Quality Report
        display in order to see global quality indices by company.
        In this display, “error” designates the sum of absolute residuals.
        In this display, “deviation” designates the standard deviation of

     4. Look at the Company Injection Standard Deviation view of the

Task 6: Tap Estimation
     In this part of the lab you will run RTNET to perform transformer tap
     estimation. You will first disable a tap measurement from being used by
     the state estimator. You will then change the tap position in the simulator,
     and ask the state estimator to estimate the new tap position.
     1. Bring up the Network Online Sequence display in one viewport.
     2. Find a transformer that can be tap estimated and with tap
        measurements. For being able to be tap estimated, a transformer
        should have its 2 terminals in the same observability island and
        redundant flow measurements, or voltage measurements on both the
        high and low sides of the transformer. Use for instance transformer
        T1 at the CEYLON substation which meets these conditions.
     3. Call up the Telemetered Network Data display at CEYLON. Note
        that the SCADA tap and the estimated tap are the same (i.e. tap Xo
        = 3.). The measured value is used as long as it is valid and enabled,
        and tap estimation is not requested.
     4. Disable the SCADA tap measurement for transformer T1 from being
        used in RTNET.
     5. Taking the position of the training instructor playing the role of the
        CEYLON substation operator, you will change the tap position for
        T1 as follows : call up of the Line/Transformer Summary display
        (Transformers view) in the simulation subsystem. Find station
        CEYLON and change transformer T1 from tap Xo to tap X’ = Xo+2
        = 3 + 2 = 5. Notice the change in transformer MVAr flows.
        Notice also on the SCADA substation oneline or tabular displays that
        the new tap position and the correspondingly modified voltages and
        flows have been received in SCADA from the simulator. An alarm is
        issued because the transformer was moved to its maximum tap
        position.
        Notice on the RTNET Telemetered Network Data display that the tap
        measurement (disabled) still has the old value Xo=3. The SCADA
        value will only be updated when running RTNET.
     6. Run the on-line network sequence.
        Notice the increased number of suspect measurements.
        Notice in the Telemetered Network Data display, that the (unused)
        tap measurement now shows as X’=5 but the estimated value still
        shows equal to Xo=3 because the tap position was not estimated in
        the last RTNET run. It also shows as disabled.
     7. In absence of valid tap measurement, and if the tap estimation has not
        been requested, the modeled tap position shown under MDL in the
        Transformers view of RTNET Line/Transformer Summary display is
        used as a substitute for the missing measurement (disabled).

Source of Base Values (1)
Source of Base Values

     2. Base = Normal MVA limit
     3. Base = Nominal KV of branch

    2. Base = Nominal KV of bus

    1. Base = Base value on assigned Accuracy Class
    2. Base = Largest tap position (MX/MN_TAPTY)

 Weight Calculation and Accuracy Class-
 Voltage Regulation Equation Weight
The weight of a Unit Voltage Regulation equation is determined by NSIGMAS and
DEVIAT_UN
                                                     2
               ⎛ Nigmas ⎞
     Weight = ⎜⎜             ⎟⎟ * VREGDMHI
               ⎝ Deviat _ un ⎠


DEVIAT_UN value is used if it is greater than TOLSIG2, otherwise 0.05 is the
hard-coded default deviation resulting in a default weight of
(NSIGMAS/0.05)(NSIGMAS/0.05)*VREGDMHI. With the typical values
NSIGMAS=3 and VREGDMHI=10, the default weight is 36000.
When voltage regulation for a bus is activated, the bus equation for the regulated
bus is deweighted by multiplying by the Process Parameter VREGDMLO whose
typical value is 0.1.

Error Processing and Identification Logic (2)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       1. Solve WLS problem.
       2. Calculate quadratic cost = the sum of the squared and weighted
          residuals.
       3. Calculate Probability Confidence, shown on record display if the “Enable
          Error Processing” option is set.
               Select the “Enable Error Processing” option
       4. If Probability Confidence < CONFDES, then the Solution is Valid.
               “Error-Detection Confidence” (CONFDES), typical value 0.90 P.U.
       5. Determine Suspect Equations. If Weighted Residual > Breakpoint,
          equation is Suspect.


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 80


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page        3-80
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (3)

         Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       6. For each equation, calculate possible Proposed Weight Multiplier,
          Prop = (Breakpoint)**2/(Weighted Residual)**2
       7. Conditionally update Proposed Weight Multipliers:
          If (abs(Weighted Residual) > Breakpoint and
          and Current Weight Multiplier > ANOMLIM
          and (Prop >= (1+REWTDB)*Current Weight Multiplier
          or Prop <= (1-DEWTDB)*Current Weight Multiplier)
          Then
          Proposed Weight Multiplier = Prop
          Else
               Proposed Weight Multiplier = Current Weight Multiplier


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 81


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page     3-81
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (4)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       7. Conditionally update Proposed Weight Multipliers:
               “Anomaly Wt Multiplier Threshold” (ANOMLIM), typical value 0.03 P.U.
               “Reweight deadband” (REWTDB), typical value 0.50 P.U.
               “Deweight deadband” (DEWTDB), typical value 0.50 P.U.
       8. Calculate the effect of Proposed Weight Multipliers on Cost, the "Cost
           Change Prediction Function", an analysis of the sensitivity of equation
           residuals to the proposed weight adjustments.
       9. Add up all cost changes for deweights, displayed as Reweight Cost High
           on Solution Record display.
       10. Add up all cost changes for reweights, displayed as Reweight Cost Low
           on Solution Record display.


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 82


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page        3-82
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (5)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       11. If Reweight Cost High < DWTHRESH
            and Reweight Cost Low < RWTHRESH, the Solution is Valid.
            (i.e. the effect of the proposed weight multipliers would not be
                 significant)
               Deweighting: “Weight change convergence requirement”
                  (DWTHRESH), typical value is 2.50.
               Reweighting: weight change convergence requirement (RWTHRESH),
                  typical value is 2.50.
       12. If every predicted cost change > DJPRMN then the Solution is Valid.
           DJPRMN is a negative number (i.e., if all negative predicted cost
           changes are smaller in magnitude than this limit, the solution is valid).


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 83


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page              3-83
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (6)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       12. If every predicted cost change > DJPRMN then the Solution is Valid.
               “Solution valid limit” (DJPRMN), typical value -100.0 (or -50 to -500)
       13. Select Subset of Suspect Equations.
               Selection Criteria:
               If Proposed and Current Weight multipliers are not equal and the Proposed
                    Weight Multiplier = 1.0, then include suspect equation in the selected
                    subset.
               OR
               If Proposed and Current Weight multipliers are not equal and the Predicted Cost
                    Change is in the selection range between the Largest Negative Cost Change
                    and DJWTFRAC*Largest Negative Cost Change, then include suspect
                    equation in the selected subset.


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 84


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page                  3-84
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (7)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       13. Select Subset of Suspect Equations.
               “Fraction of Largest Weight Change Prediction” (DJWTFRAC), typical
                   value is 0.40 P.U.
       14. If the selected subset is empty and the inner bound of the selection
           range is currently a larger negative number than DJPRMN, then change
           inner bound to DJPRMN and re-evaluate selection criteria.
               “Solution valid limit” (DJPRMN), typical value -100.0 (or -50 to -500).
       15. If the selected subset is still empty, then the Solution is Valid.
       16. If largest cost change does not exceed DJPRMN, then the
           Solution is Valid.


Network Analysis | RTNET Miscellaneous Topics | 85


                                         Proprietary – See Copyright Page            3-85
                                           RTNET Miscellaneous Topics


<!-- salto de página -->

                                                     Network Analysis


Error Processing and Identification Logic (8)

        Processing Steps and Process Parameters
       17. Implement selected subset of Proposed Weight Multipliers (i.e. make
           them the Current Weight Multipliers) and re-solve the WLS problem.

       18. Repeat until the Solution is Valid.
           Once a Valid solution is obtained, update each suspect equation's
              counter as follows:
               If both Weighted Residuals < Breakpoint, then increment counter
               Else if (either Weighted Residual > Breakpoint
                    and equation is not already Anomalous
               and either Proposed Weight Multiplier < ANOMLIM), then decrement counter
               Else if     either Weighted Residual > Breakpoint, then zero counter
