4.4.1.2 Equipment Group (DEVGRP)
All network and generation power system resources that have SCADA measurements
associated with them need to be modeled in e-terrasource with an association with a

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              217                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

parent Equipment Group to be deployed to the SCADAMDL application. Only equipment that
is associated with an Equipment Group record is displayed on the SCADA Model Substation
tree view.
The Equipment Group record must reference a valid Equipment Group Type record (if it is
not a bay).
If the equipment group is modeling a bay configuration, all children equipment referencing
this Equipment Group record must reference a valid Equipment Group Type record. The
equipment group must not reference any equipment group type since this equipment
group gathers different types of equipment. It is valid to have several devices that map to
the same equipment group type.
AC Line Segments and Series Compensators can represent two DEVICE records in the
SCADAMOM database after export. If both terminals of the device are to be represented in
the SCADAMOM database, the AC Line Segment or Series Compensator must also reference
the Far Equipment Group association. This references the Equipment Group in the far
substation that is associated with the secondary terminal.


4.4.1.3 Equipment Group Type (TYPNAM)
The Equipment Group Type table configures the valid Equipment Group types. All
Equipment Group records must reference a valid Equipment Group Type (or equipment if
the equipment group type is a bay).
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
the SCADA Topology property group is modeled on the Equipment Group Type property
sheet.


4.4.1.4 Generic Equipment (DEVICE)
Equipment that is modeled for SCADA purposes only and has no association with any
network or generation functionality should be modeled on a Generic Equipment record. This
record contains only attributes associated with the SCADA application.


4.4.1.5 Modeling Equipment in SCADA
The following sections describe the different classifications of equipment that can be
modeled in SCADA and/or have SCADA measurements or calculations modeled as children.


4.4.1.5.1 Network Equipment with SCADA Measurements (DEVICE)
Analog, Discrete, Accumulator, Constant Argument, Calculation, Block Load Shed Point, and
Block Load Shed Duplicate records may be modeled as either a child of a power system
resource (network equipment or SCADA Generic Equipment) or as a child of a terminal of
network equipment. All of the children records should be modeled consistently under the
power system resource or a child terminal of the power system resource.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             218                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

For Series Compensators and AC Line Segments, the Analog, Discrete, Accumulator,
Constant Argument, Calculation, Block Load Shed Point, and Block Load Shed Duplicate
records are always modeled as children of the appropriate near or far terminal.
For all other network equipment, the Discrete, Accumulator, Constant Argument,
Calculation, Block Load Shed Point, and Block Load Shed Duplicate records are modeled
under the object representing the network equipment.
The Analogs may be represented under either the object representing the network
equipment or under a child Terminal record. However, there is special processing for
Transformer Winding network objects.
For Transformer Winding, Series Compensator, AC Line Segment, Switch, Equivalent Branch,
and DC Converter, it may be desirable to model the Analog records under the correct side
of the device (near vs. far) so that the measurement indication in the Graphic Modeler is
displayed on the correct side of the device.
There are some special cases, like in the secondary winding of a 2-winding transformer
where it would be desirable to show Analog measurements linked to a Terminal of the
Winding, but the Transformer Winding itself may not actually represent a DEVICE record in
SCADA. There may also be cases when modeling 3-winding transformers where one of the
winding is not modeled directly in SCADA, but it would be desirable to show the
measurements as linked to this side of the transformer winding in the Graphic Modeler. If it
is desired to show the Analog measurement indication on the correct side of the device, the
following may be performed in these special cases to account for this discrepancy.
1. Model a parent Equipment Group for the Secondary Transformer Winding so that it
   shows up in the SCADA tree view.
2. Set “For SCADA” to True on the child Terminal so that it will be included in the SCADA
   Graphic Modeler view. If you set this flag to true so that it shows up on the SCADA tree
   view but no SCADA DEVICE is created from this Terminal, also set the “Does Not Map To
   SCADA” flag to True.
3. Set the “Does Not Map To SCADA” attribute to True, to indicate that this
   Terminal/Transformer Winding is not directly exported to SCADA. This flag is only
   meaningful when “For SCADA” is set to True, indicating that you want to show the
   Terminal on the SCADA tree view, but no SCADA DEVICE is created from the associated
   Terminal.
In both cases, the Analogs modeled under the non-modeled Transformer Winding will be
placed under the SCADA DEVICE represented by the primary winding when exporting to
SCADA.
There may be other special cases where this same modeling of the “Does Not Map To
SCADA” attribute on the network equipment is desired. One example is when
measurements should be shown on the correct side of an AC Line Segment or Series
Compensator device, but it does not represent a DEVICE record in the exported SCADA
model.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            219                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

When importing domain models from savecases into e-terrasource, a search is first
performed for all imported SCADA DEVICEs for a match with an existing Conducting
Equipment record or child Terminal imported from the NETMOM savecase. If a match of the
SCADA key value confirms an association with an existing Terminal or Conducting
Equipment record, that record is selected as the target and all of the SCADA information
from the DEVICE record is copied to that Conducting Equipment or Terminal record. The
choice of whether the match is to a Terminal or to a Conducting Equipment record is made
in the Network to SCADA savecase mapping. If no match is found, a search is performed on
all Power System Resource records (which may have also been created by importing the
Generation savecases). If no match is found, a SCADA Generic Equipment record is created
and all of the SCADA information is copied from the DEVICE to the Generic Equipment
record.
In general, modeling of Connectivity Nodes on Conducting Equipment for SCADA topology
processing is similar to Network modeling of Connectivity Nodes. The Network connectivity
is modeled in the “Connectivity Node” reference of the child Terminal of Conducting
Equipment. The SCADA connectivity is modeled in the “SCADA Connectivity Node” reference
on the child Terminal of Conducting Equipment, and many cases they are set to the same
values. See section 2.1.3.4 SCADA Topology Display. Following are special conditions for
modeling SCADA Connectivity Nodes on some Conducting Equipment.
• Power Transformer: A SCADA DEVICE record may be created for any or all of the
  children Terminal records of each Transformer Winding (those where “For Scada” is
  marked true and “Does not Map to Scada Device” is NOT marked true).
    The ITPND and ZTPND values for the SCADA DEVICE created for the primary Transformer
    Winding are set as follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the primary transformer winding
     – The ZTPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the secondary transformer winding.
    The ITPND and ZTPND values for the SCADA DEVICE created for the secondary
    Transformer Winding are set as follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the secondary transformer winding
     – The ZTPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the primary transformer winding.
    The ITPND and ZTPND values for the SCADA DEVICE created for the tertiary Transformer
    Winding are set as follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the tertiary transformer winding
     – The ZTPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the child Terminal of the primary transformer winding.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page           220                                 SCADA Modeling
                                                              e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    If the Power Transformer is a 3-winding transformer, and the “Scada Middle Point”
    connectivity node reference is filled in on the Power Transformer, then the ITPND and
    ZTPND values are created differently, as follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Connectivity Node
       reference of the Terminal from which the DEVICE is being created
     – The ZTPND value is set to the EMSName field of the Scada Middle Point Connectivity
       Node.
• ACLineSegment and SeriesCompensator: For these records, the ITPND, ZTPND, and ZST
  values of the exported SCADA DEVICE associated with the the near Terminal are set as
  follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the SCADA Connectivity Node
       reference of the near Terminal
     – The ZTND value is set to the EMSName field of the SCADA Connectivity Node
       reference of the far Terminal, and
     – The ZST value is set to the the EMSName field of the parent Substation of the
       FarEquipmentGroup referenced directly from the ACLineSegment or
       SeriesCompensator.
    The ITPND, ZTPND, and ZST values of the exported SCADA DEVICE associated with the
    the far Terminal are set as follows:
     – The ITPND value is set to the EMSName field of the SCADA Connectivity Node
       reference of the far Terminal
     – The ZTPND value is set to the EMSName field of the SCADA Connectivity Node
       reference of the near Terminal, and
     – The ZST value is set to the EMSName field of the parent Substation of the
       EquipmentGroup referenced directly from the ACLineSegment or
       SeriesCompensator.
Creation of the ITPND, ZTPND, and ZST values from e-terrasource Conducting Equipment
follows the descriptions detailed above. Because there is not both a near and far node
value kept on each and every Terminal, there are some cases where round trip of SCADA
may change the ITPND or ZTPND value of certain devices. It is not expected that these will
affect network to scada mapping or Scada topology processing, however. This close
association between network and Scada use of Connectivity Nodes is to provide the ability
to initialize Scada topology graphic displays and modeling directly from network modeling.
There are a couple of special flags are used when modeling SCADA information on
ConductingEquipment, “Do Not Export Base Voltage To Scada” and ScadaBaseVoltage.
For all Conducting Equipment, if the “Do Not Export Base Voltage To Scada” flag is set, then
on export the NOMKV_DEVICE field of the exported SCADA record will be unassigned, even if
the network Conducting Equipment has a reference to Base Voltage.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            221                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

For Series Compensator and AC Line Segment, if the ScadaBaseVoltage reference on the
Terminal record is set (non-null), then the NOMKV_DEVICE value of the exported DEVICE is
set to the Terminal’s ScadaBaseVoltage instead of the BaseVoltage value of the Series
Compensator or AC Line Segment. This is only for occasions when it is required that the
Scada Nominal KV be a different value than the Network Base Voltage.
For all other Conducting Equipment, if the ScadaBaseVoltage reference on the
ConductingEquipment is set (non-null), then the NOMKV_DEVICE value of the exported
DEVICE is set to the ScadaBaseVoltage instead of the BaseVoltage.


4.4.1.5.2 SCADA Generic Equipment (DEVICE)
For Generic Equipment, the Near and Far connectivity node information is modeled directly
on the Generic Equipment object.
• Near Node: If the equipment is to be included in the SCADA topology model, the Near
  Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node record.
• Far Node: If the equipment is to be included in the SCADA topology model and is not a
  single-terminal device, the Far Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node
  record.
If the SCADA topology nodes are different from the network nodes, the SCADA-only
Connectivity Node records can be created to model them.


4.4.1.5.3 Other Power System Resources with SCADA Measurements (DEVICE)
Some generation-related power system resources can also be modeled with analog or
discrete measurements. If so, those resources should be associated with an Equipment
Group record so that they are displayed on the SCADA model tree view and exported to
SCADAMDL on model deployment.
For these generation-related power system resources, the Near and Far connectivity node
information is modeled directly on the object representing the power system resource.
• Near Node: If the equipment is to be included in the SCADA topology model, the Near
  Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node record.
• Far Node: If the equipment is to be included in the SCADA topology model and is not a
  single-terminal device, the Far Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node
  record.
If the SCADA topology nodes are different from the network nodes, the SCADA-only
Connectivity Node records can be created to model them.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page           222                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                               e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.2 SCADA Reference Tables

4.4.2.1 Accumulator Data Item Type (CTRTYP)
The Accumulator Data Item type is referenced by Data Item records that model
accumulator counters. It contains a set of attributes that can be referenced from many
individual accumulator type data items.
• Maximum Count: This attribute defines the maximum decimal count before rollover.
  Use the following count for each protocol:
     – For Landis & Gyr and Vancomm RTUs, this value should be set to 65,535.
     – For Conitel, this value can be set to 4095 or 16777215, depending on the number of
       bits returned for the accumulator type.
     – For GETAC, this value should be set to 4095.
     – For CDC, this value should be set to 16777215.
• Number of Bits: The number of bits returned in the data stream from the RTU for this
  accumulator type. Use the following number for each protocol:
     – For Landis & Gyr and Vancomm RTUs, this value should be set to 16.
     – For Conitel, this value can be set to 12 or 24, depending on the physical accumulator
       device.
     – For GETAC, this value should be set to 12.
     – For CDC, this value should be set to 16.


4.4.2.2 Accumulator Name (CNTNAM)
The Accumulator Name table is used to define valid names for Accumulator records.


4.4.2.3 Alternate Limit Type (ALTTYP)
Alternate Limit types allow specification of multiple limit sets that are used at different
times. For example, an alternate type “SEASON” can include alternate limit sets “FALL”,
“WINTER”, “SPRING”, and “SUMMER”. At any given time, exactly one of the child sets is in
effect for the alternate type.


4.4.2.4 Alternate Limit Set (ALTSET)
The Alternate Limit Set record defines the different groupings for alternate limits to be
organized under an Alternate Limit Type record.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              223                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.2.5 Alternate Limit Check (ALTCHK)
The Alternate Limit Check definition allows configuration of alternate limits associated with
one Alternate Limit Set to be required to have a valid relationship to other Alternate Limit
Sets associated with the same Alternate Limit Type.
For example, the high alternate limit value for the “SUMMER” Alternate Limit Set can be
required to have a value greater than the high alternate limit for the “WINTER” Alternate
Limit Set.


4.4.2.6 Analog Alarm Category (CATALG)
The Analog Alarm Category table is used to define alarm category information associated
with Analog records.


4.4.2.7 Analog Limit Name (LMTNAM)
The Analog Limit Name table is used to define valid names for Analog Limit records.


4.4.2.8 Analog Name (ALGNAM)
The Analog Name table is used to define valid names for Analog records.
For switches:
• “MW” for MW measurement. Variants:
     – “RMW” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMW” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
• “MX” for MVAR measurement. Variants:
     – “RMX” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMX” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
• “3AM” for 3-phase amp measurements.
• “1AM” for 1-phase amp measurements.
• “MVA” for MVA measurements.
• “PF” for power factor measurements.
• Voltage and phase-angle measurements are a special case, and are discussed in their
  own section.
For shunt devices (Synchronous Machine, Static Var Compensator, Equivalent Loads, Shunt
Compensators, and Reactors):
• “MW” for MW measurement.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             224                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    Unit variants:
     – “RMW” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMW” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
    Load variants:
     – “CW” equivalent to “MW”, “RMW”, or “RCW” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMW” or “DCW” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
• “MX” for MVAR measurement.
    Unit variants:
     – “RMX” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMX” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
    Load and SVS variants:
     – “CX” equivalent to “MX”, “RMX”, or “RCX” indicates used by RTNET only.
     – “DMX” or “DCX” indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.
• “3AM” for 3-phase amp measurements.
• “1AM” for 1-phase amp measurements.
• “MVA” for MVA measurements.
• “PF” for power factor measurements.
• Voltage and phase-angle measurements are a special case, and are discussed in their
  own section.
For branches such as AC Line Segment, Series Compensator, and Transformer Winding:
• “MW” or “CW” for MW measurement. Variants:

• “1AM” for 1-phase amp measurements.

• “PF” for power factor measurements.

4.4.2.9 Calculation Function (FUNC)
Calculation Function records are referenced by Calculation records in the substation
hierarchy. Calculation Function records define a single instance for each unique delivered
SCADA calculation.
Calculation records define each group of measurements to perform the calculation on.
Each Calculation record references a Calculation Function record.
A single Calculation Function record can be referenced by many Calculation records.
For a complete list of delivered calculations, see section 4.4.5 Calculation Functions.


4.4.2.10 Calculation Function Argument (ARG)
The Calculation Function Argument record allows the definition of multiple calculation
arguments associated with a single Calculation Function.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              227                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.2.11 Command Name (CTLNAM)
The Command Name table is used to define valid names for Command records.


4.4.2.12 Conversion Table (CONV)
Conversion Table records define data conversion processing, which can optionally be
applied to any Discrete or Analog type data item telemetry input measurement defined in
the model.


4.4.2.12.1 Discrete Conversion
Conversion Table records are required for three-state or four-state discrete measurements
whose telemetered bit values must be re-ordered or flipped. The conversion is usually
required because the connection in the RTU is wired backward or does not match the
chosen convention of “Open” or “Closed” Discretes in the model.


4.4.2.12.2 Analog Conversion
Linear analog conversion information is kept on the analog Data Item record. If the Use
Conversion Table field of the Data Item record is “none”, then all of the needed conversion
data is in the Data Item record.
If the Analog has a linear conversion, the Slope and Intercept fields are computed from the
raw and engineering values entered on the Card general edit form.


4.4.2.12.3 Conversion Process
The paired data points represented by Conversion Data Point records are derived from the
calibration curve for the transducer. The data processing programs linearly interpolate
these points to scale raw values to engineering units. Each record represents the end point
of a segment, and a slope and intercept are calculated for each segment. If there is a
pointer to a non-linear conversion, then at least two Conversion Data Points must be
defined and associated with the Conversion Table record.


4.4.2.13 Conversion Data Point (DATA)
The Conversion Data Point record allows the definition of multiple data points associated
with a single Conversion record.


4.4.2.14 Discrete Alarm Category (CATPNT)
The Discrete Alarm Category table is used to define alarm category information associated
with Discrete records.

The Discrete Name table is used to define valid names for Discrete records.

  Note: The INCTOP flag on the PNTNAM record is respected on import from the application
  databases into e-terrasource. If the flag is set to False, the node information on the
  associated discretes will not be modeled when the models are imported.

For switches:
• “STTS” for open/closed status. (Variants: “RSTS” indicates used by RTNET only, “DSTS”
  indicates used by e-terrasimulator only.)
• “A/M” for auto/manual status.
• “L/R” for local/remote status.
For shunt devices (Synchronous Machine, Static Var Compensator, Equivalent Loads, Shunt
Compensators, and Reactors):
• “AVR” for auto/manual regulation status measurement (not applicable to loads).
  (Variants: “RAVR” indicates used by RTNET only, “DAVR” indicates used by

For branches such as AC Line Segment, Series Compensator, and Transformer Winding:

For DC converters:

For DC poles:
• Point measurement is not supported.
For synchronization data:
• Point map name is “SISI”.

The Discrete Type table is used to define parameters for different types of Discrete records,
grouped by type, such as for breakers and disconnects.

4.4.2.18 Permission Area (AREA)
The Permission Area table is used to define valid areas of responsibility for Substation,

4.4.2.19 Port Switching Schedule (PTHTST)
The Port Switching Schedule allows optional modeling of communication line switching

4.4.2.20 RTU Type (RTUTYP)
The RTU Type table defines the supported Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) types.


4.4.2.21 SCADA Accumulator Type (ACCUM)
The SCADA Accumulator Type table is used to define accumulator classes. It is used to
define the timers for collecting pulse accumulator data. The timers define the time at which
accumulators should be frozen or read, how often they should be frozen or read, and
whether global or individual freezes are performed. In the model, each RTU scan group that
configures pulse accumulator values must be associated with one of the Accumulator Class
records.

4.4.2.23 SCADA Deadband (DBAND)
The SCADA Deadband table defines the deadband values associated with each transducer
in the model. The raw value deadband value defines how much of a change in the raw
value is required in the e-terracontrol front end before returning the new value to the host
SCADA system.


4.4.2.24 SCADA Error Bucket (BUCKET)
The SCADA Error Bucket form is used to define classifications for communication errors
associated with an RTU Connection or Scan Group. Each record can define up to sixteen
different error classifications.
Error buckets are used to group communication errors into more categories than the three
standard categories: RTU No-Reply Errors, CRC/BCH Errors, and Other Communication
Errors.


4.4.2.25 SCADA History (SCHIST)
The SCADA History table is used to model the required information for saving Analog,
Discrete, and Accumulator information in the SCADA Short-Term History database.


4.4.2.26 SCADA Note Type (NOTTYP)
The SCADA Note Types table is used to define the default color and properties of display
notes.


4.4.2.27 SCADA Scan Rate (RATE)
The SCADA Scan Rate table is used to define valid scan rates and integrity scan rates for
RTU data. Each Scan Group in the model that is scanned on a periodic basis (except those
that model Pulse, Relay, or Analog Output records) must be associated with one of the valid
scan rates defined in this table.


4.4.2.28 SCADA Tag Type (TAGTYP)
The SCADA Tag Type table is used to define valid tag types that can be applied to a wide set
of SCADA record types, such as Substation, Equipment Group, Scan Group, Analog, Discrete,
Accumulator, Site, and RTU.
The Tag Types table provides fields for assigning properties to each tag type, such as color,
priority, record types receiving it, and blocking and restriction attributes.
A tag type’s priority setting determines whether a tag of that type causes a tag to display
on a SCADA oneline, next to the picture of the device on which it is placed. Priority 1 has the


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              235                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

highest priority. If multiple tags of different tag types are placed on a device, the tag type
with the highest priority setting prevails.
The blocking attributes prevent control actions of types open, close, or setpoint. The
restriction attributes cause SCADA to issue a warning message when a control action of
type open, close, or setpoint is received. The operator must override the warning to
continue the control action.
The Discrete open/close attribute supports the requirement that a tagged discrete record
must be in the designated state before it can accept a supervisory control.
The prevent loadshed attribute prevents load shedding from occurring at the tagged
Discrete.


4.4.2.29 SCADA Trigger Timer (TIMER)
The SCADA Trigger Timer table is used to define general timers for calculations that are
triggered by factors other than the processing of another measurement.


4.4.2.30 Setpoint Name (SPTNAM)
The Setpoint Name table is used to define valid names for Setpoint records.


4.4.2.31 Site Permission (SITPRM)
Site Permission records provide fields for modeling InterSite Data (ISD) access permissions.
The modeler enters Site Permission ID and Site Reference details in this table. Global fields
for enabling/disabling permission checking and logging prohibited-access attempts are set
to their default states using attributes defined on the SCADA Configuration table.


4.4.2.32 Site Reference (SITREF)
The Site Reference record allows the definition of multiple site references associated with a
single Site Permission record.


4.4.3 Measurements/Limits
The Calculation, Analog, Accumulator, Discrete, Constant Argument, Block Load Shed Point,
and Block Load Shed Duplicate records are modeled as children of the SCADA Generic
Equipment table, network-defined equipment, or generation-defined power system
equipment, or a child terminal of network-defined equipment.


4.4.3.1 Accumulator (COUNT)
The Accumulator record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child
terminal of the power system resource. If the accumulator record is associated with an AC

Line Segment or Series Compensator, the Accumulator record must be modeled under the
near or far terminal.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the Accumulator
property sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.
• SCADA User Flags: This property group contains user-definable quality flags and

Measurement Grouping: When the model is deployed to the SCADAMDL application, the

4.4.3.2 Accumulator Value (Currently Unused)
This table is defined in the standard Common Information Model (CIM), but it is currently
unused in e-terrasource.


4.4.3.3 Analog (ANALOG)
The Analog record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child
terminal of the power system resource. If the analog record is associated with an AC Line
Segment or Series Compensator, the Analog record must be modeled under the near or far
terminal.
If the Analog record is modeled in the SCADA topology model, it must reference a near
Connectivity Node record. If the Analog does reference a Connectivity Node record for
SCADA topology, it should be shown on the SCADA Graphic Modeler view of the Substation
record.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the Analog property
sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.
• SCADA User Flags: This property group contains user-definable quality flags and
  Boolean attributes.
Measurement Grouping: When the model is deployed to the SCADAMDL application, the
identity of the MEAS grouping record created in the SCADAMOM database as a parent of
this Analog record is created from the name in this field.
Near Node: If the Analog is to be included in the SCADA topology model, the Near Node
must reference the correct Connectivity Node record. If the SCADA topology nodes are


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             237                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

different from the network nodes, SCADA-only Connectivity Nodes can be created to model
them.


4.4.3.4 Analog Alternate Limit (ALTLIM)
The Analog Alternate Limit is modeled under an Analog Limit, and it defines a set of
alternate limit values that can be used to replace the current high and low limit values of
the parent Analog Limit record. Each Analog Alternate Limit must reference a valid
Alternate Limit Set record.


4.4.3.5 Analog Limit (LIMIT)
The Analog Limit is modeled under the Analog Limit Set grouping record, and it defines one
or more alarm and processing limits for an analog value.


4.4.3.6 Analog Limit Set (No Direct Mapping)
If any SCADA Analog Limits or Analog Rate Limits are to be defined for an Analog, they
should be grouped under a single Analog Limit Set with a Name value of “SCADA”.


4.4.3.7 Analog Rate Limit (RATLIM)
The Analog Rate Limit is modeled under the Analog Limit Set grouping record, and it defines
more rate-of-change alarms for an analog value.


4.4.3.8 Analog Value (Currently Unused)
This table is defined in the standard Common Information Model (CIM), but it is currently
unused in e-terrasource.


4.4.3.9 Block Load Shed Duplicate (BLSDUP)
This record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child terminal of
the power system resource. If the block load shed duplicate is associated with an AC Line
Segment or Series Compensator, the Block Load Shed Duplicate record must be modeled
under the near or far terminal. For additional information, see section 4.4.9 Modeling SCADA
Load Shed Data.


4.4.3.10 Block Load Shed Point (BLSPT)
This record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child terminal of
the power system resource. If the block load shed point is associated with an AC Line
Segment or Series Compensator, the Block Load Shed Point record must be modeled under


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             238                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

the near or far terminal. For additional information, see section 4.4.9 Modeling SCADA Load
Shed Data.


4.4.3.11 Calculation (MEAS that Models a Calculation)
The Calculation record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child
terminal of the power system resource. If the calculation is associated with an AC Line
Segment or Series Compensator, the Calculation record must be modeled under the near or
far terminal.
Calculations are normally triggered by the change of a scanned value that is part of a
Measurement Group or referenced from a Measurement Group. Calculations can also be
done on a timed basis. The Measurement Group can be associated with a SCADA Trigger
Timer record to link the calculation to that timer.
Each Calculation record references a Calculation Function record that defines the valid
inputs and outputs to the calculation, and it defines the calculation processing to be
performed.
Measurement Grouping: When the model is deployed to the SCADAMDL application, the
identity of the MEAS grouping record created in the SCADAMOM database to model this
calculation is created from the name in this field.
Control Type: If this calculation is used to model a “Simultaneous Control” or a “Multiple
Control”, this attribute should be set accordingly. If the calculation is modeling a normal
data acquisition calculation, this field should be set to the “Not Applicable” setting.
For a complete list of delivered calculations, see section 4.4.5 Calculation Functions.
For additional information about modeling the special Simultaneous or Multiple Control
calculations, see section 4.4.6 Simultaneous and Multiple Control Calculation Functions.


4.4.3.12 Calculation Argument (PNTREF, ALGREF, CNTREF, CONREF, CTLREF)
Calculation Arguments define the children arguments to be associated with the same
Calculation record. Each Calculation Argument record must reference a Calculation
Function Argument and an associated Analog, Discrete, Accumulator, Constant Argument,
or Command record.
Reference Flag: If the Reference flag is set to Yes (or True), the calculation arguments are
inserted into SCADAMDL as reference records. A value of Yes (or True) means that when
deploying the model, the reference should be inserted into SCADAMDL as an xxxREF record,
and inserted under a different MEAS grouping record than the referenced argument.
However, to maintain consistency with previous versions of the SCADA model, if the
Reference flag is set to False, it is assumed that this reference is to an Analog, Discrete,
Accumulator, or Constant Argument that is a direct child of a MEAS record, and the
calculation is configured directly on that MEAS record.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              239                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Measurement Grouping: All Analog, Discrete, Accumulator, and Constant Argument
records inserted into SCADAMDL on deployment are grouped under a MEAS record. This
MEAS record is not directly modeled in e-terrasource. The MEAS identifier is created from
the Measurement Grouping attribute on the Calculation record.
If the parent calculation is configured to model a special Simultaneous or Multiple Control
calculation, the Calculation Argument is set to reference a Command record instead of one
of the measurement records.


4.4.3.13 Command (CTRL)
The Command record is modeled under a Discrete record, and it defines the valid
supervisory controls command that can be issued for a discrete measurement.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there is the following SCADA property grouping for modeling on the Command property
sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.


4.4.3.14 Command Lock (LOCK)
The Command Lock record is modeled under a Command record, and it defines whether
specific supervisory control actions are allowed or disallowed based on the status of an
unrelated Discrete measurement, if the value of an unrelated Analog measurement is
within an approved range, or if the value is based on the topological state of an unrelated
device.


4.4.3.15 Constant Argument (RCONST)
The Constant Argument record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a
child terminal of the power system resource. If the constant argument is associated with an
AC Line Segment or Series Compensator, the Constant Argument record must be modeled
under the near or far terminal.
Measurement Grouping: When the model is deployed to the SCADAMDL application, the
identity of the MEAS grouping record created in the SCADAMOM database as a parent of
this Constant Argument record is created from the name in this field.


4.4.3.16 Data Item (ANOUT, CONECT, PULSE, RELAY, XDUCER)
The Data Item record is used to model a telemetry input or telemetry output point of an
RTU. Data Item records are modeled under a Card record, and all Data Item records under a
single card must be of the same type (telemetry reference to an Accumulator, Analog,
Discrete, Command, or Setpoint record).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             240                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.3.16.1 Data Item Modeling for Analog Telemetry References
There are no special modeling parameter values for the standard protocols.


4.4.3.16.2 Data Item Modeling for Discrete Telemetry References
There are no special modeling parameter values for the standard protocols.


4.4.3.16.3 Data Item Modeling for Accumulator Telemetry References
There are no special modeling parameter values for the standard protocols.


4.4.3.16.4 Data Item Modeling for Command Telemetry References
Model Parameter 1: This attribute defines special modeling attributes for different RTU
communication protocols.
• For Landis & Gyr protocol RTUs, enter the RTU’s time interval per count to match what is
  preset in the RTU. It must be set to 10, 20, 40, or 80 milliseconds. This is relevant to
  Select Before Operate controls only.
• For Pulse Train Output controls on Landis & Gyr protocol RTUs, enter the Pulse Count for
  the control.
• For Conitel, Vancomm, and CDC protocol RTUs, enter the base time. The requested
  operation time entered on the CTRL record is divided by this time in the SCADA front end
  in determining the value to send to the RTU. This parameter is only relevant to Pulse
  Width Output and Pulse Train Output controls.
• This parameter is not used for GETAC RTU protocols.
Model Parameter 2: This attribute defines special modeling attributes for different RTU
communication protocols.
• For Conitel protocol RTUs, enter the offset.
• For Pulse Train Output controls on Landis & Gyr protocol RTUs, enter the On Duration in
  tics for the control.
• For Pulse Width Output controls on CDC protocol RTUs, enter the Delta Time in
  milliseconds for the control.
• This parameter is not used for Vancomm or GETAC RTU protocols.
Model Parameter 3: This attribute defines special modeling attributes for different RTU
communication protocols.
• For Pulse Train Output controls on Landis & Gyr protocol RTUs, enter the Off Duration in
  tics for the control.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            241                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

      Note: The duration (in tics) is computed from the optime and the first two relay
      parameters. Parameter 1 is the BASE. Parameter 2 is the OFFSET.

        Duration = (OPTIME - PARM1 x PARM2)/ PARM1
• This control parameter is not currently used for Conitel, Vancomm, GETAC, or CDC RTU
  protocols.


4.4.3.16.5 Data Item Modeling for Setpoint Telemetry References
There are no special modeling parameter values for the standard protocols.


4.4.3.17 Discrete (POINT)
The Discrete record may be modeled under a power system resource or under a child
terminal of the power system resource. If the discrete is associated with an AC Line
Segment or Series Compensator, the Discrete record must be modeled under the near or
far terminal.
Discrete records are uniquely associated with Connectivity Nodes when they are defined in
the SCADA topology model. If the Discrete record is modeled as a topology Switch in the
SCADA topology model, it must reference near and far Connectivity Node records. If the
Discrete record does reference Connectivity Node records for SCADA topology, they should
be shown on the SCADA Graphic Modeler view of the Substation record.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the Discrete property
sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.
• SCADA Topology: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for
  modeling SCADA topology information.
• SCADA User Flags: This property group contains user-definable quality flags and
  Boolean attributes.
Measurement Grouping: When the model is deployed to the SCADAMDL application, the
identity of the MEAS grouping record created in the SCADAMOM database as a parent of
this Discrete record is created from the name in this field.
Near Node: If the Discrete record is to be included in the SCADA topology model, the Near
Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node record. If the SCADA topology nodes
are different from the network nodes, SCADA-only Connectivity Nodes can be created to
model them. The SCADA topology connectivity nodes are not created on import of the
models if the INCTOP flag of the referenced PNTNAM record is set to False.
Far Node: If the Discrete record is to be included in the SCADA topology model, the Far
Node must reference the correct Connectivity Node record. If the SCADA topology nodes

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             242                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

are different from the network nodes, SCADA-only Connectivity Nodes can be created to
model them. The SCADA topology connectivity nodes are not created on import of the
models if the INCTOP flag of the referenced PNTNAM record is set to False.


4.4.3.18 Discrete Value (Currently Unused)
This table is defined in the standard Common Information Model (CIM), but it is currently
unused in e-terrasource.


4.4.3.19 InterSite Alias Name (ANALAS, CTALAS, PTALAS)
The InterSite Alias Name table is used to model communication between different SCADA
sites where the CIM Path Name (known as the “virtual ID” in SCADA) of Analog, Accumulator,
and Discrete records are not the same. This record allows for defining an alternate Path
Name as known by the remote SCADA system.


4.4.3.20 Setpoint (SETPNT)
The Setpoint record is modeled under an Analog record, and it defines the valid supervisory
controls setpoint commands that can be issued for an Analog measurement.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there is the following SCADA property grouping for modeling on the Setpoint property sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.


4.4.3.21 Setpoint Lock (SLOCK)
The Setpoint Lock record is modeled under a Setpoint record. It defines whether specific
supervisory control actions are allowed or disallowed based on the value of a telemetered
measurement. The telemetered measurement reference may be to an unrelated discrete
measurement, or an unrelated analog measurement who’s value must be within an
approved range, or a topological state of an unrelated device.


4.4.4 Communications
For information about e-terracomm communications modeling, see chapter 7 e-terracomm
Modeling. The following sections refer to SCADA communications modeling.


4.4.4.1 CFE (TFE)
CFE records provide information about modeling the communications system and
represent individual e-terracontrol front ends that may or may not be running on a
separate computer.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page            243                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

The e-terracontrol front end prioritizes RTU requests. In a dual redundant configuration, the
front ends can be configured to continue scanning when the SCADA host CPU fails to the
secondary, and to return the data gathered to the new host when it becomes primary.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the CFE property sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.


4.4.4.2 CFE Network Server (NETSRV)
The CFE Network Server table is used to define which network server each CFE Reader is
configured on.
For WINSTRMS CFE Type CFE Readers, the name of the network server is used to form the
name of the CfereaderDS dataset and the corresponding data source. One instance of CFE
Reader must be started for each Cfereader data source. When dialup RTUs are included in
the model for WINSTRMS CFE Readers, they must be modeled under a CFE Reader with a
different network server name than the non-dialup RTUs.


4.4.4.3 CFE Reader (CHANEL)
CFE Reader records model a single Communications front end configured on the
e-terracontrol front end. Generally, the CFE Reader is associated with a single card on a
local bus or in a remote chassis. This record includes identifying the image to be
downloaded to the CFE when it is initially configured or restarted.
For e-terracontrol front ends, the netserver name on the Channel record can be used to
partition the communication lines on a front end into separate data sources. This is
required for dialup RTUs, which must be modeled under a separate data source from
non-dialup RTUs. It also provides a mechanism to arbitrarily divide the communication lines
of a front end into separate data sources to facilitate load leveling or to allow switching at a
finer level of granularity if a failure occurs. Under a CFE, a separate data source is created
for each separate netserver name encountered.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the CFE Reader property
sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.
Name: The name or identifier of the communication channel. For VME-based CFE types, the
CHANEL name should be in the form “nnnnnn:x”, where nnnnnn is the name of the server
(ID__NETSRV) and x is the board number. For example, if your server is named “VMEFE1”,
the CHANEL with board number 0 should have an ID of “VMEFE1:0”.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              244                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.4.4 Card (CARD)
The Card is modeled as a child of the Scan Group record and is used to model a single
communications card in the RTU. The children Data Item records modeled under a card
must reference the same type of Measurement or Control record (Analog, Accumulator,
Command, Discrete, or Setpoint). A physical card that is split between data retrieval
addresses has more than one Card record.


4.4.4.5 Port (PATH)
Port records model a single communications line from the CFE to one or more physical
RTUs. The communications line can be a physical link, or a link of any other type, such as
microwaves.
Path information includes identifying the no-reply timeout and interbyte gap in
milliseconds, the baud rate used to retrieve data, whether the communication line uses
constant carrier, sequence of events, whether more than one communication line is
bridged together with this one, whether this line is used for dialup RTUs, etc.


4.4.4.6 Protocol-Specific Info (PCLxxx)
Protocol-Specific Info records are used to model attribute values that are only used for a
unique implementation of an RTU protocol and are not easily modeled as a generic
modeling attribute. The Protocol-Specific Info record can be associated with a CFE Reader,
RTU, Port, or Data Item record.


4.4.4.7 RTU (RTU)
RTU records are used to model the data retrieval system, including information such as
what protocol is used to communicate with the RTU, the address to which the RTU
responds, and what action is to be performed (such as when alarms are inhibited).
Dialup RTUs must use a separate e-terracontrol data source from non-dialup RTUs. This
means that they must be modeled under a separate CFE Reader record from non-dialup
RTUs. In addition, the Netserver name on the dialup record must be different from the
Netserver name on the non-dialup CFE Reader record.
When dialup RTUs are modeled, it is necessary to model both a single master dialup Port
and a separate modem Port for each dialup modem. The master dialup port must have one
child Serial Port Detail record modeled for each dialup RTU used by the data source. The
dialup modem ports have no children, but model the configuration parameters for the serial
ports used with the dialup modems; otherwise, they are modeled in the same way that
non-dialup RTUs are modeled, but with a few additional parameters.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             245                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there are the following SCADA property groupings for modeling on the RTU property sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.


4.4.4.8 Scan Group (ADRS)
Each Scan Group corresponds to a single RTU request. The Scan Group can be organized by
the type of measurements that physically exist in the RTU. However, all the data associated
with a Scan Group must be scanned at a single rate, since the rate to obtain related data
from the RTU is entered on the Scan Group record.
Information modeled can include the number of immediate retries to be performed by the
CFE if communication errors are encountered, the number of communication errors to
process before failing the Scan Group, etc.
Each scan group can also have associated scan group protocol records as children.


4.4.4.9 Serial Port Details (RTUC)
Serial Port Detail records define attributes associated with a single communications path to
an RTU. The name must match an existing (modeled) RTU record.


4.4.4.10 Site (SITE)
The Site table is used to define valid SCADA sites, including the local site. Each Analog,
Accumulator, and Discrete record in the model must be associated with a SCADA Site
record in this table. Only data retrieved via InterSite Data is associated with any site other
than the local site name.
In addition to the normal property groupings of Identification, Associations, and General,
there is the following SCADA property grouping for modeling on the Site property sheet:
• SCADA Alarming: This property grouping contains attributes and properties for modeling
  alarm information.


4.4.5 Calculation Functions
The standard calculations implemented in SCADA are listed below. The calculation name is
followed by the function list name (in parentheses), as initially provided in the initialization
model. This is the name that should appear on the measurement group records. The name
can be changed on the function list display. There is not a default function list name
provided for all calculations, in which case the associated FUNC record may need to be
added.
The descriptive Subroutine attribute associates the calculation with the SCADA function to
be performed.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              246                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Existing calculations are described in the following sections.

  Note: If “ARG#” is used, you can use any record names for this argument. If another name
  is used for the argument (like AMPS) the record name must match.
  Note: The general format is “Calculation name (ID)”. The ID represents the ID as currently
  modeled in a delivered savecase. For some functions, ID is not modeled, which means
  that no examples are provided for this function.


4.4.5.1 General Analog Calculations
This section provides the list of the SCADA calculations whose outputs are an analog,
accumulator, or real constant type.


4.4.5.1.1 Analog Addition (ADD)
There must be at least two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARGn = ARG1 + ARG2 + ... + ARGn-1


4.4.5.1.2 Analog Subtraction (SUB)
There must be at least two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARGn = ARG1 - ARG2 - ... - ARGn-1


4.4.5.1.3 Analog Multiplication (MULT)
There must be at least two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARGn = ARG1 * ARG2 * ... * ARGn-1


4.4.5.1.4 Analog Division (DIV)
There must be exactly three arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 = ARG1 / ARG2

  Note: If ARG2 is close to 0 (less than 1.0E-34), ARG3 will be set to Old (SUSPECT) with value
  0.0.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              247                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.5.1.5 Analog Exponentiation (EXPN)
There must be exactly three arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3=ARG1 ** ARG2


4.4.5.1.6 Analog Square Root (SQR)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = ARG1

  Note: If ARG1 is less than 0, ARG2 is set to old (SUSPECT) with a value of 0.0


4.4.5.1.7 Analog Running Maximum (MAX)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = max(ARG1, ARG2);

  Note: If ARG2’s quality is garbage (uninitialized) and ARG1’s quality is not garbage, ARG2’s
  quality is reinitialized to ARG1’s quality.


4.4.5.1.8 Analog Running Maximum (MIN)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = min(ARG1, ARG2);

  Note: If ARG2’s quality is garbage (uninitialized) and ARG1’s quality is not garbage, ARG2’s
  quality is reinitialized to ARG1’s quality.


4.4.5.1.9 Analog Averaging Summation Part (ISUM)
There must be exactly three arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 = ARG3 + ARG1
ARG2 = ARG2 + 1


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              248                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

  Note: If ARG1’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), the calculation does not update anything
  (skipped).

If ARG2’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), ARG2’s value is set to 0, and the quality is reset to
nothing.
If ARG3’s quality is garbage, ARG3 is set to 0 and quality reinitialized to nothing.


4.4.5.1.10 Analog Averaging Average Part (IAVG)
There must be exactly three arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 = ARG1 / ARG2
ARG1 = 0
ARG2 = 0

  Note: If ARG1’s or ARG2’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), ARG3’s quality is set to old
  (suspect) and the calculation is skipped.

If ARG2 is close to 0 (1.0E-34), ARG3 is set to 0.0 with old (suspect) quality.
If ARG3 is an accumulator and the accumulator has been configured to only use the whole
part (no decimal) and keep the decimal, ARG3’s value is truncated to the whole part of the
result.


4.4.5.1.11 Analog Conditional Replacement (CRPL)
There must be exactly four arguments.
ARG1, ARG2, and ARG4 must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 has to be a discrete record type.
If ARG3 = 1 then
    ARG4 = ARG1
Else
    ARG4 = ARG2
End If

  Note: If ARG3’s quality is garbage, ARG4’s quality is set to old (suspect) and the calculation
  is skipped.

If ARG1’s quality is garbage when ARG3’s value is 1, ARG4 is set to old (suspect) and keeps
current value.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                249                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                     e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

If ARG2’s quality is garbage when ARG3’s value is not 1, ARG4 is set to old (suspect) and
keeps current value.


4.4.5.1.12 Analog Conditional Second Order (CCLC)
There must be exactly four arguments.
ARG1, ARG2, and ARG4 must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 has to be a discrete record type.
If ARG3 = 1 then
    ARG4 = ARG2 * ARG1 * ARG1
Else
    ARG4 = 0
End If

  Note: If ARG3’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), ARG4’s quality is set to old (suspect) and
  calculation is skipped.

If ARG1’s or ARG2’s quality is garbage when ARG3’s value is 1, ARG4’s quality is set to old
(suspect) and keeps current value.


4.4.5.1.13 Analog Status Counter (CNT1)
There must be at least two arguments.
The last argument has to be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
All other arguments have to a discrete record type.
ARGn = number of Argi whose value is 1.


4.4.5.1.14 Analog Threshold Counter (CNT2)
There must be at least three arguments.
All arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARGn’s value is equal to the number of ARGi whose value exceeds (greater than) ARGn-1’s
value.


4.4.5.1.15 Analog Weighted Sum (WSUM)
There must be at least two arguments, and the total number of arguments must be even.
All arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG1 = ARG2 + ARG3 * ARG4 + ARG5 * ARG6 + ...+ ARGn-1 * ARGn


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               250                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

  Note: For ARGi, if the values is inferior to 0.0000000001, it is rounded to 0.0.


4.4.5.1.16 Analog Best of N (BVAL)
There must be three, or more, arguments.
Arguments must be an analog or accumulator record type.
ARGN’s value and quality are set to the value and quality of the best measurement between
ARG1 and ARGN-1.

  Note: The quality is ordered from best to worst.

• GOOD in service
• REPLACED
• SUSPECT
• GOOD but not in service
• Garbage (uninitialized)


4.4.5.1.17 Analog Cotangent (COT)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments should be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = cotangent (ARG1)

  Note: If sinus (ARG1) calculation returns a number close to 0 (less than 1.0E-34), the
  calculation is skipped and ARG2’s quality is set to old (suspect).


4.4.5.1.18 Analog Arctangent (ATAN)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = arctangent (ARG1)


4.4.5.1.19 Analog Sinus (SIN)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = sinus (ARG1)


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               251                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

4.4.5.1.20 Analog Cosinus (COS)
There must be exactly two arguments.

ARG2 = cosinus (ARG1)


4.4.5.1.21 Analog Tangent (TAN)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = tangent (ARG1)

  Note: If ARG1’s value is close to 0, ARG2 is set to old (suspect) and the calculation is
  skipped.


4.4.5.1.22 Analog Natural Log (LOG)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = log (ARG1)

  Note: If ARG1’s value is less than or equal to 0, ARG2 is set to old (suspect) and the
  calculation is skipped.


4.4.5.1.23 Analog Absolute Value (ABS)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = |ARG1|


4.4.5.1.24 Analog Exponent Power Function (EXP)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG 2 = e ARG1

  Note: If ARG1’s value is greater than 88, ARG2 is set to 0 and old (suspect).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               252                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

4.4.5.1.25 Accumulator Alternate Value (ALTC)
There must be at least four arguments.
ARG1 has to be a discrete record type
All others must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 = first ARG4 thru ARGn available, not suspect nor uninitialized
If (new alternate value - previous alternate value) > ARG2 then
    Set ARG1 S-bit TRUE
Else
    Set ARG1 S-bit FALSE
End If
If (fewer than 2 alternates with good quality found) then
    Set ARG1 X-bit TRUE
Else
    Set ARG1 X-bit FALSE
End If


4.4.5.1.26 Analog Alternate Value (ALTA)
Same as Accumulator Alternate Value (see section 4.4.5.1.25 Accumulator Alternate Value
(ALTC)).


4.4.5.1.27 Analog Spike Filter (FLTR)
There must be exactly three arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG3 = ARG3 * (1 - ARG2) + ARG1 * ARG2

  Note: ARG2’s value must be between 0.0 and 1.0; if outside this range, ARG2’s value is
  considered to be 1.0.


4.4.5.1.28 Analog Signed Average Sum Part (ISM2)
There must be exactly five arguments.
All arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = ARG2 + 1
ARG4 = ARG4 - 1


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             253                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

If ARG1 > 0 then
    ARG3 = ARG3 + ARG1
Else
    ARG5 = ARG5 + ARG1

  Note: If ARG1’s quality is uninitialized (garbage), ARG2’s, ARG3’s, ARG4’s, and ARG5’s
  qualities are set to old (suspect).

If any of ARG2’s to ARG5’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), their value is set to 0.0.


4.4.5.1.29 Analog Issue to Setpoint (AI2SPT)
There must be at least four arguments.
All arguments must be an analog, accumulator or real constant type.
If (ARG1 is different from ARG2 by more than ARG3) OR
    (ARG2’s quality neither good or replaced)
    then
         Issue supervisory setpoint to first setpnt of each ARG4
         ARG2 = ARG1
End If

  Note: ARG1’s quality needs to be good or replaced.


4.4.5.1.30 Analog Bus Summation (ABUS)
There must be at least three arguments.
ARG2 must be a discrete type
All other arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant type.
If all ARG3 thru ARGn are of good quality then:
    summ = ARG3 + ARG4 + ... + ARGn
    if (abs(summ) .gt. ARG1) then
         set ARG2 to false
         set ANOMAL on ARG3 thru ARGn
    Else
         set point ARG2 to true
         reset ANOMAL on ARG3 thru ARGn


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                254                                   SCADA Modeling
                                                                     e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    Endif
    Else
         Set ARG2 quality to OLD (suspect)
End If


4.4.5.1.31 Analog Log Base Ten (Not Modeled)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 = log10(ARG1)

  Note: If ARG1’s value is negative or null, ARG2 is set to old (suspect) and calculation is
  skipped.


4.4.5.1.32 Analog Sinus of Degrees (Not Modeled)

  Note: ARG1 is converted to radian to use the sinus function. The result is converted back
  to degrees.


4.4.5.1.33 Analog Cosinus of Degrees (Not Modeled)

  Note: ARG1 is converted to radian to use the cosinus function. The result is converted
  back to degrees.


4.4.5.1.34 Analog Tangent of Degrees (Not Modeled)
There must be exactly two arguments.
Arguments must be an analog, accumulator, or real constant record type.
ARG2 (degree) = tangent (ARG1 - in degree)

                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

  Note: ARG1 is converted to radian to use the tangent function. The result is converted
  back to degrees.


4.4.5.1.35 Analog ArcSinus (Not Modeled)

  Note: If any of ARG1’s, ARG2’s or ARG3’s quality is garbage (uninitialized), ARG5 and ARG4

  Note: ARG1 through ARG3 represent the phases (also called AMPSa, AMPSb, and AMPSc).

4.4.6 Simultaneous and Multiple Control Calculation Functions
Calculation records can also be used to model sequencing of control events. The sections
and illustrations below provide information about the structures that support the
Simultaneous Trip/Close Control function (type MBO1) and the Multiple Trip/Close Control
function (type MBO2).

  Note: For control sequences, no matching Calculation Function record is required.


4.4.6.1 Simultaneous Control Function
In the simultaneous control function, the operator executes a control command sequence
on a single real point and control relays, which, in the field, cause multiple simultaneous
operation of several control points. To confirm control completion of all points, a Calculation
structure similar to that illustrated in Figure 72 is required.
In a simultaneous sequence, the following occurs:
1. The first Command Reference under the Calculation points is issued to the master
   Command record.
2. The master Command is issued, resulting in several controls being executed in the
   power system.
3. The other Command References under the Calculation point are issued to dummy
   Command records, which are never issued; however, their parent Discrete changes
   when the associated control in the field is executed.
Following is the structure of the calculation when deployed to the SCADAMDL application.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              268                                  SCADA Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

 SUBSTN = ALTA
  DEVTYP = CB
   DEVICE = BREAKER_1
    MEAS = CTRL
     POINT = STAT
      CTRL(1) = TRIP
      CTRL(2) = CLOS
   DEVICE = BREAKER_2
    MEAS = CTRL
     POINT = STAT
      CTRL(3) = TRIP
      CTRL(4) = CLOS
   DEVICE = BREAKER_3
    MEAS = CTRL
     POINT = STAT
      CTRL(5) = TRIP
      CTRL(6) = CLOS
   DEVICE = SIM_T&C_1
    MEAS = CTRL
     POINT = STAT
      CTRL(7) = TRIP
      CTRL(8) = CLOS
   DEVICE = SIM_TRIP_1
    MEAS = MBO1
     CTLREF = 7      (SIM_T&C_1 TRIP)
     CTLREF = 5      (BREAKER_3 TRIP)
     CTLREF = 3      (BREAKER_2 TRIP)
     CTLREF = 1      (BREAKER_1 TRIP)
   DEVICE = SIM_CLOSE_1
    MEAS = MBO1
     CTLREF = 8      (SIM_T&C_1 CLOSE)
     CTLREF = 6      (BREAKER_3 CLOSE)
     CTLREF = 4      (BREAKER_2 CLOSE)
     CTLREF = 2      (BREAKER_1 CLOSE)

Figure 72. Simultaneous Breaker Processing
