5.6 Simulation Auto-Generation
This section describes the “Simulation Model Auto-Generation” Workspace Validation
Sequence.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              379                                Simulation Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

e-terrasource allows users to automatically update their current workspace model with a
simulation and generation model, using the “Simulation Model Auto-Generation”
Workspace Validation Sequence.
This auto-generation sequence only adds missing entities or modifies property values. It
does not correct the model by deleting or changing the configuration of the existing model.


5.6.1 Enabling the Auto-Generation of the Simulation Model
To enable the “Simulation Model Auto-Generation” Workspace Validation Sequence, the
Simulation Configuration entity should have its IsAutoBuildEnabled flag set, as shown in the
Figure 102.


Figure 102. Simulation Auto-Build Enabled


  Note: This functionality can only work if you have one and only one Simulation
  Configuration entity. To create one, refer to section 5.2.1.4 Simulation Configuration.

Enabling the Simulation Model auto-build:
• Creates a new Reclose Schedule with its associated Reclose Sequences. If not, at least
  one Reclose Schedule was previously defined.
• Creates a new Synchrocheck Type. If not, at least one Synchrocheck Type was
  previously defined.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              380                               Simulation Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Creates one Default Boiler entity with its IsCoordinatedControl flag set, if this was not
  previously defined.
• Creates one Default Boiler entity with its IsCoordinatedControl flag not set, if this was
  not previously defined.
• Creates one Default Detailed Steam Turbine entity with its IsCoordinatedControl flag set,
  if this was not previously defined.
• Creates one Default Boiler entity with its IsCoordinatedControl flag not set, if this was
  not previously defined.
• Updates the Default Feed-Water Gain, Default Fuel-Air Gain, Feed-Water Gain, and Fuel-
  Air Gain entities, if their count is not equal to 64 for each of them.
• Updates the Simulation properties if they were not previously defined, of the following
  entities:
     – NetworkConfiguration
     – Switch
     – SynchronousMachine
• Allows for correcting the existing Prime-Mover Model to be enabled or not. For details,
  see section 5.6.2 Prime-Mover Auto-Correction.
• Allows the Generation Model Build to be enabled or not. For details, see section 5.6.3
  Generation Model Auto-Build.
• Allows the Prime Mover Model Build to be enabled or not. For details, see section 5.6.4
  Generation Dynamic Auto-Build.
• Allows the Protection Model Build to be enabled or not. For details, see section 5.6.5
  Protection Model Auto-Build.


5.6.2 Prime-Mover Auto-Correction
  Note: This option will tune the Simulation Model, based on the existing Network and
  Generation models.

When enabled, the Existing Prime-Mover Auto-Correction:
• Automatically corrects the existing Generating Unit Model by setting the ForGeneration
  flag to “No” when this unit is not associated with a Resource Controller.
• Automatically corrects the RatedMVA property of the Synchronous Machines based on
  its limits and the limits of its associated Generating Unit, if the ReatedMVA property is
  below the absolute value of the its greatest limit.
• Automatically corrects the Combustion, Hydro, and Steam Turbine Limit and Ramp Rate
  properties.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             381                               Simulation Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Automatically corrects the Fraction PLC Control of the Combustion, Hydro, and Steam
  Turbines based on the existing model.


5.6.3 Generation Model Auto-Build
  Caution: This option is not recommended when using an existing tuned Generation Model.

When enabled, the Generation Model Auto-Build:
• Automatically builds the Generation Configuration entity if it does not currently exist in
  the model.
• Automatically sets the ForGeneration flag to “Yes” for all the Generating Units
  referenced by non-Condenser Synchronous Machines.
• Automatically builds Resource Controllers.
• Automatically sets the ForGeneration flag to “Yes” for all the Substations and Host
  Control Areas that are referenced by Generating Units with their ForGeneration flag set
  to “Yes”.
• Automatically creates the Tie Flow and Transacting Area model based on the Network
  model.
• Automatically creates the Generation Telemetry model if it does not currently exist in
  the model.
• Automatically updates the Control Center information of the Host Control Area based on
  the existing SCADA model.


5.6.4 Generation Dynamic Auto-Build
When enabled, the Generation Dynamic Auto-Build:
• Automatically builds the missing turbines (Combustion Turbine, Hydro Turbine, and
  Steam Turbine) for the Synchronous Machines that are not marked as Condensers.
• Allows the user to enable the auto-build of the Combined Cycle Plant model.
To enable the Generation Dynamic Auto-Build, the IsAutoBuildGenDynEnabled flag should
be set, as shown in Figure 103.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            382                                Simulation Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Figure 103. Generation Dynamic Model Auto-Build Enabled


5.6.4.1 Prime-Mover Auto-Build
When the Generation Dynamic Auto-Build is enabled, the Prime Mover model is
automatically updated by inserting missing turbines.
When a Synchronous Machine is not marked as a Condenser, and does not have a turbine
associated with it, it checks if a Generating Unit is associated with it:
• If it is, it looks at the Generation Type of this Generating Unit and derives the
  appropriate turbine type for this Synchronous Machine.
• If it is not, it uses the Default Turbine Type defined by the user.

  Note: This process only checks on existing Synchronous Machines that are part of the
  Network Model, are not marked as Condensers, and do not currently have a turbine
  associated with it.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              383                                Simulation Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

5.6.4.2 Combined Cycle Plant Model Auto-Build
When Generation Dynamic Auto-Build is enabled, the user can choose to enable the
Combined Cycle Plant Model Auto-Build. To do so, the BuildCombinedCyclePlant flag should
be set.
Based on the existing Generating Unit entities, it will or will not create associated Combined
Cycle Plant entities, as well as the Heat Recovery Boiler and Steam Turbine – Boiler
Association entities.


5.6.5 Protection Model Auto-Build
To enable the Protection Model Auto-Build, the IsAutoBuildRelayEnabled flag should be set,
as shown in the following figure.


Figure 104. Protection Equipment Model Auto-Build Enabled

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              384                              Simulation Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

When enabled, the Protection Model Auto-Build:
• Acknowledges any user auto-build filtering selection.
• Enables the Automatic Switch model on existing Switches.
• Creates new Current Relays and their associated Relay – Switch Association entities.
• Creates new Frequency Relays and their associated Relay – Switch Association entities.
• Creates new Generic Under-Frequency Relays.
• Creates new Impedance Relays and their associated Relay – Switch Association entities.
• Creates new Synchro-Check Relays.
• Creates new Unit Isolation Breakers entities.
• Creates new Voltage Relays and their associated Relay – Switch Association entities.
The Maximum Iteration parameter allows you to define how many steps it will allow the
software to find the appropriate Relay – Switch Association entities for each Relay type.


5.6.5.1 Protection Equipment Build Filtering

  Note: The Protection Model Auto-Build will only consider equipment that is defined under
  the Control Center, if defined. The following filtering options will then only add to the
  Control Center filtering.

The user can define:
• The CB Type that is used to select the appropriate Switches. If no selection is made,
  there is no CB Type auto-build filtering.
• The geographical selection, by:
     – Selecting the Geographical Region where the Protection Equipment auto-build is
       performed.
     – Selecting the Sub-Geographical Region where the Protection Equipment auto-build
       is performed.
     – Selecting the Substation where the Protection Equipment auto-build is performed.

  Note: If Substation filtering is selected along with the Sub-Geographical Region and/or
  Geographical Region filtering, the auto-build follows the Substation filtering. If only the
  Sub-Geographical Region and Geographical Region filtering are selected, the auto-build
  follows the Sub-Geographical Region filtering. If none are selected, no geographical
  filtering is used by the auto-build.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              385                               Simulation Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

5.6.5.2 Automatic Switch Auto-Build
When Protection Model Auto-Build is enabled, you can choose to enable Automatic Switch
Model Auto-Build. To do so, the BuildAutomaticSwitch flag should be set.
When enabled, the automation will find every switch connected directly to an
ACLineSegment and/or SeriesCompensator and decide, based on its topology model and
the auto-build filtering criteria, if this Switch should be considered for the Automatic Switch
model. If it is, it will update the appropriate flags to enable this Switch functionality.


5.6.5.3 Current Relay Auto-Build
When Protection Model Auto-Build is enabled, the user can choose to enable the Current
Relay Model Auto-Build. To do so, the BuildCurrentRelay flag should be set.
When enabled, the user can select which type of conducting equipment the new Current
Relay will protect.

  Caution: The auto-build finds the appropriate Relay – Switch Association entities to
  protect the selected conducting equipment type, following the user CB Type auto-build
  filtering criteria. However, it is highly recommended to not rely only on this tool to define
  the new Current Relay model. An additional check on the newly created entities may be
  needed, due to the specificity of each model.


5.6.5.4 Frequency Relay Auto-Build
When Protection Model Auto-Build is enabled, the user can choose to enable the Frequency
Relay Model Auto-Build. To do so, the BuildFrequencyRelay flag should be set.
When enabled, the user can select which type of conducting equipment the new Frequency
Relay will protect, following the user geographical auto-build filtering criteria.

  Caution: The auto-build finds the appropriate Relay – Switch Association entities to

  the new Frequency Relay model. An additional check on the newly created entities may be
  needed, due to the specificity of each model.

6. Alarm Modeling
The e-terrahabitat Alarm application provides a method of notifying operators, in real time,
of events occurring on their system.
“Events” are changes to the system’s state that are detected by application software. An
application that detects an event can use Alarm to bring the event to the operator’s
attention. An event is usually printed and archived by the Alarm application. It may be
processed as an alarm depending on the attributes modeled in the Alarm model and
attached to the event. An audible and/or visual indicator is used to report the alarm to the
operator. An alarm requires operator acknowledgment and/or deletion.
Each event is typically associated with an object (e.g., an e-terrascada point representing a
circuit breaker, a PROCMAN task). An event is posted by the client application with a set of
attributes. The Alarm application processes the event according to these attributes and the
modeling information described below.
When the Alarm application is configured for a given site, its model must be defined to
reflect the site’s configuration and to obtain the desired behavior during the alarming of
significant events. Most of these modifications to the model occur when the Energy
Management System (EMS) is installed. However, it is fairly common for system managers
to update their Alarm modeling in order to satisfy operator requests (e.g., auto-delete or
multiple acknowledgment features), or to deal with hardware modifications such as new
printers.
The objective of this chapter is to document the various tables that make up the Alarm
model.
For additional information about the e-terrahabitat Alarm application, refer to the Alarm
User’s Guide in the e-terrahabitat documentation set.


6.1 Alarm Displays
Configuration of the alarm model is performed using tree view displays and property
sheets, as well as grid displays.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             389                                   Alarm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

6.2 Alarm Model

6.2.1 Alarm Configuration Parameters
Various Alarm application parameters are explained in further detail below.
• The default settings for Exception, Category, Permission Area, and Location are used
  when an event posted to Alarm has one or more of these fields that are invalid. When
  an invalid field is encountered, it is replaced by the corresponding default value.
• The timer settings determine how often to update information. For performance
  reasons, it is important to set these values at reasonable levels.
• Permit database check rate: The PERMIT settings do not change often, but when they
  do, Alarm should reload them. The recommended setting for this timer is 30 seconds.
  Checking too often results in deteriorated performance. In this scenario, the worst case
  for the new PERMIT settings to take effect is 30 seconds.
• Hdb transaction rate: Information included on displays is based on values in the Hdb
  database; therefore, if this timer is too long, the information displayed may not be
  timely. The recommended setting for this timer is 0.5 seconds.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             392                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• The Alarm List Full is issued when the alarm list has reached a defined percentage. Only
  one alarm is issued when this value is reached, until the alarm list returns to below the
  defined percentage and then exceeds it again.
• Percent to free in full list: When the alarm list becomes 100% full, Alarm automatically
  frees 1% of the alarms in the list by default. Depending on how fast alarms are entering
  the system, this value can be increased to avoid this process repeating over and over.
  Alarm removes the oldest, lowest-priority alarms first and then proceeds to newer,
  higher-priority alarms.
• Operating procedures directory: Specific alarms may have a document attached to
  them that provides additional information. This directory specifies where these
  documents are stored.
• Use special area alarming: Special area alarming defines a set of permission areas for
  which Alarm auto-acknowledges all incoming alarms. The areas included in the list must
  be separated by commas with no spaces in between (Area1,Area2,Area3). The number
  of areas that can be defined is limited to the size of a 76-character text field.
• Number of priorities: This setting is used to notify e-terrabrowser of the number of
  priority buttons to display on the alarm displays. When this value is set to zero, only the
  priority buttons that contain alarms are displayed; otherwise, if all priority buttons are to
  be shown regardless of the alarms in the system, this value is set to the largest priority
  value used. By default, Alarm uses eight priority levels, so this value is set to 8.
• Leave duplicate spaces: By default, the Alarm server removes duplicate spaces from
  the formatted text that is placed in the circular log. When spacing is critical for the
  formatted text, this setting prevents Alarm from removing the duplicate white space in
  the text before placing it into the CIRCLG log.


6.2.2 Applications
The AlarmApplication table identifies the applications that are clients of the Alarm server.
Each client that uses Alarm must have an associated AlarmApplication record defined.
The message set property should specify the name of the file that defines the application’s
MLF alarm messages, without the “.almmsg” extension.


6.2.3 Categories
Alarm categories are used for grouping related exceptions. When an alarm occurs, the
category it belongs to can be displayed on synopsis displays. The AlarmCategory table is
used to specify the options attached to a category, as follows:
• ID: A string used to identify the category.
• Label: A string used to identify the category on the synopsis displays.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                393                                 Alarm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Priority: Defines the priority of the alarms issued in the category. Alarm supports
  priorities from 1 to 8, with 1 being the highest priority.
• Severity: Used to sort the Category and Location buttons on the synopsis displays from
  the lowest (least severe) to the highest (most severe).
• Color: The color chosen for the category is used on the Category button of the synopsis
  displays and the events text.
• Prevent abnormal alarm deletion: Any abnormal alarm issued under this category
  cannot be deleted by an operator action. These alarms can only be deleted by
  auto-delete, multiple delete, or overlay/delete operations or by the RUSER force
  commands.
• Prevent category acknowledgment: This prevents an operator from performing an
  acknowledgment on every alarm issued under the category. This option directly
  corresponds to the RUSER CATACK command.
• Display in system line: If desired, a category can be defined to not appear on the
  synopsis displays.
• When selected, display: Upon selection of the category, the e-terrabrowser command
  specified on the CAT record is executed. The most typical command is to call a display.
• When selected, silence: Silence any tones associated with the category.
• When selected, acknowledge: Acknowledge all the alarms issued in the category.
• FG command: A command that is executed when the Category button is clicked from
  the synopsis or category list displays.
    Two lines are available for the command string to allow for the use of proxy strings. The
    category has two proxy strings available: %CATID% and %CATLABEL%. The %CATID%
    proxy substitutes in the two-letter category ID for the category, and the %CATLABEL%
    proxy substitutes in the category label. The proxies are to be used the same way they
    are used in keysets. It is recommended that %CATID% be set to key3 and %CATLABEL%
    be set to key4.


6.2.4 Default Logs
The AlarmDefaultLog is a child of the AlarmApplication. It identifies the default formatted
log to use for the application. If an AlarmOverrideLog is defined in the exception definition
for a particular event, the event is sent to that log instead; otherwise, it is sent to the log
indicated by the AlarmDefaultLog. More than one default log can be defined under an
AlarmApplication record.
The AlarmDefaultLog has only one field that identifies the name of a formatted log. If an
invalid name is specified, the Alarm validation program does not detect it, but the Alarm
server aborts at startup with a meaningful explanation.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              394                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

6.2.5 Object Definitions
The records in the AlarmObjectDefinition table contain a set of attributes that describe an
alarmable object in an alarm client’s database. These attributes are used by the Alarm
server when processing events associated with the object.
The ID string is used to identify the object definition. Typically, it matches a record type in
the client database.
For example, the e-terrascada application can define a “POINT” AlarmObjectDefinition
record that is used to define the exception definitions associated with events related to
e-terrascada points.
Information regarding the processing of events attached to the object definition:
• Multiple tone suppression: If Yes, the Alarm server does not issue a second tone if a
  tone has already been issued for one of the related alarms.
• Multiple ack: If Yes, acknowledgment of any one of the alarms under the same instance
  of the same object definition causes all the related alarms to be acknowledged.
• Multiple delete: If Yes, deletion of an alarm causes all the alarms under the same object
  definition to be deleted as well.
• Overlay/Ack: If Yes, there can only be one unacknowledged alarm under the object
  definition. A new alarm under the object definition is unacknowledged and the previous
  alarm is automatically acknowledged.
• Overlay/Del: If Yes, there can be only one alarm under the object definition that is either
  unacknowledged or acknowledged. A new alarm under the object definition is
  unacknowledged.


6.2.6 Exceptions
The AlarmExceptionDefinition table consists of a set of attributes that describe a particular
exception. These attributes are used by the Alarm server when processing events reporting
the exception.
The attributes of an exception can be statically modeled, or they can be specified by the
client at the time the exception occurs when “Use API Options” is set to Yes.
The AlarmExceptionDefinition record consists of the following fields:
• ID: A string used to identify the exception record.
• Log message: A string that identifies the message to be used to format the event. This
  ID identifies the proper formatting function within the message set defined either on the
  parent AlarmApplication record or in the overriding Message Set field of the
  AlarmExceptionDefinition record. An invalid ID causes the Alarm validation to produce a
  warning message and the Alarm server to use a default message.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               395                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Overriding message set: A string naming the message set to be used instead of the one
  specified on the parent AlarmApplication record.
• Operating procedure: Specifies a file to display for this alarm when an operator selects
  the URL icon on the alarm. This is designed to guide the operator in the actions to be
  taken when this alarm occurs. The URL icon appears only when this field is defined in
  the database. The directory specification for these files is modeled on the Alarm
  Configuration parameters.
• Inhibit: When Yes, indicates that the alarm for this exception is suppressed.
• Tone: If No, the Alarm server does not issue a tone for the alarm.
• Use API options: Indicates whether the options specified by the client, when it posts the
  event, should be used to process the event. This allows the client application to
  determine the characteristics of the exception at the time it occurs.
• In alarm list: If the API options are not used, this flag is used to decide if the event is an
  alarm or not.
• Auto ack: If set, the incoming alarm is acknowledged automatically, as well as the
  related alarms if “multiple ack” is set on the object definition.
• Auto delete: If set, when the alarm is acknowledged it is also deleted, as well as related
  alarms if “multiple delete” is set on the object definition.
• Allow abnormal alarm deletion: If set, an incoming alarm or event that is not abnormal
  causes deletion restrictions on related alarms to be removed. These related alarms are
  still abnormal, but the operator can delete them.
• Abnormal: Indicates whether the event is abnormal or not. Abnormal events appear
  with a red time field on the alarm displays; normal events have a black time field. If Yes,
  the alarm is forced to always be abnormal. If No, the alarm is forced to always be
  normal. If it is set to Conditional, the client issuing the alarm is responsible for
  determining the normal/abnormal state of the alarm.


6.2.7 Override Logs
The AlarmOverrideLog record is a child of the AlarmExceptionDefinition record. It identifies
a formatted log used to log events that are posted with the exception definition. Multiple
AlarmOverrideLog records can be specified under the same exception. When
AlarmOverrideLog records are defined under an exception, the formatted log specified by
the AlarmDefaultLog record at the AlarmApplication level is ignored.
The AlarmOverrideLog record has only one field that identifies the name of a formatted log.
If an invalid name is specified, the Alarm validation program does not detect it, but the
Alarm server aborts at startup with a meaningful explanation.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              396                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

6.2.8 Locations
The AlarmLocation table identifies a location. Locations are one of the keys used by Alarm
to classify alarms. Every client specifies a location when it posts an event, and the Alarm
server maintains lists of alarms for every location. Locations usually match the list of
e-terrascada substations in the system.
However, it is fairly common to have a few additional AlarmLocation records that are used
for events related to the control center (Cfgman or PROCMAN alarms, for example). If no
location is specified when an event is issued, a default location modeled in the Alarm
database is used.
The AlarmLocation record consists of the following fields:
• ID: A string identifying the location.
• Display in system line: If Yes, the location appears on the Synopsis display.
• FG command: The FG command to be executed when a user selects this location from
  the Synopsis display. Two lines are used to define the command in order to make use of
  proxy strings. The %LOCID% proxy substitutes the location name for the proxy and
  needs to be set to key201.


6.2.9 Horns
The AlarmHorn table identifies a PC name where the e-terrabrowser client is running. Every
PC that is used as an e-terrabrowser client should be modeled.
The AlarmHorn record consists of the following fields:
• ID: A string identifying the horn in the Alarm database.
• Computer name: This specifies the computer to which the audio command is to be sent.
  This is the network name of the computer.
• Silence area: This permission area is used when a silence command is received from the
  computer to which the horn is attached. The user needs to have audible permissions for
  this area in order to silence the tones.
The AlarmHornSilence record is used to specify additional horns to silence when the parent
horn receives a silence request. There are no permission checks for these silences, but the
parent horn must have audible permissions for its silence area to silence the additional
horns.


6.2.10 Tones
The AlarmTone table identifies a wave file to be sounded by the e-terrabrowser client. The
AlarmTone record is a child of the AlarmHorn record. Since a tone only identifies a wave file
to be played, a horn can have any number of tones.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             397                                   Alarm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Tones can be associated with categories and/or exceptions. Such associations are made to
identify which tone(s), if any, should be sounded for incoming alarms. The exception
definition and the category used to issue the alarm are the keys to decide which tone to
sound.
The AlarmTone record consists of the following fields:
• Wave file name: A string matching the name of a file located in the AudioAlarm
  directory.
• Single stroke: If Yes, the wave file is played once. If No, the wave file is played
  continuously until it is silenced by the operator.


6.2.11 Tones by Category
The AlarmCategoryTone table is used to identify the tone(s) to play when an alarm in a
particular category occurs. For a given category, one AlarmCategoryTone record should be
created for each AlarmTone that should be played.


6.2.12 Tones by Exception
The AlarmExceptionTone table is used to identify the tone(s) to play when a particular
exception occurs. For a given exception, one AlarmExceptionTone record should be created
for each AlarmTone that should be played.


6.2.13 Queues
The AlarmLogmanQueue table identifies Logman queues to use for printing events.
The AlarmLogmanQueue record has only one field that identifies the name of a Logman
queue.
If an invalid name is specified, the Alarm validation program does not catch the error. An
invalid name is one that does not match one of the queues defined in the LOGMAN
database. It is only when Alarm tries to print an event on that invalid queue that an error
message is logged in the Alarm message log.
The AlarmQueueArea table defines the permission areas that filter the events sent to the
logger.
The AlarmQueueArea records are associated with AlarmLogmanQueue records using the
AlarmQueueAreaQueue table. If there are no permission areas associated with a Logman
queue, all events are printed.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              398                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

6.3 Setting Up Horns and Tones
To configure horns and tones in the Alarm model for issuing and silencing tones, the
following steps should be followed:
1. Create the AlarmHorn and AlarmTone records.
2. Create AlarmCategoryTone records to define the tone(s) to issue when the Alarm server
   processes an alarm with a given category.
3. Create AlarmExceptionTone records to define the tone(s) to issue when the Alarm server
   processes an alarm with a given exception.
In addition, the following configurations can be done at the object definition, exception, and
category levels:
• AlarmObjectDefinition: If the Multiple Tone Suppression flag is set to Yes, when a new
  alarm for this object is processed with a tone to sound, the Alarm server checks to see if
  there is already at least one unacknowledged alarm for the same object. In that case,
  the tone is not issued.
• AlarmExceptionDefinition: If the Issue Tone flag is set to No, no tone is issued for an
  alarm associated with this exception.
• AlarmCategory: If the When Selected, Silence flag is set to Yes, when the Category
  button is clicked, the tones associated with this category are silenced, if the user has the
  AUDIBLE permission for the silence area defined on the Horn record.


6.4 Simple Return to Normal Scenario
This example is intended to show how to model Alarm so that alarms designed to notify
users of an abnormal state are automatically acknowledged or deleted when the state
returns to normal.
In this example, an analog alarm is used to demonstrate an analog value that crosses a
high threshold and signals an abnormal alarm. The analog then returns below the threshold
back into its proper value range and signals a Return to Normal alarm. In many cases, once
the Return to Normal alarm has been issued, the previous abnormal alarm can be
automatically removed.
For this example, Prevent Abnormal Alarm Deletion is set on the category for the abnormal
alarm. This option prevents an operator from deleting the alarm; however, it can still be
acknowledged. The only way this alarm can be deleted is for another alarm with the same
Object Identifier to be issued with an Object Definition having the Multiple Delete option set.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             399                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Figure 108. Simple Return to Normal Example

• Abnormal Alarm Settings
     – The analog object definition has the Multiple Delete option on.
     – The category definition has the Prevent Abnormal Alarm Deletion option on.
     – The exception definition has the Auto-Delete option off.
     – Issue the alarm with a specific object identifier number.
     – Acknowledge the alarm from an alarm display.
     – Ensure that the alarm cannot be deleted.
• Return to Normal Alarm Settings
     – The analog object definition is the same as the abnormal alarm.
     – The category definition has the Prevent Abnormal Alarm Deletion option off.
     – The exception definition has the Auto-Delete option on.
     – Issue the alarm with the same object identifier as the abnormal alarm.
If there are two alarms in the list, related based on the same object identifier, when the
Return to Normal alarm is acknowledged, the auto-delete function deletes it and any other
related alarms with the same object identifier, including the Abnormal alarm.
If the Abnormal alarm remains unacknowledged when the Return to Normal alarm is
acknowledged, the Abnormal alarm is not deleted. To compensate for this, set the multiple
ack and multiple delete settings on the object definition.
If the user does not need to be alerted about these alarms once they return to normal,
setting Auto-Acknowledge and Auto-Delete on the exception definition removes the Return
to Normal alarm and the previous Abnormal alarms without any user interaction
whatsoever.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              400                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

6.5 Complex Return to Normal Scenario
This example is designed to show an analog that passes through multiple threshold ranges
and overwrites the previous alarm with the latest alarm.
For this example, three thresholds are used and, at any given time, only one alarm is
displayed. Once the analog returns to its normal state, the notifying alarm is automatically
acknowledged by the alarm process.


Figure 109. Complex Return to Normal Example

• Threshold Violation Alarm Settings
     – The analog object definition has the Overlay Delete option on.
     – The exception definition has no options selected.
     – The category definition has no options selected.
     – Issue the alarm with a specific object identifier number.
• Return to Normal Alarm Settings
     – The analog object definition has the Overlay Delete option on.
     – The exception definition has the Auto-Acknowledge option set.
     – The category definition has no options selected.
     – Issue the alarm with the same object identifier as the violation alarm.
When the Threshold 2 level is crossed, a Threshold Violation alarm is issued. When the
analog drops into Threshold 1, a second Threshold Violation alarm is issued, which
acknowledges and deletes the first alarm. When the analog enters the Threshold 3 range, a
Violation alarm is issued that acknowledges and deletes the second alarm. Finally, the
analog enters the Normal operating range and a Return to Normal alarm is issued; this
acknowledges and deletes the Violation alarm, and then auto-acknowledges itself.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page               401                                   Alarm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

At any given time in the span of this example, only one alarm is displayed in the alarm list.
Any user acknowledgments or deletions of the Violation alarms have no effect on the final
results.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             402                                    Alarm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.3 e-terracomm Model

7.3.1 e-terracomm Servers
Because many systems have more than one e-terracomm server (each with its own model),
each server is represented by a separate server (CommServer) record. All e-terracomm
modeling is performed on a server-by-server basis.
When importing a model, the server name defaults to “Server1”.
When exporting a model, you can specify the name of the server to export. This also
defaults to “Server1”.


7.3.1.1 Importing Multiple Servers
The “EMS Import – All” sequence is designed to import a set of validated, cross-mapped
e-terrahabitat models and produce a federated, properly linked model. If you import
SCADAMOM and OAGMOM together during an “EMS Import – All” operation, the resulting
CommDataItemName records will be linked to the corresponding Analog, Discrete, and
Accumulator records during the transformation step.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             405                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

If you have more than one e-terracomm server that you want to manage with
e-terrasource, you can import the OAGMOM for one server together with SCADAMOM. You
can then run “EMS Import – All” for each additional e-terracomm server, specifying a
different CommServer name on each import until all OAGMOM models have been imported.
Then, you can use the sample Link_CommDataItemName_Measurement.sql script to link
the CommDataItemName records to the Analog, Discrete and Accumulator records. This
script assumes that the CommDataItemName.Name field contains the SCADAMOM
composite ID of the target measurement, with a period (.) used as a delimiter.


7.3.1.2 Exporting Multiple Servers
Upon installation, e-terrasource is configured to export a single e-terracomm server. If your
system must support multiple servers, you can modify the import/export metadata to
export up to nine e-terracomm servers.
To do so, use the Administration Explorer to browse to Import/Export > Types. In the “Java
Transform CIM/XML to All” type, expand the Targets folder, and then for each target,
expand the Parameters folder.
You will find parameters with the following names:
 Parameter Name               Parameter Value
 DestFileOagmom               [%WorkspaceId]_[%UserId]_oagmom.oagmom
 CommServer                   Server1
You can add additional pairs of these parameters for each additional server to export. For
example, if you have a total of three e-terracomm servers, you would add the following
parameters:
 Parameter Name               Parameter Value
 DestFile1Oagmom              [%WorkspaceId]_[%UserId]_oagmom1.oagmom
 CommServer1                  <second CommServer name>
 DestFile2Oagmom              [%WorkspaceId]_[%UserId]_oagmom2.oagmom
 CommServer2                  <third CommServer name>
Simply increment the number in each parameter name for each additional server you want
to export, up to a maximum of nine.
Note that the file extension for all of the DestFile<n>Oagmom parameters must be
“.oagmom”.

7.3.2 e-terracomm Configuration Parameters
The default buffering time and the grace period for reception are used as defaults for their
corresponding CommDataSet fields.
• Default buffering time: Default number of seconds to wait after an exception has
  triggered an output data set, before shipping the triggered data set (accommodates
  bursts of exceptions). Can be overridden by filling the EXCEPT BUFFER field on the
  CommDataSet. Value must be 0 or a positive number not greater than 99.
• Grace period for reception: Default percentage of the periodicity or integrity interval to
  wait before declaring an input dataset to be late. Can be overridden by filling the
  PERIODIC GRACE field on the CommDataSet. Value must be between 0 and 100%.
e-terracomm can be configured to write the data items’ value, quality, time stamp, change
of value counter, and time received in the database so they can be displayed.
• Automatic: The update is done periodically at the specified periodicity. The update is
  actually done only when changes have occurred since the last update.
    As e-terracomm is not the place where values are normally checked, except for
    debugging purposes, the periodicity can be fairly large. For databases with large
    numbers of data items, GE strongly recommends setting the database update to
    Manual. Also note that, when set to Automatic, clicking the Update button on the
    displays where data items are shown forces the update.
• Manual: The update is performed on operator request (Pokepoint button).
Note that in no cases are data values and quality changes lost. The current value and
quality are maintained in memory. The difference is that, when writing periodically, changes
of value and quality can be seen on the displays (data items or data set contents) without
operator intervention. When writing periodically, and depending on the periodicity, some
changes may not be seen.
The update mode and periodicity can be modified at run time.
The following parameters relate to Priority Pools (for more information, see section
7.3.10 Priority Pools):
• Priority Pool processing enabled: This flag can be changed to enable or disable the
  Priority Pool feature. Priority Pools are used to organize CommRemotes into prioritized
  groups to control the order in which connections to remotes are established. At least
  one pool must be modeled (with only one pool, the enabling of the remotes is the same
  as when Priority Pool processing is disabled).
• Failed remotes temporarily NISed: If checked, the remotes of a pool that are unable to
  connect/handshake during the modeled Max Time for the pool are disabled until all
  pools are processed. If not checked, the remotes of a pool that are unable to
  connect/handshake during the modeled Max Time for the pool are left enabled so they
  can continue trying.

                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.3.3 Link Applications
Link applications are the programs that implement a communication protocol. They form
the link between OAGSERVE (the e-terracomm data server) and a remote partner.
The following link applications are available in e-terracomm:
• ISDLINK implements the InterSite Data protocol, a proprietary protocol, using NETIO.
• ICCPLINK implements the Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol over TCP/IP.
• FILELINK implements a simple file-based protocol by reading an ASCII data file written
  on the e-terracomm system. Any suitable means to copy a file from one computer to
  another can be used.
• HABCLINK transfers data into and out of e-terrahabitat databases through HABConnect
  Sampler over TCP/IP.
• ELCOLINK implements the ELCOM-90 Protocol using X.25 or TCP/IP transport.
You can change, add, or remove CommLinkApplication records as needed. After choosing
the link application type, only ISDLINK and ICCPLINK have other fields that require
modeling.


7.3.3.1 ISDLINK
The only parameter that can be configured is the staggering timer.
Staggering Timer: To avoid having all the remotes connecting, downloading the
configuration, and creating data sets at the same time at startup or after a failover, it is
possible to set a timer that delays the enabling of the remotes. The staggering applies on
both e-terracomm and EMS failover. The first remote (in database order) is enabled as soon
as ISDLINK is ready, the second remote is enabled after the staggering time, the third after
twice the staggering time, and so on.
The value of this timer depends on how much data is downloaded; therefore, it is probably
necessary to experiment before finding the right value. A value too low voids the advantage
of the staggering, and a value too high delays the data exchange for the last remotes with
no reason. The value can be left to 0 (no staggering) for small systems.

  Note: For the staggering to work properly on EMS failover, the value of the retry timer
  should be set to at least the time between the disconnection from the enabled host to the
  reconnection to the new enabled host. Experimentation may be necessary.

Values between 1 and 99 are interpreted as seconds, and values between 100 and 999 are
interpreted as milliseconds. The values cannot be changed at run time.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            408                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.3.3.2 ICCPLINK

7.3.3.2.1 Flow Control
There are two types of end-to-end flow control:
• In normal operation (after associations are established and initial handshaking is done),
  only data sets are exchanged. Sending data sets via ICCP is an operation not requiring a
  response from the receiving side (in MMS, this is an “unconfirmed request”). If, for any
  reason, the receiving side does not process the received data sets at the same pace as
  they are sent, the data set messages can back up in the sender and eventually lead to
  an ICCPLINK crash because of memory resource limits.
    To avoid this situation, ICCPLINK implements an “end-to-end flow control” mechanism.
    e-terracomm can be configured so that, every T1 seconds, ICCPLINK checks whether
    the remote site is processing the data set messages in a timely manner. If the remote
    site is not processing the data in a timely manner, ICCPLINK aborts the association with
    the remote that is not responding.
• It is also possible that a remote site does not respond at all to a request that requires a
  response, such as a connection request or a read of a data item. In this case, ICCPLINK
  can be configured to timeout after T2 seconds. If one of these requests times out,
  ICCPLINK aborts the association with the remote that is not responding. When the
  association is aborted, all pending messages are lost.

  Important Note: Unanswered requests (T2) might also be an indication of network
  problems, such as discarded packets happening when exceeding the contracted
  bandwidth. Frequent disconnections triggered by the end-to-end flow control should
  prompt you to check with your WAN provider.

If T1 is set to a value <= 0 or not filled, ICCPLINK uses 120 seconds. Note that T1 is not a real
“keep-alive” timer; therefore, it should be a fairly large value (e.g., >= 30 seconds). T2 should
be set to a value smaller than T1 (e.g., 15 seconds). If T2 is set to a value <= 0 or not filled,
ICCPLINK uses 0.5 * T1 seconds.
T1 and T2 are used for all ICCPLINK remotes, but the flow control can be enabled/disabled
on a remote basis.
T1 and T2 can be changed at run time, as described in the e-terracomm User’s Guide –
Real-Time Operation.


7.3.3.2.2 MMS Queue Parameters
MMS-EASE V7.x implements a flow control mechanism (independent of the ICCPLINK
end-to-end flow control). This mechanism is intended to prevent ICCPLINK from
overwhelming the OSI stack with requests.
In ICCPLINK, confirmed requests and information reports pass through a queue before
being sent (the queue is necessary to maintain request and information report order).

Proprietary – See Copyright Page               409                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Before retrieving a message from the queue, ICCPLINK checks if there are enough stack
resources available. If enough resources are available, the message is sent. If not, the
message remains on the queue and ICCPLINK tries to send the message later.
Queue Timer T1: Time (in milliseconds) before sending the next message when there are
resources available to send the current one. The recommended value is 50 ms.
Queue Timer T2: Time (in milliseconds) before re-sending the same message when there
were not enough resources available to send it. The recommended value is 100 ms.
Queue Max Size: Maximum number of messages queued. If the queue reaches this number
of messages, ICCPLINK aborts the association with the remote site; this cleans up the queue
(purge) and all stack resources. The recommended value is 100. The maximum is 500.
Queue Max Resources: Number of stack resources available allowing ICCPLINK to send a
message. If the number of resources available is lower than this value, ICCPLINK leaves the
message on the queue and waits Queue Timer T2 milliseconds. The recommended value
is 4.
The MMS Queue parameters can be changed at run time, as described in the e-terracomm
User’s Guide – Real-Time Operation.


7.3.3.2.3 MMS Queue Statistics
Statistics about stack resources availability and about the MMS Queue can be printed
periodically and/or every time an association with a remote site is lost. Statistics are printed
in the ICCPLINK application log file (stdout). Printing is enabled/disabled on a remote basis
(see the remote configuration in ICCPLINK).
Statistic Timer: Periodicity at which statistics are printed (when periodic printing is enabled;
see ICCPLINK). Defaults to 60 minutes if <= 0 or not filled.
The value can be changed at run time, as described in the e-terracomm User’s Guide –
Real-Time Operation. When the value is changed at run time, it is taken into account only
after the current timer elapses. For example, if the timer was 60 minutes and it is changed
to 10 minutes, it can take up to 60 minutes, if the timer just restarted, for changing to
10 minutes.
Staggering Timer: To avoid having all the remotes connecting and creating data sets at the
same time at startup or after a failover, it is possible to set a timer that delays the enabling
of the remotes. The first remote (database order) is enabled as soon as ICCPLINK is ready,
the second remote is enabled after the staggering time, the third after twice the staggering
time, and so on. The value of this timer depends on how many data sets (average) each
remote creates; it is probably necessary to experiment before finding the right value. A
value too low voids the advantage of the staggering, and a value too high delays the data
exchange for the last remotes with no reason. The value can be left to 0 (no staggering) for
small systems.
Values between 1 and 99 are interpreted as seconds, and values between 100 and 999 are
interpreted as milliseconds. The value cannot be changed at run time.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              410                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.3.3.2.4 AR Names
TCP AR Name: At least one TCP/IP local AR name must be modeled. It is possible to
configure more than one TCP/IP local AR name for specific situations that are described in
the e-terracomm & e-terracontrol SISCO Stack and MMS Security Configuration Guide.
The value must match the local AR name(s) for TCP/IP transport configured in MMS EASE.
For details about the MMS-EASE configuration, refer to the e-terracomm & e-terracontrol
SISCO Stack and MMS Security Configuration Guide. The value can be entered literally or as
an environment variable.
It is better to use an environment variable on dual redundant systems, because you are
able to have exactly the same savecase on both machines, the actual AR name being the
translation of the variable.


7.3.4 Legal Applications
The CommLegalApplication table is used only for HABCLINK. For HABCLINK, a
CommDataSet must be associated with an application on the remote.
The legal application ID is the name of the target database, and the e-terrahabitat
application in which it is found. Each HABCLINK set can reference only items within a single
database within a single application. The legal application ID is entered as
“database,application”.


7.3.5 Communications Topology
The communication topology describes the quantity of and various qualities about the
connections between e-terracomm and remote communications partners. This topology is
represented by a hierarchy of three record types:
• CommRemote: Describes a remote communications partner: an entity with which you
  want to exchange data, such as another control center or a local EMS system. That
  partner can be across the state or country, or just across the room.
• CommLink: Models a virtual connection to a remote communications partner. The
  number of links that are modeled corresponds to the number of simultaneous
  connections that you want to communicate on with that partner.
• CommPath: Designates the actual connection instances that are possible for a
  CommLink. When multiple CommPath records occur under a CommLink record, the link
  application accepts or makes a connection on only one of the CommPaths at a time.
The modeling of the communications topology varies depending on the communications
protocol. For details, refer to the following sections.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            411                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.3.5.1 ICCPLINK
ICCP connections are categorized as either “single-direction association” or “dual-direction
association”.
Single-direction associations require one link for the client and one link for the server if data
is exchanged in both directions. Each link has one or two paths depending on whether the
remote system is redundant or not. Single-direction associations with one-way data
exchange require only one link with one or two paths. All paths under a given link must
have the same setting for the master and single-direction association properties.
Dual-direction associations require one link, typically with two paths to represent a dual
redundant remote system.
For either configuration, the number of paths under a link is not limited to two. As many
paths as necessary can be configured to support backup control centers, for example, but
only one path is active at a time.
Valid configurations are:
• Single-direction association (all paths have the single-direction association set with a
  maximum of two links; it is possible to have only one link when data is exchanged only
  one way).
      Remote
      +-- Link
      |   +-- Path (master)
      |   +-- Path (master)
      |
      +-- Link
          +-- Path (slave)
          +-- Path (slave)


• Dual-direction association (all paths have the single-direction association reset).
      Remote
      +-- Link
          +-- Path (master or slave)
          +-- Path (master or slave)


7.3.5.1.1 CommRemote
The following information applies to modeling ICCP CommRemote records.
• Name: Identification of the remote site. This is an arbitrary name with a length
  <= 16 characters. It is recommended that the name be limited to 14 characters because
  this remote identification is used to create the device part of a status data item ISD
  name, which has a maximum length of 14.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              412                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

      Note: Prior to e-terracomm 2.3, the remote name was also the remote domain name.
      The remote domain name now has its own field (see below) where the name can be
      entered in mixed case with up to 32 characters as per the ICCP specification.

• Description: Brief description of the remote site.
• Remote type: Picklist to select the link application that the remote belongs to. Set this to
  ICCP Link.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• Remote domain: This is the name of the MMS domain created for the remote site. The
  remote site refers to this name when requesting data. The MMS domain name is an
  MMS identifier, and thus it must begin with a letter and contain only the characters
  [a...z], [A...Z], [0...9], $, and _ (underscore). The length must be <= 32 characters.

      Note: If left unfilled, the remote name is used. However, the use of an environment
      variable is no longer supported.

• Protocol version: The ICCP version the remote is using. Versions 1996-08 and 2000-08
  are supported. If the version selected here does not match the actual version the
  remote is using, the connection is aborted.
• Bilateral table ID: Version identifier of the bilateral table agreement for this remote. The
  version is exchanged between communicating sites and must be the same. This is a
  character string with a length <= 32 characters.

      Note: Prior to e-terracomm 2.1, the bilateral table ID was configured in the Version
      field of the TBLVER record (Bilateral Tables display). Starting with e-terracomm 2.1, you
      model the bilateral table ID directly on the remote record.

• Max scan rate: The maximum rate (in seconds) e-terracomm is allowed to send output
  data sets to that remote node. Not used for input data sets.
• Print statistics: Select the conditions under which MMS Queue statistics are printed.
• Log data set creation error: When a remote site creates a data set or the local site
  creates a data set at the remote site, the list of data items not found or without Read
  permission, if any, can be logged.
• Max transfer sets: The number of transfer sets that may be active at one time.
  Recommended value: the maximum number of data sets that are served to the remote
  site (output data set), including future expansions.
• Client/server flow control: Specifies whether ICCPLINK end-to-end flow control is
  disabled or enabled. Flow control can be disabled on a client/server path basis. If the
  path(s) under the remote is dual (one path for both client and server), disabling either
  client or remote disables the flow control. If the path(s) is single, flow control is disabled
  only on the selected path(s).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              413                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

      Note: When the flow control is enabled for the server, ICCPLINK periodically sends an
      identification request on the server path of a single association. Some ICCP
      implementations do not support receiving requests in such a configuration. In this
      case, you must disable the flow control for the server.

• Drop hung slave associations: When set, this flag allows ICCPLINK to drop slave
  associations that seems to be hung. If the remote site sends association requests while
  ICCPLINK thinks that the association is already up, after three association requests,
  ICCPLINK drops the current one and creates a new one. This flag can be changed at run
  time.
• Supplemental data types with 1996-08 protocol: When enabled, this option allows
  ICCPLINK to exchange data types that were created for ICCP 2000-08 while the version
  is set to 1996-08. Obviously, the remote must be able to receive and/or send those data
  types.


7.3.5.1.2 CommLink
The following information applies to modeling ICCP CommLink records.
• Name: Identification of the link record. This character string is limited to 16 characters
  or fewer, with no embedded blanks. It is recommended that the length be limited to 14
  because this link identification is used to create the device part of a status data item ISD
  name, which has a maximum length of 14 characters.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• Retry timeout: How often (in seconds) the master paths under this link are retried when
  none is connected.


7.3.5.1.3 CommPath
The following information applies to modeling ICCP CommPath records.
• Name: Identification of the path. This character string is limited to 16 characters or
  fewer if the path is not registered with Configuration Manager; otherwise, the length is
  limited to 8 characters. If not registered, it is recommended that the length be limited to
  14 because this path identification is used to create the device part of a status data
  item ISD name, which has a maximum length of 14 characters.
• Register with Configuration Manager: Whether this path is registered with the
  Configuration Manager (configured as a device). For details about configuring paths in
  the Configuration Manager database, refer to the e-terracomm Software Installation
  and Maintenance Guide.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• Transport method: TCP/IP. This is the only transport allowed.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             414                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Master: This indicates whether the association with the remote is initiated locally or at
  the remote site.
• Single-direction association: In a single-direction association, the path acts as a client
  (if Master is Yes) or as a server (if Master is No). In a dual-direction association, the path
  acts as a client and server at the same time; the Master flag only specifies who initiates
  the association.
• Remote AR name: Must match one of the remote AR names configured in MMS-EASE for
  the transport selected. For details about configuring MMS-EASE (for TCP/IP AR name
  only), refer to the e-terracomm & e-terracontrol SISCO Stack and MMS Security
  Configuration Guide. The value can be entered literally or as an environment variable.
• Local AR: Indicates which local AR name to use to form the association with the remote
  AR name.
• Domain name: This is the name of the MMS domain on the remote accessible to the
  local site. The MMS domain name is an MMS identifier, and thus it must begin with a
  letter and contain the characters [a...z], [A...Z], [0...9], $, and _ (underscore) only. The
  value can be entered literally or as an environment variable.


7.3.5.2 ISDLINK
The sections below describe the communications topology modeling for InterSite Data (ISD)
communications.


7.3.5.2.1 CommRemote
The following information applies to the modeling of ISD CommRemote records.
• Name: Identification of the remote, usually a local host (EMS system). The value can be
  entered literally or as an environment variable. This is an arbitrary name with a length
  <= 16 characters. It is recommended that the name be limited to 14 characters because
  this remote identification is used to create the device part of a status data item ISD
  name, which has a maximum length of 14.
• Description: Brief description of the remote.
• Remote type: Picklist to select which link application the remote belongs to. Set this to
  ISD Link.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• ISD max scan rate: The maximum rate (in seconds) e-terracomm is allowed to send
  output data sets to the remote node. Not used for input data sets.
• MCD processing: Picklist to select the type of multiple change detection processing
  done by ISDLINK (see section 7.5 MCD Processing).
     – None: No MCD processing.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               415                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

     – Delta Count: Use a change of value counter. The counter reflects the number of
       changes since the last update.
     – Running Count: Use a change of value counter. The counter reflects the number of
       changes since the first time the value was sent.
     – Data Discrete: Use an integer value to add the MCD flag to a 2- to 4-state status
       value.
• ISD protocol version: The ISD version that ISDLINK tries to use. When a link is
  established, the version is negotiated, so the actual version used may change.
  Specifying the same version as the EMS host version speeds up the initialization.
  Supported versions are:
     – Version 5.0: For data exchange with e-terracomm, this version is the same as
       version 4.0 plus the ability to pass tag values (none, block open, block close, block
       open and close) and expected values for status points. On the EMS side, this version
       is available beginning with e-terrascada 2.4.
     – Version 4.0: This version has better quality mapping than the previous versions, and
       the ability to add and remove requested points without the need of a full download.
       Data exchanged can be time stamped. Analogs and counts are exchanged using
       IEEE floating point numbers. This version can be used with e-terrascada 2.2 or later
       (see section 7.7 InterSite Data 4.0).
     – Version 3.0: Analogs and counts are exchanged using IEEE floating point numbers
       (native mode for e-terrascada 2.x and e-terracomm 2.x).
     – Version 2.0: Analogs and counts are exchanged using VAX floating point numbers
       (native mode for e-terrascada 1.5.x).
     – Version 1.0: Same as 2.0 but for e-terrascada 1.4.x.
• Send BAD data to EMS: If set to Yes, data with bad quality is not sent to the EMS (it is
  treated as garbage quality data). This flag does not need to be used with ISD 4.0 or 5.0
  because the “BAD” quality can be transmitted to the EMS (see section 7.6 Filtering Bad
  Data).


7.3.5.2.2 CommLink
The following information applies to the modeling of ISD CommLink records.
• Name: Identification of the link. This is an arbitrary name with a length <= 16 characters.
  It is recommended that the name be limited to 14 characters because this link
  identification is used to create the device part of a status data item ISD name, which
  has a maximum length of 14.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• ISD retry timeout: How long (in seconds) after a connection is lost ISDLINK waits before
  trying to reconnect. If using staggering, all the ISDLINK remotes should have the same
  retry timeout, and its value should be the time necessary for the EMS failover to

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             416                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    complete (i.e., the time elapsed between the disconnection from the old enabled host
    and the time the new enabled host is ready to make connections).
• Usage: Picklist to select the type of data exchanged on this link:
     – SCADA data (analogs, status, and counts)
     – SCADA controls (digital controls and setpoints)
     – Information messages (equivalent to ICCP Block 4)
     – Account messages and requests (equivalent to ICCP Block 8)


7.3.5.2.3 CommPath
The following information applies to the modeling of ISD CommPath records.
• Name: Identification of the path. This character string is limited to 16 characters or
  fewer if the path is not registered with Configuration Manager; otherwise, the length is
  limited to 8 characters. If not registered, it is recommended that the length be limited to
  14 because this path identification is used to create the device part of a status data
  item ISD name, which has a maximum length of 14 characters.
• Register with Configuration Manager: Whether this path is registered with the
  Configuration Manager (configured as a device). For details about configuring paths in
  the Configuration Manager database, refer to the e-terracomm Software Installation
  and Maintenance Guide.
• In service: In/out of service default setting (can be changed at run time).
• NETIO source object definition: This is the name of the source NETIO object for
  e-terracomm. On the remote side (usually the EMS host), a NETIO destination object with
  the same name must exist. The value can be entered literally or as an environment
  variable.
• NETIO destination object definition: This is the name of the destination NETIO object for
  e-terracomm, and it must correspond to the NETIO source object on the remote side
  (usually the EMS host). The value can be entered literally or as an environment variable.

  Note: Even when ISDLINK connects to a dual redundant EMS host, only one path is needed
  because only the EMS host having the primary role tries to form a connection. ISDLINK
  does not try alternative paths; instead, it tries to open a connection on all enabled paths if
  more than one is configured. This creates a duplicated path and ISDLINK aborts. Some
  e-terracomm installations need to have alternate connections to more than one EMS host
  (e.g., to a primary control center and to an emergency/backup control center). In this case,
  more than one path can be configured but only one at a time can be enabled. Switching
  from one control center to another requires that an operator disable the path to the
  current control center, then enable the path to the alternate control center.

7.3.5.3 HABCLINK
The sections below describe the communications topology modeling for HABCLINK.

The following information applies to the modeling of HABCLINK CommRemote records.

  send output data sets to the remote node. Not used for input data sets.

  when none is connected.

• File operation: This field indicates whether the data is to be read from the file or written
  to the file.
• Multiple periods per file: This field indicates whether the data file contains multiple
  samples of data for each point or a single sample of the data.
• Number of periods per file: This field indicates how many periods to read/write in a
  “Multiple Periods per File” file.
• Preserve input file: This field is relevant only when the file operation is Read. It is for use
  in the special circumstance where it is desired to use FILELINK as a simulator to replay
  the same data over and over from an input file.
    This field should not be selected if you are doing FTP because FILELINK normally deletes
    the INPUT file so that it stops processing until the next file (which has the same name)
    comes in. If you want to archive your received files, do not use this option; use the
    archive directory option described below.
• File name: This value can be entered literally or as an environment variable, but it may
  need to be an environment variable since the field is limited to 32 characters. No
  embedded blanks are allowed.
     – For Read: The value is the complete file name specification (including the path) of the
       input data file. Redundant data files can be modeled by making this environment

       variables for FILELINK, see the note below).

Proprietary – See Copyright Page              420                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                   e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

        FILELINK first attempts to read the first file name, and it only attempts to read the
        second value (filename) if the attempt to open the first file fails.
     – For Write: The value is the complete file name specification (including the path) of
       the intermediate output data file. Redundant data files can be modeled by making
       this environment variable multi-valued (for details about how to configure
       multi-valued environment variables for FILELINK, see the note below).
        FILELINK first attempts to write the first file name, and it only attempts to write the
        second value (filename) if the attempt to open the first file fails. If the file already
        exists, it is overwritten. When the output file is filled, it is closed and immediately
        renamed to a file with the same name postfixed with the indicator “_0” (only if the
        file does not already exist). An application processing the _0 output file should either
        rename or delete it when it is done processing, so that FILELINK can re-create it
        when the next periodic scan is processed.

      WARNING: Do not use files mapped on a drive across a network. Any network problem
      may result in hanging the whole e-terracomm system for up to 30 seconds. If you do
      need to have the files coming or going across a network, have the other end mapping
      a local e-terracomm drive. This warning also applies to the Archive Directory field
      described below.

    Multi-valued environment variables for FILELINK must follow OSAL File Management
    parsing rules. The different values must be separated with a comma. Example:
    D:\TOPDIR\FILEDIR\OUTPUT.OUT,E:\TOPDIR\FILEDIR\OUTPUT.OUT

• Archive directory: The value can be entered literally or as an environment variable, but
  it may need to be an environment variable since the field is limited to 32 characters. No
  embedded blanks are allowed. The value is the complete directory specification for an
  archive directory. If a value is specified here, both input and output processed data files
  are copied to this directory. The number of versions of the files maintained in the
  directory is specified by “Max archive versions” in the remote record. Older versions are
  deleted. The files in the directory are renamed
  “<File Name>.<extension>_xxx”, where xxx is a sequential number starting from 1. For
  example, using the name of the file above, archive files have names such as
  “INDATA.DAT_17”, “INDATA.DAT_18”, etc. If using the date and time stamp, the format is
  INDATA.DAT_09-AUG-2004_095304 (colons cannot be used in the time due to file name
  restrictions).
