7.3.6 Data Semantics Conversion
Data semantics conversion is provided to support:
• Defined representations of status and conversions to alternate representations
• Conversions between different meanings of the sign bit on analog values
    Although it is common among utilities to use the sign of an analog to represent the
    direction of flow, no convention as to whether positive represents “from” or “to” is
    universally accepted — aside from the obvious problem that “from” one utility means
    “to” another.
• Conversions between different units of value (scaling)
A data semantics conversion can take place when the data is received (“on input”) or when
the data is transmitted (“on output”).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            423                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

The first step in modeling data semantics conversion is to determine the proportion of data
items of a given base type that requires conversion when exchanged with a given remote. If
the majority of the data items require conversion, the conversion should be modeled as
remote-wide, then blocked from the minority using data item–specific modeling.
The second step is to enter the conversion records that are needed. Both remote-wide
(CommDataConversion) and data item–specific (CommDataConversionDataItem) modeling
require conversion records. CommDataConversion records are entered as children of
CommRemote records.
Sequential conversions of the same type are allowed, and are performed only to the extent
of their common scope. This means that all the conversions explicitly modeled for a given
data item (“data item–specific”) are executed, regardless of their types, but only new types
of remote-wide conversions are then executed on that data item. For example, consider the
following model (all the conversions shown are for the single remote):
Data Item (1)                      Remote
 |                                   |
 +-- Scaling 1:100                   +-- Scaling 1:25
 |                                   |
 +-- Scaling 1:53                    +-- Flowdir: reverse

Data Item (2)
 |
 +-- Flowdir: don't reverse

Data Item (3)
Data Item (4)
Data Item (1) has two SCALING operations (1:100 then 1:53) and one FLOWDIR operation
(reverse) performed on it. The remote-wide 1:25 SCALING is not performed because a
data item–specific conversion of the same type (SCALING 1:100 and 1:53) pre-empted it.
Data Item (2) has one SCALING operation (1:25) performed on it, but the remote-wide
FLOWDIR operation (reverse) is blocked by the data item–specific FLOWDIR operation (do
not reverse).
Data Item (3) and Data Item (4) have both remote-wide conversions (SCALING 1:25 and
FLOWDIR reverse) performed.


7.3.6.1 Conversions of Status Representation
Conversions of status representation are modeled remote-wide or on a per-data item
per-remote basis, so that only when the exchanging sites differ in representation is a
conversion required.
When a status conversion is modeled, it is applied to both the current state and the
expected state when using data items of type supplemental.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              424                          e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.3.6.1.1 Modeling Status Conversion on Input
The conversion is always done from the remote representation to the ICCP standard
representation, as described in the section “Use of Indication Point Model” in ICCP
IEC 870-6-802, TASE.2 Object Models, version 1996–08.
For example, breaker status values are defined as follows:
 TRIPPED                 Binary 01 = decimal 1
 CLOSED                  Binary 10 = decimal 2
 BETWEEN                 Binary 00 = decimal 0
 INVALID                 Binary 11 = decimal 3
Insert a CommDataConversion under the CommRemote to perform remote-wide
conversion, or under CommDataItem to perform data item–specific conversion.
• Name: User-friendly identifier of the conversion record. Not otherwise used.
• Conversion type: Select Status Map from the picklist.
• Input: Set this to Yes for conversion on input.
• Apply to all status measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of STATUS should have the conversion applied.
• Apply to all real measurements: Not relevant for status conversions.
• Apply to all integer measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of INT32 should have the conversion applied. Only the two lowest
  bits are affected by the conversion.
• Tripped/1: The one- or two-bit value that means “tripped”, “open”, or “off” in the parent
  remote’s protocol. All except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off
  during conversion.
• Closed/2: The one- or two-bit value that means “closed” or “on” in the parent remote’s
  protocol. All except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during
  conversion.
• Between/0: The two-bit value that means “between states” or “in transition” in the
  parent remote’s protocol. All except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are
  masked off during conversion. If the remote does not define more than one bit for status
  values, this field should be left unfilled, or entered as minus one (-1).
• Illegal/3: The two-bit value that means “invalid state” in the parent remote’s protocol. All
  except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during conversion. If the
  remote does not define more than one bit for status values, or does not handle
  four-state readings, this field should be left unfilled, or entered as minus one (-1).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                 425                        e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    If the Between value is unfilled or negative, but the Illegal field is not, the remaining
    possible bit combination is also considered invalid. For example, if:
        Tripped= 3, Closed= 1, Between= -1, and Illegal= 2
    then, upon input, a value of 0 is translated to ICCP_STATUS_INVALID.
    If the Between and Illegal values are unfilled or negative, a value that translates to
    either Between or Illegal:
     – is translated to ICCP_STATUS_INVALID upon input.
     – is not translated upon output, and the quality is set to Garbage so the link
       application can take the appropriate decision (ISDLINK does not send the value to
       the EMS, and the other link applications flag the data with Bad quality).
    To block a remote-wide conversion for a few data items, model a data item–specific
    CommDataConversion record with parameters of minus one:
        Tripped= -1, Closed= -1, Between= -1, Invalid= -1
    This signals the conversion routine to leave the value alone.


7.3.6.1.2 Modeling Status Conversion on Output
The conversion is done between the ICCP standard representation and the remote’s own
representation. However, it is more likely that the status values in the e-terracomm
database do not follow the ICCP standard (this is probably why you need a conversion in
the first place). Therefore, for modeling status conversion on output, you need to specify
whether the values in your database follow the ICCP standard.
Insert a CommDataConversion under the CommRemote to perform remote-wide
conversion, or under a CommDataItem to perform data item–specific conversion.
• Name: User-friendly identifier of the conversion record. Not otherwise used.
• Conversion type: Select Status Map from the picklist.
• Input: Set this to No for conversion on output.
• Apply to all status measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of STATUS should have the conversion applied.
• Apply to all real measurements: Not relevant for status conversions.
• Apply to all integer measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of INT32 should have the conversion applied. Only the two lowest
  bits are affected by the conversion.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               426                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Database values follow ICCP standard: Set this to Yes or No. The ICCP standard is:
     TRIPPED            Binary 01 = decimal 1
     CLOSED             Binary 10 = decimal 2
     BETWEEN            Binary 00 = decimal 0
     INVALID            Binary 11 = decimal 3
• Tripped/1: If the database values follow the ICCP standard, enter the one- or two-bit
  value that means “tripped”, “open”, or “off” in the parent remote’s protocol; otherwise, a
  status in the database with a value of 1 is converted to the value you enter in this box.
  All except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during conversion.
• Closed/2: If the database values follow the ICCP standard, enter the one- or two-bit
  value that means “closed” or “on” in the parent remote’s protocol; otherwise, a status in
  the database with a value of 2 is converted to the value you enter in this box. All except
  the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during conversion.
• Between/0: If the database values follow the ICCP standard, enter the two-bit value that
  means “between states” or “in transition” in the parent remote’s protocol; otherwise, a
  status in the database with a value of 0 is converted to the value you enter in this box.
  All except the two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during conversion. If
  the remote does not define more than one bit for status values, this field should be left
  unfilled, or entered as minus one (-1).
• Illegal/3: If the database values follow the ICCP standard, enter the two-bit value that
  means “invalid state” in the parent remote’s protocol; otherwise, a status in the
  database with a value of 3 is converted to the value you enter in this box. All except the
  two lowest bits (values 0, 1, 2, and 3) are masked off during conversion. If the remote
  does not define more than one bit for status values, or does not handle four-state
  readings, this field should be left unfilled, or entered as minus one (-1).
    If the Between value is unfilled or negative, but the Illegal field is not, the remaining
    possible bit combination is also considered invalid. For example, if
        Tripped= 3, Closed= 1, Between= -1, and Illegal= 2
    then, upon input, a value of 0 is translated to ICCP_STATUS_INVALID.
    To block a remote-wide conversion for a few data items, model a data item–specific
    CommDataConversion record with parameters of minus one:
        Tripped= -1, Closed= -1, Between= -1, Invalid= -1
    This signals the conversion routine to leave the value alone.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                427                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.3.6.2 Conversion of Flow Direction Sign
e-terracomm has no native convention for direction of flow, and some values have no
directional meaning.
Insert a CommDataConversion under the CommRemote to perform remote-wide
conversion, or under a CommDataItem to perform data item–specific conversion.
• Name: User-friendly identifier of the conversion record. Not otherwise used.
• Conversion type: Select Flow Direction from the picklist.
• Input: Set this to Yes for conversion on input or No for conversion on output.
• Apply to all status measurements: Not relevant for flow direction conversions.
• Apply to all real measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of REAL32 should have the conversion applied.
• Apply to all integer measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of INT32 should have the conversion applied.
• Enter -1 to reverse flow: If a negative number is entered, it is forced to -1 during
  validation. If the field is left unfilled, or any zero or positive number is entered, it is forced
  to 1 during validation. A “-1” signals the conversion routine to negate the data item’s
  value. A “1” signals the conversion routine to leave the value alone.
To block a remote-wide conversion for a few data items, model a data item–specific Flow
Direction conversion with a parameter of one (1).


7.3.6.3 Scaling
e-terracomm has no native convention for units of value.
The formula for scaling upon input is:
    OagValue = (RemoteValue - intercept) / slope
The formula for scaling upon output is:
    RemoteValue = (OagValue * slope) + intercept
in which:
• RemoteValue is the data item value as received from or shipped to the remote site.
• OagValue is the data item value as stored in the e-terracomm transient value database.
• slope is the number or fraction of remote units equal to one e-terracomm unit. For
  example, if the value received from the remote is in units 100 times smaller than the
  units stored on e-terracomm, the slope is 100. If the value received from the remote is in
  units 100 times larger than the units stored on e-terracomm, the slope is .01.
• intercept is a positive, negative, or null constant.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               428                              e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                     e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Insert a CommDataConversion under the CommRemote to perform remote-wide
conversion, or under a CommDataItem to perform data item–specific conversion.
• Name: User-friendly identifier of the conversion record. Not otherwise used.
• Conversion type: Select Linear Scaling from the picklist.
• Input: Set this to Yes for conversion on input or No for conversion on output.
• Apply to all status measurements: Not relevant for linear scaling conversions.
• Apply to all real measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of REAL32 should have the conversion applied.
• Apply to all integer measurements: Used for remote-wide conversions, to signal that all
  data items with a type of INT32 should have the conversion applied.
• Slope: Enter the slope value based on the formulation given above.
• Intercept: Enter the intercept value based on the formulation given above.
To simply add a bias to a received value, model a conversion with
slope = 1 and intercept = bias.
To block a remote-wide conversion for a few data items, model a data item–specific Linear
Scaling conversion with parameters
slope = 1 and intercept = 0.


7.3.7 Quality Semantics Conversion
The document TASE.2 (ICCP) Implementation Recommendations (IEC 60870-6-505 Annex C)
provides guidelines for the translation of quality codes between SCADA and ICCP. However,
the document does not reach far enough, leaving the ICCP’s HELD quality without a
definition (“this is a local issue”, as IEC puts it), and the reverse translation from ICCP to
SCADA is not addressed at all.
Also, customers have shown interest in being able to choose the way quality translations
between SCADA and ICCP (and vice versa) are applied.
Starting with e-terracomm 2.6, for each ISD remote using protocol version 4.0 or above, it is
possible to specify the desired quality mapping for both incoming and outgoing data.
Mapping can be different for each remote.
The mapping is based on both the quality and the source of the data as well as the Not In
Service and Replaced flags.
It is not mandatory to model quality mapping. e-terracomm uses default mapping tables if
nothing is modeled. The conversions modeled are meant to override some of the default
mappings (although it is possible to modify all default mappings using 16 conversion
records for ICCP to ISD and 64 conversion records for ISD to ICCP).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             429                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Quality conversion records should only be inserted under ISD remotes. Conversions from
ICCP to ISD and ISD to ICCP can be mixed. The order can be important if two or more
conversions modify the same mapping.
• Direction: Choose “ICCP to ISD” or “ISD to ICCP”.
• ICCP Quality/Source: For ISD to ICCP conversions, enter the ICCP quality and source
  information that the ISD fields map to. For ICCP to ISD conversions, enter the ICCP
  quality/source that you want to convert.
• ISD Quality/Source/Replace/Not in Service: For ISD to ICCP conversions, enter the ISD
  information that you want to convert. For ICCP to ISD conversions, enter the ISD
  information that you want the ICCP quality/source to map to.
Possible values for quality and source are selected using a picklist. One of the available
values is <Any>, which is used as a wildcard:
• When <Any> is used on the side the data is coming from (ICCP for input conversion, ISD
  for output conversion), it means “for all possible quality/source combinations”.
• When <Any> is used on the side the data is going to (ISD for input conversion, ICCP for
  output conversion), it applies to the same quality/source as the side the data is coming
  from.


7.3.8 Data Items
Most data items are created by the user. One type is created by the validation program:
Component Status data items.


7.3.8.1 Data Item Type
For the purposes of e-terracomm, data items can be categorized as:
• SCADA, Fixed Length: Integers, Reals, and Statuses.
• Non-SCADA, Variable Length: Periodic Account Objects, Profile Account Objects,
  Account Request Objects (all ICCP Block 8 data items), Message Objects (ICCP Block 4),
  and Control Messages (used to forward ICCP Block 5 operations (command and
  setpoint) between remotes).
The data item type defines the format of the data (Real, Integer, Status, Account Object, etc.)
and associated qualifiers (Quality, Time Stamp, Change of Value Counter).
A data item can have more than one type:
• DB type defines the format and qualifiers as they are stored in the database.
• Network type defines the format and qualifiers exchanged with the remotes sites. There
  is one network type per remote.
In most cases, DB type and Network type are the same. When DB and Network types are
different, they must be compatible.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             430                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

The rules are protocol-specific, as described in the table below.
 ICCPLINK              SCADA data items:
                       To enable interoperability between remotes using different versions of
                       ICCP, qualifiers can be dropped or added (e.g., a value sourced from a
                       1996–08 version needs to be served to a 2000–08 version with
                       different qualifiers (e.g., timestamp with milliseconds).
                        • The database validation program issues a warning when attributes
                           present in the DB type and the Network type are different, or when
                           the format is different (REAL-INTEGER may result in loss of
                           precision).
                        • The database validation program issues an error when the format
                           of the DB type and the format of the Network type are incompatible
                           (e.g., REAL - Status).
                       Non-SCADA data items:
                       Network type must be the same as DB type.
 ISDLINK               SCADA data items:
                       ISDLINK uses the network type only to distinguish between analogs
                       and counts. Analogs must have a REAL32 (with or without qualifier)
                       and counts must have an EMSCOUNT as Network type (for details
                       when using ISD 4.0, see section 7.7 InterSite Data 4.0).
                       Non-SCADA data items:
                       Network type must be the same as DB type.
 HABCLINK              Network type must be the same as DB type.
 FILELINK              Only INT32, REAL32, and STATUS with or without quality are read or
                       written; however, qualifiers can be configured (they are either dropped
                       or filled with default values).
 ELCOLINK              Only INT32, REAL32, and STATUS with quality and timestamp are
                       exchanged via ELCOLINK. Timestamp is optional. Other qualifiers can
                       be configured (they are either dropped or filled with default values).


7.3.8.2 Data Item Permissions
Data item permissions are e-terracomm’s translation of the access rights defined in the
ICCP’s bilateral table agreement. They define which remote sites can access a given data
item, and they indicate the type of access.
There are three types of permissions: Read, Write, and Execute. Although the bilateral table
agreement is ICCP-specific, e-terracomm has extended the use of access permission to all
supported protocols.
A remote site having Read permission to a data item can access it either by a direct read
data value request (if the protocol supports reading of a single data item; currently, only the

Proprietary – See Copyright Page               431                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

ICCP protocol supports reading a single data item), or by putting it in a data set (input data
set on the remote site, output data set in e-terracomm). In e-terracomm, any remote can
have Read permission.
A remote site having Write permission to a data item can access it either by a direct write
data value request (if the protocol supports writing of a single data item; currently, only the
ICCP protocol supports writing a single data item), or by putting it in a data set (output data
set on the remote site, input data set in e-terracomm). In e-terracomm, only the remote
source of the data item can have Write permission.
A remote site having Execute permission is allowed to operate the device associated with
the data item. Any remote sites can have Execute permission, except the remote source of
the data item (i.e., a remote site cannot have Execute and Write permissions at the same
time).


7.3.8.3 Data Item Identification
Each protocol supported by e-terracomm has its own rules for the names used to identify
data items. Usually, rules for a given protocol are incompatible with the rules for another
one. This is especially the case for ISD and ICCP. Characters allowed in an ICCP data item
name are restricted to the upper/lower letters, the 10 digits and two special characters
(dollar sign and underscore) without embedded blanks. ISD allows the full ASCII character
set.
Another difference is the length of the data item names. For performance, the shorter an
ICCP data item name, the better. ICCP names are exchanged over the network when data is
sent by exception, which is the most common way of transferring data. ISD names are long
because they are built by concatenating the substation, device type, device, and point IDs
of the corresponding item in EMS.
When an e-terracomm system is used as an ICCP hub, another problem that can arise is
duplicated names, as in the example shown in Figure 114. In this example, the ICCP hub is
receiving data from both Utility A and Utility B. In addition, by coincidence, each utility is
using the same name to refer to points in their databases (when previously separate
networks are combined, this is likely to happen). These are physically different points and
the ICCP hub must store them as such. The ICCP hub must use the same name to obtain the
points from each utility, yet must be able to store them as separate points in its database,
since they are different points. In addition, if the ICCP hub is serving these points to a third
utility, the third utility must be able to distinguish between the two.
On the ICCP hub, the e-terracomm database must have two data items with different
names for ICCP as a server (to serve either point A_MW from Utility A or point A_MW from
Utility B) and, at the same time, use the same name for ICCP acting as a client of Utilities A
and B.

                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.3.8.3.1 ICCP Hub Configuration
“A_MW_A” (the point A measurement from Utility A) and “A_MW_B” (the point A
measurement from Utility B) are the server names of the ICCP hub. Utility C must use these
names to read the point A value, either from Utility A or Utility B.
“A_MW” (the same name for the point A measurement from Utility A and B) is the name
used by ICCPLINK acting as a client on the ICCP hub to read the point A value from each
utility.


7.3.8.3.2 ICCP Utility C Configuration
Utility C uses “A_MW_A” when it wants the value from Utility A and “A_MW_B” when it
wants the value from Utility B.


7.3.8.3.3 Data Item Identification and Optional Names
In the e-terracomm database, a data item has:
• An identifier, unique among all defined data items (CommDataItem.Name)
• One or more optional names, to allow solving all the problems listed above
  (CommDataItemName.Name)


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                                     433                                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                                                          e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Optional names, when needed, inserted as children CommDataItemName records of
  CommDataItem
The data item identifier is well-suited for ICCP names — names used by remote clients such
as Utility C in the example above (i.e., server names of the ICCP hub) — while optional names
are more likely for ISD names, or to be used by ICCP when acting as a client (as in the ICCP
hub) to read data from Utilities A and B as in the example above.
The ICCP protocol allows using data item names containing lowercase characters.
HABCLINK uses the data item identifier from the HABC optional name if supplied; otherwise,
it uses the data item identifier to pass to SAMPLER. The syntax and requirements are
discussed below, in section 7.3.8.3.6 Building HABCLINK Names.

  Important Note: Whenever possible, use only one name (the identifier) for all protocols,
  both for clarity and to have a smaller database.


7.3.8.3.4 Recommended Configuration of Data Item Name Based on Data Type
• SCADA data (INT32, REAL32, STATUS)
• The data item name must follow protocol-specific rules:
     – Transfer Account (periodic or profile) or Information Message
        The data item name must be a number for all protocols supporting these data types.
        No optional names are needed. Use the data item identifier. This is the Transfer
        Account Reference (Transfer Account) or the Information Message Reference
        (Information Message).
     – Account Request and Control Message
        These data items are only for internal use (used to forward request or control from
        one remote to another through OAGSERVE). No optional names are needed. Use the
        data item identifier.
At run time, ICCPLINK always uses two data item names (they can be identical), while all
other link applications use only one name.
Which names are used by a link application depends on whether optional names are
configured:
• ISDLINK, HABCLINK, ELCOLINK, and FILELINK: If an optional name is configured, it is used
  at run time; otherwise, the data item identification is used.
• ICCPLINK: See the table below.

7.3.8.3.5 Building ISD Names
ISDLINK supports names configured using either single- or multiple-byte character sets. The
rules are slightly different for each type of character set.
• Single-Byte Character Set
     When a data item is to be exchanged with an ISDLINK remote, the data item
     identification or an ISD optional name must be built from the SCADA hierarchy of
     Substation, Device Type, Device, and either Analog, Count, or Point IDs. Each ID must be
     separated from the next one by a blank, a dollar sign, or an underscore. The dollar sign
     and underscore characters can be used only if neither of the IDs already has these
     characters. ISDLINK looks first for blank, then dollar, then underscore; blank must not be
     used for the data item identification (use only in the ISD optional name).
     Maximum ID lengths are:
     – SUBSTN = 8
     – DEVTYP = 6
     – DEVICE = 14
     – POINT, ANALOG, COUNT = 4
     The SCADA IDs:
     – Cannot have embedded blanks
     – Can contain any printable ASCII character (except the one used as a separator)


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                435                          e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    Examples of valid and invalid ISD names:
     LAKEVIEW$PLC$LV1_CONTROLER$SPFB                 Valid as data item identification and as optional
                                                     name.
     LAKEVIEW_PLC_LV1_CONTROLER_SPFB                 Invalid: Underscore cannot be used as separator
                                                     because one of the IDs already contains this
                                                     character.
     LAKEVIEW PLC000 LV1_CONTROLER SPFB              Valid as ISD optional name but invalid as data item
                                                     identification.

• Multiple-Byte Character Set
    When a data item is to be exchanged with an ISDLINK remote using a multi-byte
    character set, an ISD optional name must be used. It is built from the SCADA hierarchy
    of Substation, Device Type, Device, and either Analog, Count, or Point IDs. Each ID must
    be separated from the next one by a blank.
    Maximum ID lengths depend on how many bytes are needed to represent a single
    character. The maximum number of bytes (not characters) allowed is:
     – SUBSTN = 8
     – DEVTYP = 6
     – DEVICE = 14
     – POINT, ANALOG, COUNT = 4
    The SCADA IDs cannot have embedded blanks.
    You must define an environment variable to enable multi-byte character support at run
    time. For more information, refer to the e-terracomm Software Installation and
    Maintenance Guide.

      Note: Currently, only the Korean character set is supported.


7.3.8.3.6 Building HABCLINK Names
The name provided to HABCLINK must be in the form “field,compositekey” (excluding the
quotes, but including the comma) in which:
• field is the e-terrahabitat field_record name. For example:
     – OPEN_LN2: A True/False bit on the LN2 record
     – PEAKTIME_UNIT: An R*4 field on the LN2 record
     – TOPDELAY: A global item
    You can use the full complement of HABConnect specifications, as defined in the
    HABConnect User’s Guide (“Specifying an e-terrahabitat Link – Specifying the Topic”). For
    example:
     – I$BS_ND>KV_BS: An R*4 field on the BS record pointed to by the ND record
Proprietary – See Copyright Page               436                                 e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                        e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• compositekey is the e-terrahabitat composite key. Except for ranges and subscripts, you
  can use the full complement of HABConnect specifications, as defined in the
  HABConnect User’s Guide (“Specifying an e-terrahabitat Link – Specifying the Item”). For
  example:
     – TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.DOUGLAS.10.T538
        For OPEN_LN2 in the NETMOM database: ID_DECK.ID_CO.ID_DV.ID_ST.ID_ND.ID_LN2
     – TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.LAKEVIEW.38
        For I$BS_ND>KV_BS: DECK in the NETMOM database:
        ID_DECK.ID_CO.ID_DV.ID_ST.ID_ND
    Range specifications that are undetected during validation cause a run-time error.
    Subscripts provoke a warning during validation; they are discouraged because
    subscripts can change very easily in the target e-terrahabitat database. HABCLINK and
    HABConnect Sampler do not know the difference, and they fetch or deposit the wrong
    data without objection.
Some complete names are:
• OPEN_LN2,TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.DOUGLAS.10.T538
• I$BS_ND>KV_BS,TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.LAKEVIEW.38

 Protocol                  Naming Rules
 ICCPLINK                  Must be ICCP compliant: No embedded blanks, [a...z], [A...Z], [0...9], or [$, _ ]; must
                           begin with a letter; maximum length is 32 characters.
                           For Transfer Account and Information Message data items, the name must be a
                           number (this is not an ICCP name, this is the Transfer Account Reference or the
                           Information Message Reference).
 ISDLINK                   Must follow ISD protocol naming rules described above.
                           Control Message data item names are not exchanged with EMS; there is no
                           specific restriction.
 HABCLINK                  See section 7.3.8.3.6 Building HABCLINK Names.
 FILELINK                  Maximum length 32 when using data item identification (ID_DI), 60 when using
                           optional name (NAME_DINAME). For input, the name cannot contain a comma
                           (used as delimiter between name and value); this restriction also applies for
                           output if the generated file is to be read by FILELINK at a remote node.
 ELCOLINK                  The maximum size is defined on the remote record (Max ID Length field).

7.3.8.4 Data Item Modeling Information
The following properties are available for modeling CommDataItem records:
• Name: Identification of the data item. This is a character string with a length
  <= 32 characters and no embedded blanks. It must be unique. If no optional name
  (CommDataItemName) is used, it must conform to the protocol-specific rules described
  in section 7.3.8.3 Data Item Identification.
• Description: Optionally, enter a description for the data item.
• Base type: Picklist to select the basic type of the data item. Existing types are listed
  below (an “S” denotes a SCADA type data item, a “V” denotes a non-SCADA data item).
  For a detailed description of the new data types available when using ICCP version
  2000–08, see section 7.9.1 New SCADA Data Types.
     INT32              S    32-bit signed integer value
     REAL32             S    32-bit signed floating point value (SCADA analogs and counts)
     STATUS             S    2-bit status (SCADA statuses), internally stored in a 16-bit integer
     STATUSEX           S    Data state supplemental (2-bit current value, 2-bit expected value, 2-bit
                             tag value)
     PERACT             V    Periodic account (ICCP Block 8)
     PRFACT             V    Profile account (ICCP Block 8)
     ACTREQ             V    Account request (ICCP Block 8)
     INFOMSG            V    Information message (ICCP Block 4)
     CTRLMSG            V    Control message

    For SCADA types, the base type combined with the attributes (Quality, Timestamp, and
    Change of Value Counter) gives the database type (DB type).

 ICCPLINK           SCADA data can have Quality, Timestamp (with or without milliseconds), and Change of

                    - - - - No qualifier at all

       of space allocated by OAGSERVE, not the size of the data part of the message.
     – The size of an Account Request (ACTREQ) data item must be 30.
     – The size of a Control Message (CTRLMSG) data item must be 20.

 Applications


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     440                                 e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                              e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Source remote: Specify the remote source of the data item.
• ICCP scope: The ICCP protocol allows data items to be created with either “VMD scope”
  or “Domain scope”.
    When a data item is created with “VMD scope”, only one MMS named variable is created
    for that data item, regardless of the number of remotes with access. Unauthorized
    requests for that data item are not refused until ICCPLINK processes the request.
    When a data item is created with “Domain scope”, the number of MMS named variables
    created for that data item is equal to the number of remotes with access to that data
    item. Unauthorized requests for that data item are refused immediately by MMS.
    A general rule to apply is to set a data item’s scope to “VMD scope” if more than one
    remote has Read access to it, and set the scope to “Domain scope” if only one remote
    has Read access to it. However, all data items can be configured with VMD scope, the
    only access control being through appropriate setting of the Read permission.
• Data conversion: You can specify a CommDataConversion record that should be used
  for data item–specific conversion (see section 7.3.6 Data Semantics Conversion).


7.3.8.5 Control Devices
CommControlDevice records are used to model supervisory controls associated with
CommDataItems.
• Name: Enter the identifier of the device. For ICCP, this is an MMS identifier; therefore, it
  must begin with a letter and contain the characters [a...z], [A...Z], [0...9], $, and _
  (underscore) only. It must not duplicate data item identification or the ICCP optional
  name. If the device is Select Before Operate (SBO), the name length must not exceed
  24 characters because ICCPLINK has to build a name such as “<ICCP device
  name>_success” (concatenation of up to 8 characters). For a Direct Operate (DO) device,
  the maximum length is 32 characters. If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK,
  and no ICCPLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field
  can be left blank.
• ICCP scope: The ICCP protocol allows devices to be created with either “VMD scope” or
  “Domain scope”.
     – VMD scope: only one MMS named variable is created for that device, regardless of
       the number of remotes with access. Unauthorized requests for that device are not
       refused until ICCPLINK processes the request.
     – Domain scope: the number of MMS named variables created for that device is equal
       to the number of remotes with access to that device. Unauthorized requests for that
       device are refused immediately by MMS.
    A general rule to apply is to set a device’s scope to “VMD scope” if more than one
    remote has Execute permission to it, and set the scope to “Domain scope” if only one
    remote has Execute permission to it.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             441                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    A device and the data item with which it is associated can have different scopes. It
    makes sense, for example, that all remotes can read the data item value (data item in
    VMD scope), but only one can control the associated device (device in Domain scope).
• ISD site name: This is the site originating command/setpoint on the device. If the control
  is not passing through ISDLINK, and no ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to
  the parent data item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through
  ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent
  data item, this field must be filled with any two characters. For more information, see
  section 7.8 InterSite Control 1.0.
• Class: Specify whether the device is a Select Before Operate (SBO) or Direct Operate (DO)
  device. For more information, see section 7.8 InterSite Control 1.0.
• Timeout: Time, in seconds, that an SBO device stays in the armed state after a
  successful Select operation. This field is relevant for SBO devices only. If an Operate
  operation on the device is not received within this time, the device is de-selected and
  returns to the idle state. If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK, and no ICCPLINK
  remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field can be left blank.
  If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK, but one of the ICCPLINK remotes has
  Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field must be filled with a valid
  value (> 0).
• Check back name: This is an arbitrary number, agreed upon by the ICCP partners, that
  the ICCP server returns to the client as a result of a Select operation. The client can then
  check that the returned value is the expected one; whether to make this check is a client
  issue. If ICCPLINK is acting as a client, it always checks the returned value. If the value
  does not match the expected one, ICCPLINK logs an error and does not send the
  Operate request. This field is relevant for SBO devices only. Leave it blank if the control is
  not passing through ICCPLINK.
• Intersite control 0/1 name: For digital status, these are the names of the commands
  sent to a remote site that represent a 0 (ICCP_OPEN) and a 1 (ICCP_CLOSE), respectively.
  They must match the names configured in the SCADA Command record because
  matching a command between SCADA and ISDLINK is done by name. If the control is
  not passing through ISDLINK, and no ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to
  the parent data item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through
  ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent
  data item, this field must be filled (any string).
• Intersite setpoint name: This is the name of a setpoint. It must match the name
  configured in the SCADA Setpoint record because matching a setpoint between SCADA
  and ISDLINK is done by name. If the control is not passing through ISDLINK, and no
  ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field can be
  left blank. If the control is not passing through ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes
  has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field must be filled (any
  string).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             442                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• ELCOM group/point: ELCOM group and point ID for the control. It is a numeric value
  between 1 (for group) or 0 (for point) and 255. If the control is not passing through
  ELCOLINK, and no ELCOLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data
  item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through ELCOLINK, but one
  of the ELCOLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field
  must be filled with a valid value.

  Note: There is nothing to configure for support of ICCP Conformance Block 7 (Events).
  ICCPLINK automatically enrolls in the four pre-defined event conditions for SBO devices
  (Timeout, Local Reset, Success, and Failure) if the remote site owning the SBO device also
  supports ICCP Conformance Block 7 (the phrase “owning the device” means that the
  remote has Write permission to the data item the device is child of).

As a server, ICCPLINK supports the three ICCP defined operations: Create Event Enrollment,
Delete Event Enrollment, and Get Event Enrollment Attributes. ICCPLINK supports the Event
Notification action. All pre-defined event conditions are supported (Access Violation, Data
Failure, and the four SBO devices’ related event conditions). ICCPLINK triggers the Success
and Failure events only when ISDLINK is using InterSite Controls 1.0.
As a client, ICCPLINK only supports the Create Event Enrollment operation for the four
pre-defined event conditions for SBO devices. It never enrolls in Access Violation or Data
Failure event conditions. Success and Failure events received from the server are passed to
ISDLINK but reach the EMS only if InterSite Controls 1.0 is used.

  Note: Support for ICCP Conformance Block 7 can be disabled (see the “ICCPLINK Options”
  section of the e-terracomm Software Installation and Maintenance Guide).


7.3.8.6 Optional Name
The CommDataItemName record is used to model additional or optional names for data
items.
• Name: Enter the optional name. This character string has a maximum length of 60
  characters. The actual maximum depends on the protocol (see section 7.3.8.3.7 Data
  Item Identification or Optional Names Restrictions Based on Protocol). For
  CommDataItemName records associated with ISDLINK, enter the association to the
  measurement instead.
• Name for: Use the picklist to choose the protocol that the optional name is for.
• Measurement: For names associated with ISDLINK, the CommDataItemName record
  should point to the associated SCADA measurement in e-terrasource. During export, the
  ISD name of the measurement is automatically computed and filled in the e-terracomm
  model instead of the Name field. During import, the linkage between
  CommDataitemName records and SCADA measurements is automatically performed
  when SCADAMOM and OAGMOM are imported together. Otherwise, a sample script
  (Link_CommDataItemName_Measurement.sql) is provided to assist in linking

    CommDataItemName records to the correct SCADA Analog, Discrete, and Accumulator
    records. Refer to the e-terrasource Software Installation and Maintenance Guide for

7.3.8.7 Limit Sets
The CommLimitSet record is used to model the limit sets associated with a given data item.
Only data items with a base type of REAL32 can have limit sets. Any number of limit sets
can be associated with a data item. The actual number depends on the number of limits
modeled in SCADA and whether some limits are relevant for remote sites.
• Name: Name of the limit set for ICCP exchange. It must follow the same ICCP naming
  rules as for data items, and it must not exceed 28 characters because “_L” or “_H” is
  added to create two REAL32 named variables, one for the low and one for the high limit
  values (the size limit is set to 28 for possible future expansion to more than two values
  for a limit set).
• ISD name: ISD name of the limit, which must match the name modeled in SCADA
  (Substation, Device Type, Device, Analog, Limit). Naming follows the ISD naming rules.
• Disable high limit check: If Yes, the high limit is not checked.
• Disable low limit check: If Yes, the low limit is not checked.

  Note: The number of limits modeled for a given data item is what you make available for
  ICCP remotes or what you want to receive from ICCP remotes. It does not mean that
  remotes request all the limits you have made available, or that you can receive all the
  limits you have modeled. Only the high or low limit may be available from a remote, or you
  may decide to make available only the low or high limit of a limit set. Partial ICCP data
  sets are created when not all requested limits are available, as for non-limit data items.

Limit sets’ Read/Write permissions are inherited from the parent data item.
Figure 115 shows how limits flow between GE and non-GE systems.

7.3.9 Data Sets

7.3.9.1 Definition
The purpose of CommDataSets is to group data items according to the reporting
preferences of the parent remote. For uniformity of modeling, e-terracomm uses the data
set record to hold trigger, reporting style, and timing information even for non-SCADA data
items. The data set structure does not prevent ICCP sites from reading and writing
individual data items — indeed, for Block 8 and Block 4, data sets are invisible to the remote
ICCP sites.
The data sets themselves are modeled using the CommDataSet record, whereas the data
items within the data sets are referenced with CommDataSetDataItem records.
Not all data sets need to be modeled. It depends on which protocol the data sets are for.


7.3.9.1.1 Protocol-Specific Modeling
 ICCPLINK          Output data sets do not need to be created at modeling time. It is the ICCP client’s
                   responsibility to check that data sets exist on the server (output data sets) and, if not,
                   create them. Note that, if output data sets are modeled, the attributes (Trigger, Style, etc.)
                   are overwritten by the remote site when it enables the data set.
                   Data sets can reference both data items and limit sets.
 ISDLINK           Only one output data set per remote is allowed. Output data set parameters must be
                   modeled, but the content of the output data set does not need to be modeled. It is the
                   client’s (the EMS host) responsibility to tell ISDLINK which data items it wants to receive.
                   Input data sets must be fully modeled, including transmission parameters and contents.
                   Data sets can reference both data items and limit sets.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                      447                                 e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                               e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

 HABCLINK          Input and output data sets must be fully modeled, transmission parameters and
                   contents.
                   Limit sets are not allowed.
 FILELINK          Only one input or one output data set per link per remote is allowed. This data set must
                   be PERIODIC with a reporting style of ALL. FILELINK data sets can contain only REAL,
                   INTEGER, and STATUS type data items.
                   Limit sets are not allowed.
 ELCOLINK          Input data sets must be modeled while output data sets can be modeled, or the creation
                   and deletion can be done by the remote site at run time. Both modeled and dynamically
                   created data sets are supported and can coexist for a given remote. If Group
                   Management functions are not supported, the output data sets must be modeled.
                   Limit sets are not allowed.

The CommDataSet properties are detailed below.
• Name: The identifier of the data set. This is a string of 32 characters or fewer with no
  embedded blanks. It must be unique within the remote. See below for protocol-specific
  restrictions.
     ICCPLINK          Must begin with a letter. Only alphanumeric characters (0–9, a–z,
                       A–Z) and $ and _ (underscore) characters are allowed.
     ISDLINK           No specific restrictions.
     HABCLINK          No specific restrictions.
     FILELINK          No specific restrictions.
     ELCOLINK          Must be a number between 1 and 32767. This is the ELCOM-90 group number.

• In service: In/out of service default setting.
• Data set type: Picklist to select Input or Output. An input data set contains incoming
  data (from a remote to e-terracomm). An output data set contains outgoing data (from
  e-terracomm to a remote).
• Trigger: Picklist to select when the data set is sent (Output) or when it is supposed to be
  received (Input). e-terracomm supports the triggers listed below, but not all protocols
  support all triggers (see protocol-specific information after the description of the
  Transmission Style field below).
     – Periodic: Data set is input/output on a periodic basis.
     – Exception: Data set is input/output when an exception occurs (data value and/or
       attribute of a data item in the data set has changed).
     – On request: Data set is input/output upon request.
     – On receipt: For output data sets only. The data set is output upon receipt of its twin
       data set.
     – Periodic data transfer (ELCOM only): The periodicity is given by the priority class
       (see the Serial Number/Priority Class fields).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     448                               e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                            e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

     – Periodically requested data transfer (ELCOM only): ELCOLINK polls the remote for
       these data sets at the modeled periodic rate, which is given by the priority class (see
       the Serial Number/Priority Class fields).
     – Unsolicited data transfer: ELCOLINK unsolicited or unsolicited mixed data transfer.
       For ISDLINK and ICCPLINK, this is the same as trigger by exception, except that all
       changes occurring during the buffering time are reported (for details, see section
       7.9.2 New Way of Reporting Data Changes). The transmission style must be Report
       by Exception.
• Transmission style: Picklist to select All (all data items in the data set are transmitted),
  or Report by Exception (RBE, only data items that have their value or attributes change
  are transmitted).
    The Exception trigger and the Report by Exception transmission style govern different
    characteristics of the data set. It is entirely reasonable to define a data set that is
    triggered upon change of value, but reports all its data items, even the unchanged ones.
    Trigger and transmission style restrictions apply, depending on data types and protocol.
    A data set carrying SCADA data is called a “SCADA data set”; a data set carrying
    non-SCADA data is called a “non-SCADA data set”. A given data set cannot carry both
    SCADA and non-SCADA data.
    Non-SCADA data sets (Account Objects, Info Message, and Control messages) must be
    configured as follows:
     – Input data sets must have Trigger set to On Request and Transmission Style set to
       All.
     – Output data sets must have Trigger set to On Receipt and Transmission Style set to
       All.


7.3.9.1.2 Protocol-Specific Modeling
 ICCPLINK          SCADA data sets:
                   Input: Trigger = Periodic, On Request, Exception, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = All or
                   RBE.
                   Output: Trigger = Periodic, Exception, On Receipt, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = All or
                   RBE.
                   Non-SCADA data sets: see the section above.
 ISDLINK           SCADA data sets have restricted triggers and transmission styles:
                   Input: Trigger = Periodic; Style = RBE. The periodicity is the polling rate.
                   Output: Trigger = Exception, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = RBE.
                   Non-SCADA data sets: see the section above.
 HABCLINK          Data sets have restricted trigger settings:
                   Input: Trigger = Periodic or On Request.
                   Output: Trigger = Periodic, Exception, On Receipt.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       449                                  e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

 FILELINK          FILELINK data sets have restricted trigger and transmission style settings:
                   Input: Trigger = Periodic and Style = All.
                   Output: Trigger = Periodic and Style = All.
 ELCOLINK          Trigger: Periodic and Exception are invalid. On Request, Periodically Requested Data
                   Transfer, and Periodic Data Transfer must have Style = All. Unsolicited Data Transfer must
                   have Style = RBE.

• Data item count: This is a non-enterable (calculated) field that displays the number of
  CommDataSetDataItem children in the data set.
• Exception buffering time: This is the exception buffering time in seconds. The exception
  buffering time applies only to output data sets that are triggered by Exception (or
  Unsolicited Data Transfer for ICCPLINK). This field designates the amount of time
  OAGSERVE waits (in case other changed values arrive) before shipping out the data set.
  Its purpose is to avoid triggering the same data set multiple times within a short period.
    For Unsolicited Data Transfer data sets, the buffering time is not monitored by
    OAGSERVE. Instead:
     – For ICCP, ICCPLINK does the monitoring.
     – For ISD, the buffering time is actually the EMS polling interval (i.e., value changes are
       buffered between consecutive polls).
    By default, the exception buffering time is set equal to the global default buffering time
    (see section 7.3.2 e-terracomm Configuration Parameters). To specify a different value,
    set the Override global exception buffering time field to Yes, then enter the desired time
    in the Exception buffering time field.
• Periodic timer: For output data sets, this property specifies how often the data set is
  shipped out. If the data set’s style is RBE and no data item values/attributes have
  changed, a transmit message (with a zero data item count) is nonetheless sent to the
  link application. Depending upon the protocol, the link application may or may not ship
  a report to the remote. For input data sets, this property specifies how often the data set
  is expected. The timer is synchronized to the receipt of the first report. The period is
  specified in seconds.
• Grace percentage: For input data sets, the grace percentage is used to calculate how
  long OAGSERVE should wait after the periodic timer or the integrity timer expires, before
  deciding that the report is late. When a report is late, all of its data items are marked
  invalid (“No current reading available”). By default, the grace percentage is set equal to
  the global grace period for reception value (see section 7.3.2 e-terracomm
  Configuration Parameters). To specify a different percentage, set the Override global
  grace percentage flag to Yes, and enter a value for the grace percentage. There is a
  minimum value of 1% for the grace percentage. The grace percentage is not used by
  output data sets.
• Integrity timer: Used by data sets that are triggered by exception, and by periodic data
  sets whose transmission style is Report by Exception. When the integrity timer expires,
  OAGSERVE transmits the output data set or expects the input data set. The grace

Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     450                                e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                             e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    percentage is also used by OAGSERVE in the same manner for the integrity period as for
    the Period. The integrity timer is specified in seconds.


7.3.9.1.3 Protocol-Specific Modeling
 ISDLINK            The integrity timer must be 0 for input data sets (due to the way EMS sends integrity
                    scans — separate for status, analogs, and counts, a few points at a time).
                    Output data sets must have a non-zero integrity period to make sure that ISDLINK sends
                    all current values as soon as a connection is established.
 ICCPLINK           For output exception data sets (trigger is Exception or Unsolicited Data Transfer, or
 HABCLINK           trigger is Periodic and transmission style is Report By Exception), the value should be > 0;
                    otherwise, data is sent only when changes are detected. This can take a long time and,
 FILELINK
                    after a connection with the remote is established, data remains invalid until a change is
                    detected. When the integrity period is not 0, all data is sent as soon as a connection with
                    the remote is established.
 ELCOLINK           ELCOM-90 does not have integrity scans defined.

• Twin data set: Identity of the twin data set. Each pair of twin data sets must contain one
  input and one output. They must name each other as their twin. The lists of their
  contents (CommDataSetDataItem records) must match exactly. The input twin can have
  any trigger, and the output twin must be triggered on receipt. The twin of a critical
  (end-to-end acknowledgment requested) data set must also be defined as critical. Each
  critical or non-SCADA data set must have a twin.
• Legal application: For HABCLINK data sets only. This specifies the identity of a
  CommLegalApplication record associated with the data set.
• Data item holding data set state: For input data sets, you can specify the identifier of
  the data item used to hold the state of the data set (Not Active, Active, Late). Modeling of
  the data item is detailed in section 7.10.3.2 Data Set Component Data Items.
• Control timeout: For ICCPLINK and ISDLINK control message data sets, this is the device
  timeout. A Select Before Operate (SBO) device returns to the idle state if no response to a
  Select or Operate request is received within the specified time. This timeout is for
  messages exchanged internally between link applications (e.g., ICCPLINK forwarding an
  Operate request received from a remote site to ISDLINK to be passed to EMS).

      Note: When defining ICCPLINK control data sets, make sure that the device timeout at
      the remote site (if e-terracomm is used) is shorter than the end-to-end flow control
      timer T2 (if flow control is enabled); otherwise, failure to receive a response for a device
      can trigger the abort of the association.

• Periodic offset: For ELCOM input data sets with trigger Periodic Data Transfer or
  Periodically Requested Data Transfer, or output data sets with trigger Periodic and
  FILELINK input data sets, it is possible to specify a relative time offset.
    Data sets with periods of an integer number of days can be scheduled to be shipped at
    a given hour:minute:second within the first day (the “first” day is the one in which the
    offset occurs following the startup of the data set).

Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     451                                 e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                              e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    Data sets with periods of an integer number of minutes can be scheduled to be shipped
    at a given second within the first minute (the “first” minute is the one in which the offset
    occurs following the startup of the data set).
    Data sets with periods of an integer number of hours can be scheduled to be shipped at
    a given minute:second offset within the first hour (the “first” hour is the one in which the
    offset occurs following the startup of the data set).
    The offset is specified as a date where the month, day, and year are ignored.
• Periodic offset type: This is a picklist that allows you to specify whether the periodic
  offset is relative to the time the link application started, or is synchronized to the wall
  clock.
• Partial data set allowed: When used for ICCPLINK, it applies to input ICCPLINK data sets
  only:
     – If Yes, the corresponding output data set is created at the remote site even when
       some of its data items are not available.
     – If No, the corresponding output data set is not created at the remote site when some
       of its data items are not available.
    When used for FILELINK, it applies to input FILELINK data sets only.
     – If Yes, the dataset is read from the file even if data items are missing.
     – If No, the data items are not loaded unless all of the data items are present in the file
       for the data set.
    The steps to create partial data sets are detailed in the e-terracomm User’s Guide –
    Real-Time Operation. Note that the flag is only relevant for SCADA data sets.
• Ack: Set to Yes if local acknowledgement is requested.
• Critical: Set to Yes if end-to-end acknowledgement is requested.
    Local and end-to-end acknowledgment cannot both be requested. Non-SCADA data
    sets do not support any kind of acknowledgment.


7.3.9.1.4 Protocol-Specific Modeling
 ICCPLINK                 Supports both local and end-to-end acknowledgment for SCADA data sets.
 ISDLINK                  Does not support any kind of acknowledgment.
 HABCLINK                 Does not support local acknowledgment.
 FILELINK                 Does not support any kind of acknowledgment.
 ELCOLINK                 Does not support any kind of acknowledgment.

• ELCOM priority class: For ELCOLINK, the priority class is a number between 0 and 15.
  The number is used as an index in a table that contains, for each index, the period (in
  seconds) to be used for the data set. Default values are hard-coded. They can be


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                   452                              e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                         e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    overridden by the values found in a configuration file (for details about the configuration
    file, see the e-terracomm Software Installation and Maintenance Guide).
• HABConnect request type: For HABCLINK input data sets only, specifies whether data is
  requested individually, as a range, or all the records.
     – Individual: Signals HABCLINK to fetch each data item individually (behavior in
       e-terracomm prior to version 2.3). This request type is suited for a data set
       containing unrelated data in the target database (i.e., referencing a different
       FIELD_RECORD).
     – All: Signals HABCLINK to fetch all instances of the desired FIELD_RECORD in the
       target database, then to match the returned component keys with the data items
       actually listed in the dataset. Every data item in the data set must specify the same
       FIELD_RECORD. Data items do not have to be listed in the same order in the data set
       as in the target e-terrahabitat database, but HABCLINK processes the report from
       SAMPLER more quickly if they are. The transmission style of the data set must be All.
     – Range: Signals HABCLINK to issue a single request for all of the FIELD_RECORD
       instances between the first data item in the dataset and the last data item in the
       dataset. HABCLINK matches the returned component keys with the data items
       actually listed in the dataset. Every data item in the data set must specify the same
       FIELD_RECORD. Data items do not have to be listed in the same order in the data set
       as in the target e-terrahabitat database, but HABCLINK processes the report from
       SAMPLER more quickly if they are. The transmission style of the data set must be All.


7.3.9.2 Contents
The CommDataSetDataItem records are used to define the data items or limit sets that
belong to data sets. These records are used to describe the contents of SCADA (Analogs,
Status, and Limit Sets), Control Message, Message Object, and Account Request data sets.
One record per data item or limit set is inserted as a child of the CommDataSet. Only SCADA
data sets can contain more than one data item or limit set.
Simply insert a CommDataSetDataItem record and fill the association with the
CommDataSet parent record. Then fill either the data item or the limit set association.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page              453                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.3.9.3 Other Considerations

7.3.9.3.1 Protocol-Specific Modeling
 ICCPLINK           Number of CommDataSetDataItem records per data set is limited by the maximum MMS
                    PDU size.
                    During handshaking, ICCPLINK exchanges with other remote(s) the list of data items in
                    the data sets. The list contains the data item names and, for each data item in Domain
                    scope, the name of the domain. Depending on the size of the names, the absolute limit
                    can be divided almost by a factor of 2. For example, with names of 20 characters and
                    domain names of 8 characters, the limit falls to approximately 800, for a PDU size of
                    32 K, the maximum supported by ICCPLINK.
                    When possible, it is better to have:
                     • Short data item names
                     • Maximum number of data items in VMD scope (in this case, only the data item name
                        is exchanged, not the domain name)
                    In any case, GE recommends not having data sets with more than 800 data items.
                    The validation program gives an estimate of the PDU size for each data set. When
                    exchanging limit sets:
                     • It is recommended to have them in separate data sets triggered by exception
                       because the limit value does not change very often.
                     • When requesting both high and low limits, non–GE remotes requesting limits must
                       request them in the order high then low without any other data item in between.
 ISDLINK            Does not allow duplicate entries (i.e., the same data item modeled more than once) in
                    the same or different data sets. An error is logged when validating the database if
                    duplicate entries are found in ISDLINK data sets (only for input data sets because output
                    data sets contents are created at run time).
 ELCOLINK           The maximum number of CommDataSetDataItem records per data set is 255.


7.3.10 Priority Pools
Priority Pool processing is meant to improve the initialization of ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD
connections when e-terracomm starts up or fails over. Initializing the connections includes
establishing the TCP/IP connections as well as the protocol handshakes required to get
data flowing between the EMS and remote systems.
On very large systems, it can take minutes before the initialization of the ICCP, ELCOM, and
ISD connections is complete. Often, the connections remain unstable for a long period of
time, impairing the reception of data from remote systems. Staggering the connections that
currently exist does not work well, because it relies on the assumptions that all data has the
same importance and that it takes the same amount of time to complete the handshake for
each remote; these assumptions are not true.
Priority Pool processing is optional. When it is used, the remotes need to be grouped in
“Priority Pools”. Each Priority Pool has a list of remotes. The number of remotes per pool is
not limited and may contain ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD remotes that are treated in parallel.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                     454                                e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                             e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

The number of Priority Pools is not limited. The Priority Pools constitute a list; the first pool in
the list has the highest priority. When Priority Pool processing is enabled, all the ICCP,
ELCOM, and ISD remotes must be referenced in the pools. Remotes for other link
applications must not be modeled in a pool.
At startup or upon e-terracomm failover, the list of Priority Pools is scanned from the first
element (highest priority) to the last (lowest priority). For each Priority Pool, the remotes in
the pool are enabled in sequence. When all pools have been scanned, Priority Pool
processing is done and is only activated again at the next startup or failover.
Each pool has a modeled time for determining when it is the next pool’s turn. For the first
pool, the time countdown starts when ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD applications are ready (on a
dual system, this is when they receive the enabled role). Only the existing applications are
checked. Not all systems use the three link applications.
It is possible to model what happens when a pool’s time elapses:
• Non-connected remotes, or remotes going up and down, are disabled and re-enabled
  when all pools are finished.
• Remotes of previous pools are left enabled independently of not being connected or
  going up and down. This is the default option.
Priority Pool processing works best for master remotes (ICCP or ELCOM); ISD remotes that
are both master and slave work well. Connection requests received for slave remotes that
have not yet been enabled by Priority Pool processing are rejected until the pool the
remotes belong to is active.
The CommPriorityPool properties are detailed below.
• Name: User-friendly identification, otherwise not used.
• Max Time: This is the time the pool is active (i.e., waiting for the remotes in that pool to
  make their connection/handshake). If this is not the last pool, the remotes in the next
  pool(s) are not enabled until the pool they belong to is activated. When the configured
  time elapses, the next pool is activated. If not all remotes of the current pool have
  finished their connection/handshake, they are either disabled until all pools are finished,
  or they continue trying to make their connection/handshake, depending on the global
  parameter “Failed Remotes Are Temporarily NISed”.
The CommPriorityPoolRemote properties are detailed below. One record is modeled for
each remote in the pool.
• Remote: This is the associated remote that belongs to the pool.
• Number of output data sets: This is the number of output data sets for that remote.
  This field is optional; it is meant to help fine-tune the timing of the pools.
    At run time, the number of active input and output data sets are displayed as they are
    being activated. The display shows the <number of active data sets> / <number of
    modeled data sets>. It is easy to see whether the maximum time for the pool is too long
    (all the expected data sets are active before the maximum time for the pool elapses) or


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                455                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                     e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

    too short (many data sets are not active when the maximum time elapses). Based on
    that information, the maximum time can be adjusted.


7.3.11 Cfg Site (SITE)
This record is used to define the different sites known by Configuration Manager. Note that
site here is in the context of Configuration Manager, not ISD.
Initial CfgSite state for first/second site: This field configures how e-terracomm will
consider the site’s state before any notification from CfgSite.


7.3.12 ISD Site (RSSITE)
This record is used to define the name of the ISD sites for each Configuration Manager’s
site.


7.4 Quality Mapping
This section shows mapping of the quality flags between ICCP and other protocols.


7.4.1 ISD V1.0 thru V3.0
ISD protocol carries only a few bits among the quality bits handled by SCADA or ICCP.
• SCADA / ISD status/source bits:
     – SUSPECT: Set if one or more of OLD, BAD, OVER, or NIS is set.
     – REPLACED: Set if either MANREP, GENREP, or ESTREP is set.
     – CMD: For Status Point only, set if the value is a result of a control command (not
       used in ISD versions 1.0 and 1.1).
     – TFAIL: Set if telemetry failed (used in version 1.1 only).
• ICCP status/source bits:
     – GOOD: Value is valid.
     – HELD: Previous data value has been held over (local interpretation).
     – SUSPECT: Value is questionable.
     – BAD: Value is not valid.
     – TELEMETERED: Value was received from a telemetered site.
     – CALCULATED: Value was calculated based on other data values.
     – MANUAL: Value was entered manually.
     – ESTIMATED: Value was estimated.
Proprietary – See Copyright Page               456                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

       – NORMAL: Value is the one configured as normal.
       – ABNORMAL: Value is the one configured as abnormal.
       – TSOK: Timestamp reflects when value was last updated.
       – TSBAD: Timestamp does not reflect when value was last updated.
