7.4.2 ISD 4.0 and Later
ISD 4.0 introduced improvements for transferring data attributes (quality, source).
ISD version 5.0 added BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE, giving information about tags.
• Value can have the following flags set (status only):
     – MDIS: If set, multiple changes occurred between the reporting of this value and the
       previous value reported.
     – ABNRM: If set, this value represents an abnormal state.
     – BLKOPEN: If set, a tag preventing open operations exists (V5.0).
     – BLKCLOSE: If set, a tag preventing close operation exists (V5.0).
         BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE can be sent/received via ICCP only when Supplemental
         status data objects are supported.
• Source can be one of the following:
     – TELEM: If set, this data is received via telemetry.
     – CALC: If set, this data value has been calculated based on other data values.
     – MANL: If set, either this data is normally entered manually, or the value has been
       manually replaced. If the value has been manually replaced, the REPL flag is also set.
     – ESTIM: If set, either this data is normally provided from the State Estimator, or the
       value has been provided as a replacement value from the State Estimator. If the
       value has been provided as a replacement value, the REPL flag is also set.
• Quality:
     – SUSP: If set, this data quality is SUSPECT. This quality can result if the data is out of
       scan on the host computer or if suspect data is provided from an outside source.
     – REPL: If set, this data quality is REPLACED. This quality is reported if the value is an
       operator-overridden value.
     – CMD: If set, this data quality is COMMANDED. This quality occurs if the state was
       altered as the result of a supervisory control request (Status only).
     – INTG: If set, it indicates that this value and quality were sent in response to an
       integrity scan.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                 458                           e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

       – TFAIL: If set, this data quality is Telemetry Failed.
       – BAD: If set, this data quality is Bad. This quality can result if the data is in an illegal
         state or if errors were encountered in producing the engineering value.
       – NIS: If set, this data point has been removed from service.
       – OVER (analogs only): If set, this data point is beyond a reasonable range on the
         source system.
       – LONG (counts only): If set, the value associated with this data point is for a time
         range that may be longer than normal, and thus the value may be larger than an
         average reading (for example, a value is returned for an accumulator that is read
         hourly, but the value is for a time range of three hours because of missed readings
         due to telemetry failure or equipment unavailability).
       – BLKSETP: If set, setpoint operations are not allowed (V5.0). This flag is stored in the
         database but is not used (ICCP does not have a way to pass it).


7.4.2.1 ISD to ICCP Mapping
Not all ISD quality flags are used in the mapping to ICCP quality because ICCP has many
fewer flags, and some ISD flags are not even related to quality. The following flags are not
mapped: TFAIL, OVER, LONG, BLKSETP, INTG, and CMD.
The ISD ABNRM flag is directly mapped to the ICCP ABNORMAL flag.
The ISD MDIS flag is processed when MCD processing is configured.
The ISD flags BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE are mapped to ICCP only when the data item is of
type supplemental (type STATUSEX with or without quality and timestamp).

7.4.2.2 ICCP to ISD Mapping
ICCP has the same source flags but many fewer quality flags. Mapping to ISD is almost
one-to-one, except for the ICCP quality HELD, which is translated to GOOD, plus the ISD NIS
flag set when the source is telemetered (unless modified by quality semantics conversion
modeling).
If the database validity of a data item is INVALID, quality mapping is not applied; the ISD
quality is set to BAD. The source mapping is based on the mapping table (default or
modified by quality semantics conversion modeling).
If the database validity of a data item is GARBAGE, the data is not sent at all to the EMS, as
specified by the ISD protocol.

7.4.3 ELCOM-90
ELCOM-90 has the following quality/source flags:
• Origin
     – Measured: A point is “measured” when its value is acquired by one of several
       possible measuring methods (e.g., scanning).
     – Manual: The value of a point is “manually entered” when its current value is provided
       by input from an operator or simulator.
     – Estimated: A point is “estimated” when its value is calculated by a State Estimator
       program.
     – Computed: A point is “computed” when its value is the result of a calculation using
       other data (scanned, computed, and/or estimated) as input variables.
     – Held: A point whose value is measured is “held” when the most recent update was
       unsuccessful and an old value is held in the database.
• Validity
     – OK/Not OK: A point whose value is measured is “OK” when its value was acquired by
       the previous update — i.e., the point is not off-scan, and communications with the
       substation are successful.
        A manually entered value is always “OK”.
        A point whose value is estimated by a State Estimator is “OK” when the State
        Estimator is running at its normal assigned frequency.
        A point whose value is computed is “OK” when all the independent data points from
        which it is computed are “OK”.
        A point whose value is held is always “Not OK”.

                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.5 MCD Processing
The ISD protocol allows passing Multiple Changes Detection information (MDIS flag in status
message), but the ICCP protocol does not allow a direct mapping of this flag. Instead, ICCP
can carry the MCD information in two ways:
• Use of Data_StateExtended (with a “change of value counter” – COV)
• Use of Data_Discrete (a 32-bit integer)
The semantics of both are not strictly defined in the ICCP specification. Does the counter
reflect the number of changes since the last update or since data exchange began? What
are the possible values for a Data_Discrete when multiple changes are detected?
The MCD processing in e-terracomm is done in ISDLINK and is configurable on a
per-remote basis:
• No MCD processing
• Delta count
• Running count
• Data discrete


7.5.1 Modeling
To enable processing of MCD information for a given data item, it must be configured as
follows:
• Delta or Running Count
     – The CommDataItem should have the Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value
       Counter flags set to Yes.
     – The CommDataItemPermission for the ISDLINK remote should have the network
       type set to 26 (Status with Quality).
     – The CommDataItemPermission for the ICCPLINK remote should have the network
       type set to 30 (Status with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value Counter).
• Data Discrete
     – The CommDataItem should have only the Quality flag set to Yes.
     – The CommDataItemPermission for the ISDLINK remote should have the network
       type set to 26 (Status with Quality).
     – The CommDataItemPermission for the ICCPLINK remote should have the network
       type set to 8 (INT32 with Quality).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            464                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.5.2 Processing

7.5.2.1 Sending MCD Information
ISDLINK receives the MCD information from the EMS local host, processes it, and passes it
along with the data item value and quality to OAGSERVE to be stored in the e-terracomm
database. The data item is then ready to be sent by ICCPLINK to a remote site.
The processing done by ISDLINK is as follows:
• Delta or Running Count
     – ISDLINK determines the COV value based on two kinds of information:
         ∗ Whether the value changed since last received
         ∗ Whether the MCD flag in the received message is set or reset
         The actual number of changes is not known. What is important is that the remote
         sites must be able to determine whether the MCD flag was set or not with the COV
         and point values. The parity of the COV value and whether it is greater than 1 are
         what matters.
The tables below show how the COV value is set.


Delta Count
 Value                MCD Received          COV

 Changed              Set                   3

 Changed              Not set               1

 Not Changed          Set                   2

 Not Changed          Not set               0


Running Count
 Value                MCD Received          COV

 Changed              Set                   Previous value +3

 Changed              Not set               Previous value +1

 Not Changed          Set                   Previous value +2

 Not Changed          Not set               Previous value


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                465                         e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.5.2.1.1 Data Discrete
If the MCD flag is set in the message received from SCADA, ICCPLINK adds a constant to the
status value. If the MCD flag is not set, the value is not changed.
The constant value is 4, which gives a total of 8 possible values for the status. For example:
 0   Between, no MCD                    4   Between MCD sets (*)
 1   Open, no MCD                       5   Open, MCD set
 2   Closed, no MCD                     6   Closed, MCD set
 3   Invalid, no MCD                    7   Invalid, MCD set (*)
 (*) These values are unlikely.

Note that Data Semantics translates only the two lower bits of the value so the MCD
information is maintained.


7.5.2.2 Receiving MCD Information
ICCPLINK receives the MCD information from the remote site. It passes that information
along with the data item value and quality to OAGSERVE to be stored in the e-terracomm
database. The data item is then ready to be sent by ISDLINK to the local EMS host.
Before sending data to EMS, ISDLINK processes MCD information, if any, as follows.


7.5.2.2.1 Delta or Running Count
ISDLINK determines whether the MCD flag was set based on two kinds of information:
• Whether the value changed since last received
• The COV value
The MCD flag in the message to SCADA is set or not depending on the two kinds of
information shown in the following table.
 Value                        COV *                                MCD
 Changed                      0                                    Not set**
 Changed                      1                                    Not set
 Changed                      Even                                 Not set**
 Changed                      Odd > 1                              Set
 Not Changed                  0                                    Not set
 Not Changed                  1                                    Not set**
 Not Changed                  Even                                 Set
 Not Changed                  Odd > 1                              Not set**


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                        466                               e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                               e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

 Value                          COV *                                    MCD
 (*) Running count: COV = COV value received – previous COV value; Delta count: COV = COV value
 received.
 (**) These cases are theoretically impossible. However, when receiving data for the first time, the
 previous value or previous COV are not known; therefore, any combination may happen.


7.5.2.2.2 Data Discrete
If the received value is greater than 3, as shown in the table below, this means that the
MCD information is set. ISDLINK sets the MCD flag in the message sent to SCADA.
 0   Between no MCD                     4    Between MCD set (*)
 1   Open, no MCD                       5    Open, MCD set
 2   Closed, no MCD                     6    Closed, MCD set
 3   Invalid, no MCD                    7    Invalid, MCD set (*)
 (*) These values are unlikely.

Note that Data Semantics translates only the two lower bits of the value so the MCD
information is maintained.


7.6 Filtering Bad Data
  WARNING: Do not use this option if you exchange data with your EMS using ISD protocol
  version 4.0 or later.

Because the ISD protocol versions 1.0 thru 3.0 have only one quality bit (Good/Suspect), the
mapping from the richer ICCP quality bits may not reflect the actual “quality” sent to the
EMS. Also, there is no ICCP “Garbage” quality bit. Due to these deficiencies, it is difficult for
e-terracomm to indicate to the EMS any degree of confidence on the value of any given
data. To make matters worse, e-terraplatform uses the value of data even when the quality
is suspect.
When a remote value is received via ICCPLINK, the worst quality is BAD, but that does not
mean that this is not actually garbage. The BAD quality is mapped to ISD Suspect, and the
EMS may be using garbage values (you notice that by seeing your power applications
producing bad results or even crashing).
A workaround is to instruct ISDLINK to not send data with BAD quality to the EMS. To do
this, set the “Send BAD data to EMS” option to No on the ISDLINK CommRemote record(s). It
is safe to set this flag when receiving data from an e-terracomm remote because the BAD
flag is only set when the DB quality is Garbage (i.e., the value must not be used). However,
other ICCP vendors may send BAD quality with a value that is not really garbage (it may be
the last known value and the power applications can use it without a problem).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page                           467                                   e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                                      e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

If you want to use BAD data coming from a non–GE remote site, and not use BAD data
coming from GE remote sites, you can configure different ISDLINK remotes (i.e., SCADA
sites), mapping them with the ICCPLINK remotes.


7.7 InterSite Data 4.0
This section lists the modifications made in the InterSite Data protocol with the introduction
of version 4.0, and how the modifications are supported in e-terracomm.
• Added new messages for adding and removing data points from the set of
  measurements passed between sites, without breaking and re-establishing the link or
  otherwise forcing a complete download.
• Added an integrity scan message to force the source site to send an integrity scan of a
  single measurement, or to send an integrity scan for all measurements mapped
  between the source and destination sites.
• Modified the function codes of the data messages to identify that the format of the data
  submessages has changed. The new format indicates the type of data passed in each
  submessage, and passes additional quality information.
• Added a new flag to indicate whether the new state of a status point is abnormal.
• Added new flags to indicate whether the analog, status, or accumulator data is
  telemetry failed, is a bad reading, or is marked Not In Service.
• Added data source flags, which are now also passed in the data messages, to indicate
  whether the current data is telemetered, calculated, manually entered, or estimated.
• Added new extended-data messages that can be returned from the source site. These
  include a time stamp identifying when the value was last modified. The source site
  implementation is responsible for determining the conditions under which the
  extended-data message is returned, instead of the normal data message.


7.7.1 Adding and Removing Data Points
e-terracomm supports the request from the EMS to add or remove points in the list of point
it sends (output data set) with the restriction that, when adding points, these points must
already exist in the e-terracomm database (i.e., the e-terracomm database should be a
step ahead of the EMS database).


7.7.1.1 Adding Data Points
After checking that the new requested data points exist and have the correct permission
(Read), e-terracomm adds these points (or a subset if some do not exist) to the output data
set. They are always added at the end. After adding the data points, an integrity scan is sent
so the EMS receives the current value of the new points.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             468                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.7.1.2 Removing Data Points
The requested data points are not actually removed from the output data set. Instead, they
are marked as “deleted” and ISDLINK stops sending them to the EMS. Each deleted entry in
the output data set as well as the data set itself is displayed in a different color (for details,
see the e-terracomm User’s Guide – Real-Time Operation).
The data points are actually removed from the output data set at the next full download.


7.7.2 Integrity Scan Message
e-terracomm responds to the EMS request (either for an individual data point or the full set),
but does not request integrity scans of the EMS. Note that the integrity scan mechanism
existing in the previous versions of the protocol continues — i.e., an integrity scan is
automatically performed after a full download or after failed communications are
re-established.


7.7.3 New Flags
The mapping between the new flags and the e-terracomm quality flags is described in
section 7.4 Quality Mapping.


7.7.4 Extended Data Messages

7.7.4.1 Input
When an extended data message is received from the EMS, the timestamp is sent to
OAGSERVE to be stored in the database. It is discarded if the data item is not modeled with
the timestamp attribute set (DB type).
If the data item is modeled with the attribute timestamp set (DB type) but EMS does not
send an extended message, ISDLINK timestamps the data at the time it is received from the
EMS (the millisecond part is always set to 0 in this case).


7.7.4.2 Output
If a data item is modeled with the timestamp attribute set (DB type), ISDLINK sends an
extended message; otherwise, it sends a normal message.


7.8 InterSite Control 1.0
This section lists the modifications made in the InterSite Control protocol with the
introduction of version 1.0, and how the modifications are supported in e-terracomm.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               469                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                    e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Passed version information in each of the four different types of supervisory control
  messages.
• Added four new messages for sending a control response to each type of supervisory
  control request. Added a placeholder to each of the supervisory control messages. The
  response message is formatted the same as the originating message, except that the
  placeholder field is filled in with an error code identifying the success or failure of the
  control, and an indication of the problem if the control was not successful.


7.8.1 Version Information
When the default ISD protocol version modeled on an ISD remote is set to 4.0, ISDLINK
automatically tries to use InterSite Control 1.0, sending a “Hello” message to Control on the
EMS. If the EMS does not respond within 5 seconds, ISDLINK assumes that InterSite
Control 1.0 is not supported by the EMS and it falls back to version 0.0.
“Hello” messages that are received from the EMS indicating version 1.0 are always
responded to with a success status.


7.8.2 Control Response
In e-terracomm, controls are sent to/received from a remote site using two link
applications: ISDLINK between the EMS and e-terracomm, and ICCPLINK between
e-terracomm and a remote site.
In the ICCP protocol, there is no synchronous control response except when the controlled
device does not exist, or when other errors such as communication problems are detected
preventing the remote EMS from initiating the control. Once the control has reached the
remote EMS, the result of the control is through asynchronous events (ICCP Block 7),
indicating success or failure.
ICCPLINK supports Block 7 and is able to forward to ISDLINK control responses that can
then be sent to the EMS. However, not all ICCP vendors support Block 7 (older versions of
e-terracomm do not support Block 7 either). Therefore, in this case, it is not possible to send
the control responses to the EMS.
When an EMS device is controlled from a remote site, ISDLINK forwards the control
responses to ICCPLINK, which in turn triggers the success or failure events if the remote site
supports Block 7 and has requested to receive such events.


7.9 ICCP 2000-08 vs ICCP 1996-08
There are not a lot of changes introduced in ICCP 2000–08. Of those changes, only a subset
are implemented in e-terracomm 2.3.1.
• New Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data types
• New way of reporting data changes

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             470                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• Modified/new Block 8 objects

  Note: The ICCP specification has no provision for interoperability between different
  versions — i.e., once a new version is published, the previous one no longer exists. This is
  not how the “real world” works. It is not possible for a utility with 30 ICCP partners to
  switch simultaneously to a new version of ICCP with its 30 partners. e-terracomm 2.3.1
  supports both versions of ICCP. The version to use must be modeled on a per-remote
  basis.


7.9.1 New SCADA Data Types
e-terracomm 2.3.1 supports the new SCADA data types introduced in ICCP 2000–08 as well
as the Supplemental Objects data types defined in IEC 60870-6-802 Annex B.
The three new SCADA data types are:
• INT32 with Quality and Extended Timestamp
• REAL32 with Quality and Extended Timestamp
• STATE with Quality and Extended Timestamp
While the Timestamp has a resolution of one second, the Extended Timestamp has a
resolution of one millisecond. The Extended Timestamp is made of a 32-bit integer
representing a time in seconds (GMT time) and a 16-bit integer representing the
milliseconds.
The Supplemental Objects data types allow passing more information for status points. The
following information can be passed:
• Tag value (0 = No Tag, 1 = Open and Close inhibit, 2 = Close only inhibit)
• Expected State (2 bits as for the current state)
The Supplemental Objects data types are:
• State Supplemental (no attributes)
• State Supplemental with Quality
• State Supplemental with Quality and Timestamp
• State Supplemental with Quality and Extended Timestamp
• State Supplemental with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value Counter
In e-terracomm 2.3.1, the Supplemental Objects data types can be modeled. However, the
Tag value and Expected State are just displayed; there is no processing of these fields. A
future version of the ISD protocol will provide a way of sending them to and receiving them
from the EMS.
The new data types are modeled and displayed as indicated in the following table.

7.9.2 New Way of Reporting Data Changes
With ICCP version 1996–08, only the last value is reported with any kind of data set trigger
(PER/EXC/REQ) or style (ALL/RBE).
ICCP version 2000–08 introduces the ability to report all changes that have occurred during
a modeled buffering time — i.e., multiple instances of a given data item can be reported in a
single report.
ISDLINK has always been able to do this for status (the buffering time is actually the polling
interval of the EMS). However, to work properly, it was necessary to modify OAGSERVE to
not do the buffering time monitoring because changed values were replacing previous ones
in the database during the buffering time. The buffering time needs to be done by the link
application to allow maintaining a buffer with all the changes.
The change in OAGSERVE had already been done when ELCOLINK was implemented
(ELCOM-90 allows reporting all changes), and a new trigger type (UDT) was introduced to
instruct OAGSERVE to pass received changes from the source of the data (input data set)
immediately to the destination(s) of the data (output data set(s)).
The same new trigger is now allowed for ICCPLINK and ISDLINK data sets (for ISDLINK, only
for output data sets). It is not necessary for input data sets because ISDLINK already reports
changes for a given data item separately.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page               472                          e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

  Note: The name of the trigger, “UDT”, comes from ELCOM-90 and stands for “Unsolicited
  Data Transfer”.

To model such data reports from a remote ICCP up to the EMS, the ICCPLINK input data set
must have Trigger=UDT, Style=RBE, and a non-zero exception buffering time (a zero
exception buffering time generates a report for every single change). The ISDLINK output
data set has the same trigger and style (UDT, RBE). The exception buffering time does not
matter (the time changes are buffered before they are sent to the EMS depending on the
EMS polling interval).
To model such data reports from the EMS to an ICCP remote, the ISDLINK input data set is
(as usual) Trigger=PER, Style=RBE.
The ICCPLINK output data set is created and enabled by the remote site. The remote needs
to enable the data set with the “AllChangesReported” flag set to True in the TransferSet.
For e-terracomm remotes, the input data set must be modeled with Trigger=UDT and
Style=RBE. Setting the trigger to UDT instructs ICCPLINK to set the “AllChangesReported”
flag to True in the TransferSet used to remotely enable the data set.


7.9.3 Modified and New Block 8 Objects
The Transfer Account object has been modified to include the field TransactionCode, and
two new objects have been added: General Data Report and General Data Response.
As of e-terracomm 2.3.1, the implementation of these changes has been deemed
unnecessary due to the lack of procurement for Block 8 support.
ICCP Block 8 is not supported with ICCP version 2000–08 (error in validation if configured),
but it continues to be supported with ICCP version 1996–08.


7.10 Special Modeling
This section describes the specific modeling of Account and Information Messages objects
(ICCP Blocks 8 and 4), and Control messages.
• Account objects are supported by ICCPLINK and ISDLINK.
• Information messages are supported by ICCPLINK and ISDLINK.
• Control messages are supported by ICCPLINK, ELCOLINK, and ISDLINK.


7.10.1 Modeling Information Messages
Figure 116 describes the modeling of information messages exchanged, in both directions,
between two remotes: KENT and AUBURN. Only the configuration at KENT is detailed. In the
figure below, AUBURN is shown as GE’s e-terracomm.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             473                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Figure 116. Information Messages

The KENT site configuration has a scheduling application, a messaging application, and
e-terracomm. The messaging application exchanges messages, using ICCP, with a remote
site located at AUBURN. KENT receives one message (Information Reference = 6755) from
AUBURN, and also sends a message (Information Reference = 6754) to AUBURN.
1. CommDataItem: For each message, define a CommDataItem record with type
   Information Message, and with Size set to the maximum number of bytes that might
   ever be used by the Information Message plus 14 (ICCP Information Message header).
   The other required data item fields must also be filled in. The data item name (either the
   identification or the optional name depending on the data item configuration) must be a
   number; this number is the Information Reference that identifies the Information
   Message.
2. Input CommDataSet: For each Information Message, create an Input data set as a child
   of the Source remote. The trigger must be On Request, and the transmission style must
   be All.
3. Input CommDataSetDataItem: Insert a CommDataSetDataItem record for each input
   data set and associate it with the data item created in step 1.
4. Output CommDataSet: For each Information Message, insert an Output data set as a
   child of the destination remote. The trigger must be On Receipt, and the transmission
   style must be All.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            474                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

5. Output CommDataSetDataItem: Insert a CommDataSetDataItem record for each
   output data set and associate it with the same data item created in step 1.
6. On the CommDataSets records, fill in the Twin field for both Input and Output data sets
   so they reference each other.
7. Fill in the rest of the Input and Output data sets as necessary.


7.10.2 Modeling Control Messages
Figure 117 describes the modeling of controls exchanged, in both directions, between two
remotes: KENT and AUBURN, and in one direction between RENTON and KENT. Only the
configuration at KENT is detailed.


Figure 117. Control Configuration

Among other data, KENT’s EMS sends SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 to AUBURN
and RENTON, and receives SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 from AUBURN.
Devices are associated with the data so they can be remotely controlled. KENT controls
SCADA2_ANALOG1 (Setpoint) and SCADA2_STATUS2 (Open/Close) while AUBURN and
RENTON can control SCADA1_ANALOG1 (Setpoint) and SCADA1_STATUS1 (Open/Close).


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             475                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

Devices associated with SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 are Select Before
Operate (SBO).
Devices associated with SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 are Direct Operate (DO).
1. CommDataItems: Control commands require two-way communication between the
   controlling remote and the remote source of the device (i.e., the source of the data item
   with which the device is associated). The data items are used to carry control requests
   and responses. Each data item can carry a request or a response, meaning that if each
   remote sends control to the other one, the same data items can be used both ways.
    For the KENT site to be able to control SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 at
    AUBURN, you need two data items: one with source KENT and the other with source
    AUBURN. These two data items also allow the AUBURN site to control
    SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 at KENT. You do not need other data items.
    For the RENTON site to also be able to control SCADA1_ANALOG1 and
    SCADA1_STATUS1, you need two more data items: one with source RENTON and the
    other with source KENT. Set Write permission for the source remote and Read
    permission for the non-source remote.
2. Input CommDataSets: Under each remote that sends or receives control, insert an
   Input data set for the other remote with which it exchanges control messages. In our
   configuration:
     – Remote SCADA: Two Input data sets, one for AUBURN and one for RENTON.
     – Remote AUBURN: One Input data set for SCADA.
     – Remote RENTON: One Input data set for SCADA.
    The trigger must be On Request, and the transmission style must be All.
3. Input CommDataSetDataItems: For each Input data set, insert a
   CommDataSetDataItem record; associate it with the data item created in step 1. The
   data item is the one with source = parent remote of the Input data set (e.g., for the
   SCADA_CTRL_IN data set, the ENTRY must reference the CTRL1 data item because its
   source is the SCADA remote, parent of the data set). This is also the data item with Write
   permission for the data set’s parent remote.
4. Output CommDataSets: Repeat step 2, this time inserting an Output data set. The
   trigger type must be On Receipt, and the transmission style must be All.
5. Output CommDataSetDataItems: For each Output data set, insert a
   CommDataSetDataItem record. Associate it with the data item created in step 1. The
   data item is the one with Read permission for the Output data set’s parent remote.
6. On the CommDataSet records, fill in the Twin field for both Input and Output data sets
   so they reference each other.
7. Fill in the rest of the Input and Output data sets as necessary.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page             476                             e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                  e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

7.10.2.1 ELCOLINK Dynamic Control Data Sets
When required, it is possible for ELCOLINK acting as Initiator to dynamically create and
define ELCOM groups for controls on remote partners.
The following modeling is an example, where DataSet 101 must be an Input data set
triggered On Request with transmission style All:
DataSet 1 >> Group 1
  pointer to DataItem P1      point 1
      Device C1 control 1 attached (ELCOM: Grp: 101 Pnt: 1)
  pointer to DataItem P2
      Device C2 control 2 attached (ELCOM: Grp: 101 Pnt: 2)

DataSet 2 >> Group 2
  pointer to DataItem P3
      Device C3 control 3 attached (ELCOM: Grp: 101 Pnt: 3)

etc...

DataSet 101 >> Group 101 for controls
  pointer to DataItem P1      point 1
      Device C1 control 1 attached
  pointer to DataItem P2
      Device C2 control 2 attached
  pointer to DataItem P3
      Device C3 control 3 attached
Modeling the same data twice under the same remote in two different data sets generates
validation warnings, but this is not a problem.


7.10.3 Component Status Data Items
There are two types of component data items:
• Topology component data items
• Data set component data items


7.10.3.1 Topology Component Data Items
These data items are created automatically by the database validation program.
In this context, a “component” is a topology component: CommLinkApplication,
CommRemote, CommLink, or CommPath. For each component, the validation program
creates a CommDataItem. At run time, OAGSERVE deposits a coded number representing
the current status of the component. The identification of a Component Status data item is
formed by appending the component’s ID to a conventional prefix.


Proprietary – See Copyright Page            477                            e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

 Component              Prefix
 LNKAPP                 ASTS_
 REMOTE                 RSTS_
 LINK                   LSTS_
 PATH                   PSTS_
The remote source of such data items is set to OAGSERVE (“pseudo remote”).
If an ISDLINK remote exists in the database, the validation program creates an ISD optional
name:
    <SUBSTN> <DEVTYP> <DEVICE> <POINT>
where:
• SUBSTN = ID of the link application (under which the component is)
• DEVTYP = “OAG”
• DEVICE = ID of the component
    The ID is truncated to the first 14 characters, so be aware that it is possible that the
    truncation will create duplicate device names (the database validation issues a warning
    when truncation happens).
• POINT = Prefix depending on the component type (as shown above, but without the
  underscore)
No data sets are automatically defined to contain Component Status data items. The user
can reference them like any other SCADA data item when defining a data set.
If you want to exchange Component Status data items using ISDLINK, the network type for
ISDLINK remotes must be set to “STATUS-Q-T”. This is actually done by the validation
program.
The Component Status data items can have the following values:
 State                         Value
 Up                            2 = ICCP_STATUS_CLOSED
 Down                          1 = ICCP_STATUS_TRIPPED
 Out of Service                8 = When sent to the EMS via ISD, 0 is passed, which is equivalent
                               to ICCP_STATUS_BETWEEN.
 Returned to Service           1 = Down = ICCP-STATUS_TRIPPED
 (*)
 (*) This state is specified only to clearly indicate that when the component is put back into service, there are
 two state transitions: “Out of Service” to “Down” and “Down” to “Up”.

If you change the ID of one or more components between runs of the validation program,
new data items are created with the new ID, and the data items with the previous ID are

Proprietary – See Copyright Page                       478                                e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                               e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

automatically deleted (a warning is logged for every Status data item that has been
deleted). If Status data items are exchanged in data sets, and you change the ID of a
component, remember to also change the ID in the data set (Data Set Contents display).
You can change the automatically generated ISD optional name of a component data item.


7.10.3.2 Data Set Component Data Items
The data set component data items are not automatically created. They need to be
modeled.
For each Input data set you want to report the state to the EMS, you need to model a data
item as any other SCADA data item, and reference this data item in the data set (field Data
Item for Data Set state). The specific settings for the data item are as follows:
• Name: No restrictions
• Database type: Integer 32-bit with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value counter
• ISDLINK optional name: As needed for the EMS modeling
• Source: Must be OAGSERVE
• Permissions: Read for the ISDLINK remote on which the data item is sent to the EMS
• Network type: Status with Quality and Timestamp for the ISDLINK remote on which the
  data item is sent to the EMS
The Data Set Component data items can have the following values:
 State                                                 Value
 Active (enabled and received as expected)             2 = ICCP_STATUS_CLOSED
 Not Active (out of service, not yet remotely          1 = ICCP_STATUS_TRIPPED
 enabled)
 Late (enabled but not being received as expected)     0 = ICCP-STATUS_BETWEEN


7.11 e-terracomm Model Validation Rules
Many of the e-terracomm model validation rules are implemented in the attribute and
association definitions of the metadata entity (such as data range, string length, and
association cardinality). Those model rules are enforced during data entry. In addition to
those data entry rules, the following rules are defined in the validation modules that are
only triggered as part of full validation and e-terracomm model validation.


7.11.1 Comm Auxiliary Validation Module
The following validation is performed using SQL directly in the database. The rules being
validated are not as visible as those that are defined in the Validation Rules modeling.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page                479                         e-terracomm Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

• PriorityPoolWithSameRemote: Error if the same remote has been found multiple times in
  the Priority Pool modeling (either in the same pool or a different pool, or both).
• NonReferencedRemote: Error if not all ISD, ELCOM, and ICCP remotes are referenced in
  priority pools.
• CommSiteWithNoIsd: Error if a CommCfgSite does not have at least one CommIsdSite
  pair.
• CommRemoteNoProtocol: Error if a remote does not specify which protocol is used.
• CommRemoteWithNoPath: Error if a CommRemote does not have at least one
  CommPath.
• CommLinkAppWithSameType: Error if more than one LNKAPP record is found with the
  same linkappType.
• CommDupName: Error if duplicated names are found within LNKAPP and/or global

• CommDupLimSetNameOnISD: Error if duplicate ICCPName is found when any
  ISD_LNKAPP is True and SDINAME_ITEMS is False.

  entries.

8.3 TAGGING Model

8.3.1 TAGGING Configuration
This contains the global parameters for the TAGGING application. Follow the description for
each field for more details:
• USE IMS: e-terraplatform 3.0 uses the Identifier Mapping Service to provide the
  application the long names and MRIDs for the records. On a development system where
  an IMS may not be available, TAGGING could generate fake MRIDs for the tagged object.
  On production systems it is highly recommended to set this to Yes. Note that tags and
  tagged objects created on a system not using IMS are not compatible with a system
  that is using IMS, due to MRID incompatibility.
• USE DATA Service: This option is currently disabled, as data service is not available in
  e-terraplatform 3.0.
• IMS Resynchronization Interval: When the MRID of a tagged object cannot be verified
  because IMS is not available, this setting provides the interval in seconds between each
  attempt to verify the MRID.
• Number of Comment Lines: When a comment is changed (when creating, deleting, or
  modifying a tag), TAGGING logs the comment’s content. The log might become
  overloaded when operators enter long comments. TAGGING uses this setting to
  truncate the comments in the log (displayed with ellipses). Full content is still accessible
  in the tagging displays.
• Longname Prefix: When no long name is available, TAGGING creates its own long name
  based on the object’s composite key. This setting is used as the prefix for this created
  long name (e.g., Longname, LN ...).


8.3.2 TAGGING Expiration
Expiration time is used to automatically remove a tag after a specified duration. Default
expiration can be defined on the tag types, but this list is mainly used in the tag popup.


8.3.3 TAGGING Communication
This models an ISTSITE site. IST is the intersite Tagging protocol used to exchange tag
information between two tagging applications.
TAGGING supports only two sites: the local site and the remote one.
• Is the Site Independent?: If Yes, this setting indicates that the peer site that TAGGING is
  connected with can be simultaneously active. If No, then only one site is active at a time.
  For example, this can be used between an EMS and a DTS, or between TAGGING running
  on a production system and another one used as display backup.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page             487                                TAGGING Modeling
                                                                 e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide


<!-- salto de página -->

8.3.4 TAGGING GrpTypes
This models the type of group supported by the TAGGING application.


8.3.5 TAGGING TagTypes
This models the tag types of the application.
Use the TAGGING/behavior grouping to set the restriction(s) on the record. These
restrictions are not managed by TAGGING, but are sent to the TAGGING clients. The client
will interpret these attributes according to its processing. For example, Block close is used
only by applications that manage statuses and can detect if the status is opened or closed,
and that can issue controls. e-terrascada is one example.


8.3.6 TAGGING Datasources
The datasource tells TAGGING what source will be using TAGGING data and what this
source can handle.


8.3.6.1 Datasource
• Host1: This is used for datasources that TAGGING needs to know how to contact, such
  as e-terradistribution. For datasources that use NETIO on the same NNI as the TAGGING
  application, you do not need to provide this setting. Specify localhost in this case.


8.3.6.2 Tagable Record Type
Unlike SCADAMOM, where tagable record types were hardcoded as masks, TAGGING is free
to receive any record types for the given data source.
Note the following:
• TAGGING will not verify in the datasource schema that these record types exist.
• The default tagtype should be an applicable tagtype.


8.3.6.3 Applicable Tagtypes
This gives the list of all tagtypes that can be applied to the record type.
